Running statistics — Welford & EMA

Mean, variance, a z-score anomaly check and a smoothed level, each in O(1) memory.

import kotlin.math.abs
import kotlin.math.sqrt

/** Online mean and variance. Numerically stable, unlike a running sum of squares. */
class RunningStats {
    var count = 0L; private set                 // Long: an Int wraps after 2^31 samples
    var mean = 0.0; private set
    private var m2 = 0.0

    fun add(x: Double) {
        count++
        val delta = x - mean
        mean += delta / count
        m2 += delta * (x - mean)
    }

    val variance get() = if (count > 1) m2 / (count - 1) else 0.0
    fun isAnomaly(x: Double) = sqrt(variance).let { sd -> sd > 0 && abs(x - mean) / sd > 3 }
}

/** Exponential moving average: no window, no history. alpha = 2 / (period + 1). */
class Ema(private val alpha: Double) {
    var value: Double? = null; private set
    fun add(x: Double): Double = (value?.let { alpha * x + (1 - alpha) * it } ?: x).also { value = it }
}

fun main() {
    val stats = RunningStats()
    val ema = Ema(alpha = 0.5)
    val smoothed = listOf(100.0, 110.0, 90.0, 105.0, 95.0).map { stats.add(it); ema.add(it) }
    println("n=${stats.count} mean=${stats.mean} variance=${stats.variance}")
    println("ema=$smoothed")
    println("400 ms anomalous? ${stats.isAnomaly(400.0)}; 104 ms? ${stats.isAnomaly(104.0)}")
}
Result
n=5 mean=100.0 variance=62.5
ema=[100.0, 105.0, 97.5, 101.25, 98.125]
400 ms anomalous? true; 104 ms? false

Reservoir sampling

A uniform sample of k orders from a stream of unknown length, in O(k) memory — for audits and upload sampling.

import kotlin.random.Random

class Reservoir<T>(private val capacity: Int, private val random: Random = Random.Default) {
    private val items = ArrayList<T>(capacity)
    private var seen = 0L
    val sample: List<T> get() = items

    fun add(item: T) {
        seen++
        if (items.size < capacity) {
            items += item
        } else {
            val slot = random.nextLong(seen)        // keep with probability k / n
            if (slot < capacity) items[slot.toInt()] = item
        }
    }
}

fun main() {
    // Seeded only so the page is reproducible; production code keeps Random.Default.
    val random = Random(42)
    val audit = Reservoir<String>(capacity = 5, random = random)
    for (i in 1..10_000) audit.add("order-$i")
    println(audit.sample)

    // Uniformity check: 20 000 samples of 2 out of 4 — each item should survive ~50% of the time.
    val survived = IntArray(4)
    repeat(20_000) {
        val r = Reservoir<Int>(capacity = 2, random = random)
        (0..3).forEach(r::add)
        r.sample.forEach { survived[it]++ }
    }
    println(survived.map { it * 100 / 20_000 })
}

[49, 50, 50, 49]

Count-Min Sketch — approximate frequencies

Hits per endpoint for any number of endpoints in a fixed width × depth table, never undercounting.

/** MurmurHash3's finaliser: spreads every input bit across the output. */
fun mix(x: Int): Int {
    var h = x
    h = (h xor (h ushr 16)) * 0x85EBCA6B.toInt()
    h = (h xor (h ushr 13)) * 0xC2B2AE35.toInt()
    return h xor (h ushr 16)
}

/** width ≈ e / ε, depth ≈ ln(1 / δ). Memory is width × depth longs, whatever the key count. */
class CountMinSketch(private val width: Int, private val depth: Int) {
    private val table = Array(depth) { LongArray(width) }

    // String.hashCode is 32 bits and easy to collide on purpose ("Aa" and "BB" share every row):
    // for untrusted keys, hash the UTF-8 bytes with a 64-bit hash (Guava Hashing.murmur3_128).
    private fun column(key: String, row: Int) =
        Math.floorMod(mix(key.hashCode() + row * 0x9E3779B9.toInt()), width)

    fun add(key: String, count: Long = 1) {
        for (row in 0 until depth) table[row][column(key, row)] += count
    }

    /** The smallest of the row counters: collisions only ever add, so this is an upper bound. */
    fun estimate(key: String): Long = (0 until depth).minOf { table[it][column(key, it)] }
}

fun main() {
    // 1024 × 4 (32 KB): over by at most e / 1024 ≈ 0.27% of all hits, with 98% probability (1 − e⁻⁴).
    val hits = CountMinSketch(width = 1024, depth = 4)
    repeat(500) { hits.add("/checkout") }
    repeat(300) { hits.add("/cart") }
    repeat(200) { hits.add("/search") }
    for (id in 1..5_000) hits.add("/product/$id")              // the long tail
    val exactCounts = listOf("/checkout" to 500, "/cart" to 300, "/search" to 200, "/product/7" to 1)
    for ((path, exact) in exactCounts) {
        println("$path exact=$exact estimate=${hits.estimate(path)}")
    }
}

/search exact=200 estimate=202

Bloom filter — approximate membership

"Have I already synced this event id?" — definitely not, or probably yes, in about 10 bits per id.

import java.util.BitSet
import kotlin.math.ln
import kotlin.math.roundToInt

fun mix(x: Int): Int {
    var h = x
    h = (h xor (h ushr 16)) * 0x85EBCA6B.toInt()
    h = (h xor (h ushr 13)) * 0xC2B2AE35.toInt()
    return h xor (h ushr 16)
}

class BloomFilter(expected: Int, falsePositiveRate: Double) {
    // m = -n·ln(p) / (ln 2)²    k = (m / n)·ln 2
    val bitCount = (-expected * ln(falsePositiveRate) / (ln(2.0) * ln(2.0))).toInt()
    val hashCount = (bitCount.toDouble() / expected * ln(2.0)).roundToInt()
    private val bits = BitSet(bitCount)

    // Two hashes make all k positions: h1 + i·h2 (Kirsch–Mitzenmacher). String.hashCode is
    // 32 bits and easy to collide on purpose: for untrusted keys use a 64-bit hash of the bytes.
    private fun positions(key: String): List<Int> {
        val h1 = mix(key.hashCode())
        val h2 = mix(h1) or 1
        return List(hashCount) { i -> Math.floorMod(h1 + i * h2, bitCount) }
    }

    fun add(key: String) = positions(key).forEach { bits.set(it) }

    /** false: definitely absent. true: probably present. */
    fun mightContain(key: String) = positions(key).all { bits.get(it) }
}

fun main() {
    // Sized for `expected` ids: past that the false-positive rate climbs (~16% at 2×), so rotate or rebuild.
    val synced = BloomFilter(expected = 10_000, falsePositiveRate = 0.01)
    for (i in 1..10_000) synced.add("evt-$i")
    println("${synced.bitCount / 8 / 1024} KB, ${synced.hashCount} hashes")
    println("evt-42 seen? ${synced.mightContain("evt-42")}")
    val falsePositives = (1..10_000).count { synced.mightContain("new-$it") }
    println("false positives: $falsePositives of 10000 unseen ids")
}
Result
11 KB, 7 hashes
evt-42 seen? true
false positives: 93 of 10000 unseen ids

Heavy hitters — Misra–Gries

The clients hammering an API in O(k) memory, where any client above n / (k + 1) requests is guaranteed to survive.

class HeavyHitters<K>(private val capacity: Int) {
    private val counters = LinkedHashMap<K, Long>()          // Long: a busy stream outgrows Int

    fun add(key: K) {
        val current = counters[key]
        when {
            current != null -> counters[key] = current + 1
            counters.size < capacity -> counters[key] = 1L
            else -> {
                // No free slot: everyone loses one, and whoever reaches zero frees a slot.
                for (entry in counters.entries) entry.setValue(entry.value - 1)
                counters.values.removeAll { it == 0L }
            }
        }
    }

    /** Counts are lower bounds: each may be short by at most n / (k + 1). */
    fun top(): List<Pair<K, Long>> =
        counters.entries.sortedByDescending { it.value }.map { it.key to it.value }
}

fun main() {
    val requests = (0 until 1_000).map { i ->
        when (i % 10) {
            in 0..3 -> "crawler-7"              // 40% of the traffic
            in 4..6 -> "mobile-app"             // 30%
            else -> "user-${i % 97}"            // a long tail of real users
        }
    }
    val hitters = HeavyHitters<String>(capacity = 4)
    requests.forEach(hitters::add)
    println(hitters.top().take(2))
    val exact = requests.groupingBy { it }.eachCount()
    println("exact: crawler-7=${exact["crawler-7"]} mobile-app=${exact["mobile-app"]}")
}
Result

Streaming quantiles

p50 / p95 / p99 latency within 1% relative error, without storing the samples.

import kotlin.math.ceil
import kotlin.math.ln
import kotlin.math.pow
import kotlin.math.roundToLong

/** Log-spaced buckets (the DDSketch idea): relative error bounded, memory O(log(max / min)). */
class QuantileSketch(relativeError: Double = 0.01) {
    private val gamma = (1 + relativeError) / (1 - relativeError)
    private val buckets = sortedMapOf<Int, Long>()
    var count = 0L; private set
    val bucketCount get() = buckets.size

    fun add(positive: Double) {
        require(positive > 0) { "log buckets take positive values; count zeros separately" }
        val index = ceil(ln(positive) / ln(gamma)).toInt()
        buckets[index] = (buckets[index] ?: 0L) + 1
        count++
    }

    fun quantile(q: Double): Double {
        val rank = (q * (count - 1)).toLong()
        var seen = 0L
        for ((index, n) in buckets) {
            seen += n
            if (seen > rank) return 2 * gamma.pow(index) / (gamma + 1)   // the bucket's midpoint
        }
        error("empty sketch")
    }
}

fun main() {
    val latency = QuantileSketch()
    for (ms in 1..10_000) latency.add(ms.toDouble())
    repeat(200) { latency.add(30_000.0) }                  // a slow dependency timing out
    val report = listOf(0.5, 0.95, 0.99)
        .joinToString { q -> "p${(q * 100).toInt()}=${latency.quantile(q).roundToLong()}" }
    println("$report from ${latency.count} samples in ${latency.bucketCount} buckets")
    // Report percentiles, not the mean: the mean here is ~5.5 s and describes nobody.
}
Result
p50=5066, p95=9607, p99=30040 from 10200 samples in 316 buckets

Rate limiting — token bucket vs sliding window

The same arrivals through both limiters, on an injected clock — the bucket lets a refilled trickle through, the window is exact.

import kotlin.time.*
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.milliseconds
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.seconds

/** Bursts up to `capacity`, then `perSecond` sustained. O(1) memory. */
class TokenBucket(private val capacity: Double, private val perSecond: Double, clock: TimeSource) {
    private var tokens = capacity
    private var lastRefill = clock.markNow()

    @Synchronized                                              // request threads call it concurrently
    fun tryAcquire(): Boolean {
        val elapsed = lastRefill.elapsedNow()
        lastRefill += elapsed                                  // advance the mark: no drift
        tokens = minOf(capacity, tokens + elapsed.toDouble(DurationUnit.SECONDS) * perSecond)
        if (tokens < 1) return false
        tokens -= 1
        return true
    }
}

/** At most `limit` in ANY trailing `window`. Exact, O(limit) memory. */
class SlidingWindowLog(private val limit: Int, private val window: Duration, private val clock: TimeSource) {
    private val accepted = ArrayDeque<TimeMark>()

    @Synchronized
    fun tryAcquire(): Boolean {
        while (accepted.isNotEmpty() && accepted.first().elapsedNow() >= window) accepted.removeFirst()
        if (accepted.size >= limit) return false
        accepted.addLast(clock.markNow())
        return true
    }
}

fun verdict(allowed: Boolean) = if (allowed) "ok" else "429"

fun main() {
    val clock = TestTimeSource()
    val bucket = TokenBucket(capacity = 3.0, perSecond = 3.0, clock = clock)
    val window = SlidingWindowLog(limit = 3, window = 1.seconds, clock = clock)
    var now = 0
    for (at in listOf(0, 0, 0, 0, 500, 900, 1000, 1000)) {
        clock += (at - now).milliseconds
        now = at
        println("t=${at}ms bucket=${verdict(bucket.tryAcquire())} window=${verdict(window.tryAcquire())}")
    }
}

Debounce, throttle & sample over a Flow

A search box's keystrokes on virtual time — debounce waits for a pause, throttle keeps the first of each window, sample the latest per tick.

import kotlinx.coroutines.ExperimentalCoroutinesApi
import kotlinx.coroutines.FlowPreview
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest

/** Typed at 0, 120, 240, 640, 700 and 760 ms. */
fun keystrokes(): Flow<String> = flow {
    val typing = listOf("k" to 0L, "ko" to 120L, "kot" to 120L, "kotl" to 400L, "kotli" to 60L,
        "kotlin" to 60L)
    for ((text, pauseMs) in typing) {
        delay(pauseMs)
        emit(text)
    }
}

/** Flow has no throttle-first: the first value of each window passes, the rest are dropped. */
fun <T> Flow<T>.throttleFirst(windowMs: Long, now: () -> Long): Flow<T> = flow {
    var windowStart: Long? = null
    collect { value ->
        val start = windowStart
        if (start == null || now() - start >= windowMs) {
            windowStart = now()
            emit(value)
        }
    }
}

@OptIn(FlowPreview::class, ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)   // debounce/sample; virtual currentTime
fun main() = runTest {
    println("debounce(300): " + keystrokes().debounce(300).toList())
    val clock = { testScheduler.currentTime }
    println("throttle(300): " + keystrokes().throttleFirst(300, clock).toList())
    println("sample(250):   " + keystrokes().sample(250).toList())
}

Backpressure & buffering policy

A sensor emitting every 10 ms into a 27 ms consumer — when production outruns consumption, choose what to lose.

import kotlinx.coroutines.ExperimentalCoroutinesApi
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.BufferOverflow
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.toList
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.TestScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest

fun readings(): Flow<Int> = flow { for (i in 1..8) { delay(10); emit(i) } }

@OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)                       // the virtual testScheduler.currentTime
suspend fun TestScope.render(policy: String, source: Flow<Int>) {
    val start = testScheduler.currentTime
    val shown = mutableListOf<Int>()
    source.collect { delay(27); shown += it }
    println("$policy $shown in ${testScheduler.currentTime - start} ms")
}

fun main() = runTest {
    render("suspend (default)     ", readings())                                   // producer slowed down
    render("buffer(2, DROP_OLDEST)", readings().buffer(2, BufferOverflow.DROP_OLDEST))
    render("conflate()            ", readings().conflate())                        // only the latest waits
    val latest = mutableListOf<Int>()
    readings().collectLatest { delay(27); latest += it }                           // new value cancels work
    println("collectLatest          $latest")

    // A Channel states its policy up front; trySend never suspends.
    val telemetry = Channel<Int>(capacity = 2, onBufferOverflow = BufferOverflow.DROP_OLDEST)
    for (i in 1..5) telemetry.trySend(i)
    telemetry.close()
    println("Channel(2, DROP_OLDEST) kept ${telemetry.toList()}")
    val strict = Channel<Int>(capacity = 2)                                        // SUSPEND when full
    println("Channel(2) trySend: ${(1..3).map { strict.trySend(it).isSuccess }}")
}

conflate()             [1, 3, 6, 8] in 118 ms

flowOn moves the upstream, never collect

Blocking parse work belongs above `flowOn(Dispatchers.IO)` or inside `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`, because the body of `collect` always runs in the collector's context.

import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext

fun onIo() = Thread.currentThread().name.startsWith("DefaultDispatcher-worker")

/** Decoding one uploaded chunk: blocking work that must stay off the collector's thread. */
fun decode(chunk: String): String {
    Thread.sleep(5)                                             // stands in for blocking I/O or parsing
    return chunk.uppercase()
}

fun main() = runBlocking {
    val chunks = flowOf("a", "b")

    // flowOn moves only what is ABOVE it (and inserts a buffer): map runs on IO, collect stays on main.
    chunks.map { "${decode(it)} decoded on IO=${onIo()}" }
        .flowOn(Dispatchers.IO)
        .collect { println("$it, collected on IO=${onIo()}") }

    // Blocking work that has to happen inside collect: wrap that call, not the flow.
    chunks.collect { chunk ->
        val decoded = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { "${decode(chunk)} decoded on IO=${onIo()}" }
        println("$decoded, collected on IO=${onIo()}")
    }
}
Result
A decoded on IO=true, collected on IO=false
B decoded on IO=true, collected on IO=false
A decoded on IO=true, collected on IO=false
B decoded on IO=true, collected on IO=false

Batching, chunking and coalescing

Upload telemetry when 3 events are waiting or the oldest has waited 200 ms, whichever comes first.

import kotlinx.coroutines.ExperimentalCoroutinesApi
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.selects.onTimeout
import kotlinx.coroutines.selects.select
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest

@OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)
fun <T> Flow<T>.batched(size: Int, maxWaitMs: Long, now: () -> Long): Flow<List<T>> = channelFlow {
    val upstream = this@batched.produceIn(this)
    val batch = mutableListOf<T>()
    var openedAt = 0L
    var open = true
    while (open) {
        select<Unit> {                              // atomic: an element is received OR the timer fires
            upstream.onReceiveCatching { result ->
                if (result.isClosed) open = false
                else { if (batch.isEmpty()) openedAt = now(); batch += result.getOrThrow() }
            }
            if (batch.isNotEmpty()) onTimeout(openedAt + maxWaitMs - now()) {}
        }
        val due = batch.size >= size || !open || now() - openedAt >= maxWaitMs
        if (batch.isNotEmpty() && due) { send(batch.toList()); batch.clear() }
    }
}

@OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)
fun main() = runTest {
    // Events at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 ms, then a quiet spell, then 550 and 560 ms.
    val pauses = listOf("a" to 10L, "b" to 10L, "c" to 10L, "d" to 10L, "e" to 10L, "f" to 500L, "g" to 10L)
    val events = flow { for ((name, pauseMs) in pauses) { delay(pauseMs); emit(name) } }
    events.batched(size = 3, maxWaitMs = 200) { testScheduler.currentTime }
        .collect { println("at ${testScheduler.currentTime} ms upload $it") }
    println("chunked(3): ${events.chunked(3).toList()}")      // size only, never time
}

Deduplication with a TTL

Remember each payment id as in flight while its handler runs and as done for 5 minutes after it succeeds, in bounded memory.

import kotlin.time.*
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.minutes

enum class Seen { NEW, IN_FLIGHT, DONE }

// Synchronized: deliveries arrive on many threads. Past `capacity` done ids the oldest are forgotten
// early (size it as peak rate × TTL); an in-flight id is never evicted.
class RecentIds(private val ttl: Duration, private val capacity: Int, private val clock: TimeSource) {
    private val inFlight = HashSet<String>()
    private val doneAt = LinkedHashMap<String, TimeMark>()          // insertion order is age order

    @Synchronized fun begin(id: String): Seen {
        val oldestFirst = doneAt.values.iterator()
        while (oldestFirst.hasNext() && oldestFirst.next().elapsedNow() >= ttl) oldestFirst.remove()
        return when (id) {
            in inFlight -> Seen.IN_FLIGHT
            in doneAt -> Seen.DONE
            else -> Seen.NEW.also { inFlight += id }
        }
    }

    /** Only a success is remembered: after a failure the next delivery is handled again. */
    @Synchronized fun finish(id: String, succeeded: Boolean) {
        inFlight -= id
        if (!succeeded) return
        doneAt[id] = clock.markNow()
        if (doneAt.size > capacity) doneAt.remove(doneAt.keys.first())
    }
}

fun main() {
    val clock = TestTimeSource()
    val recent = RecentIds(ttl = 5.minutes, capacity = 10_000, clock = clock)
    println("first delivery:      ${recent.begin("pay-1")}")
    println("retry while running: ${recent.begin("pay-1")}")
    recent.finish("pay-1", succeeded = false)
    println("retry after failure: ${recent.begin("pay-1")}")
    recent.finish("pay-1", succeeded = true)
    println("redelivery:          ${recent.begin("pay-1")}")
    clock += 6.minutes
    println("6 minutes later:     ${recent.begin("pay-1")}")
}
Result
first delivery:      NEW
retry while running: IN_FLIGHT
retry after failure: NEW
redelivery:          DONE
6 minutes later:     NEW

Idempotent webhook handling

Webhooks arrive at least once, so answer a redelivery of a handled payment with 200, one still being handled with 409, and a failure with 500 so the provider retries.

enum class Seen { NEW, IN_FLIGHT, DONE }

class Deliveries {                                               // the card above, minus TTL and capacity
    private val inFlight = HashSet<String>()
    private val done = HashSet<String>()

    @Synchronized fun begin(id: String): Seen = when (id) {
        in inFlight -> Seen.IN_FLIGHT
        in done -> Seen.DONE
        else -> Seen.NEW.also { inFlight += id }
    }

    @Synchronized fun finish(id: String, succeeded: Boolean) {
        inFlight -= id
        if (succeeded) done += id
    }
}

// In a database: insert a pending row with an expiry, mark it done after handling — a crash in between
// must leave a row that expires, or every retry is skipped forever.
fun deliver(deliveries: Deliveries, id: String, handle: (String) -> Unit): String {
    val state = deliveries.begin(id)
    if (state == Seen.DONE) return "200 duplicate, skipped"
    if (state == Seen.IN_FLIGHT) return "409 in progress, provider retries later"
    var succeeded = false
    try {
        handle(id)
        succeeded = true
        return "200 processed"
    } catch (e: Exception) {
        return "500 failed, provider retries"                  // not a 2xx: the provider delivers again
    } finally {
        deliveries.finish(id, succeeded)                       // on an Error too: never stuck in flight
    }
}

fun main() {
    val deliveries = Deliveries()
    val slowThenFails: (String) -> Unit = { id ->                 // the provider times out and redelivers
        println("retry during attempt 1 -> ${deliver(deliveries, id) {}}")
        error("ledger timeout")
    }
    println("attempt 1  -> ${deliver(deliveries, "pay-1", slowThenFails)}")
    for (label in listOf("retry     ", "redelivery")) println("$label -> ${deliver(deliveries, "pay-1") {}}")
}
Result
retry during attempt 1 -> 409 in progress, provider retries later
attempt 1  -> 500 failed, provider retries
retry      -> 200 processed
redelivery -> 200 duplicate, skipped

Merging ordered streams & change detection

Merge two sensors' time-ordered readings into one timeline, then raise an alarm with hysteresis so it does not flap.

import java.util.PriorityQueue

data class Reading(val atMs: Long, val sensor: String, val celsius: Double)

/** k-way merge of streams each sorted by time: O(log k) per item, O(k) memory. */
fun mergeByTime(streams: List<Sequence<Reading>>): Sequence<Reading> = sequence {
    val sources = streams.map { it.iterator() }
    val heads = PriorityQueue<Pair<Reading, Int>>(compareBy { it.first.atMs })
    sources.forEachIndexed { i, source -> if (source.hasNext()) heads += source.next() to i }
    while (heads.isNotEmpty()) {
        val (reading, i) = heads.poll()
        yield(reading)
        if (sources[i].hasNext()) heads += sources[i].next() to i
    }
}

/** Two thresholds: ON above `enter`, OFF only below `exit`. Returns the new state, or null. */
class Hysteresis(private val enter: Double, private val exit: Double) {
    private var on = false
    fun update(x: Double): Boolean? = when {
        !on && x > enter -> true.also { on = true }
        on && x < exit -> false.also { on = false }
        else -> null
    }
}

fun main() {
    val a = sequenceOf(Reading(0, "A", 78.0), Reading(20, "A", 81.0), Reading(40, "A", 80.5),
        Reading(60, "A", 73.0))
    val b = sequenceOf(Reading(10, "B", 79.0), Reading(30, "B", 79.5), Reading(50, "B", 81.5))
    val timeline = mergeByTime(listOf(a, b)).toList()
    println(timeline.map { "${it.atMs}${it.sensor}" })
    val alarm = Hysteresis(enter = 80.0, exit = 75.0)
    for (r in timeline) {
        alarm.update(r.celsius)?.let { on -> println("${r.atMs} ms alarm ${if (on) "ON" else "OFF"}") }
    }
    val flips = timeline.map { it.celsius > 80.0 }.zipWithNext().count { (x, y) -> x != y }
    println("a single threshold would have flipped $flips times")
}
Result
[0A, 10B, 20A, 30B, 40A, 50B, 60A]
20 ms alarm ON
60 ms alarm OFF
a single threshold would have flipped 4 times

What are the top K keys?Misra–Gries / Space-SavingO(k)may miss keys at or below n / (k + 1); counts low by at most thatDataSketches FrequentItemsSketch (ItemsSketch before 9.0)
What is the p95 latency?DDSketch / KLL / t-digestO(log range) / O(1 / ε) / O(compression)DDSketch: ≤ α relative value error; KLL: ± ε·n rank; t-digest: tightest at the tailscom.datadoghq:sketches-java, DataSketches KllDoublesSketch, com.tdunning:t-digest, HdrHistogram
A uniform sample of k itemsReservoir samplingO(k)unbiased: each item kept with probability k / nhand-rolled (above)
A rolling averageRing buffer or EMAO(k) or O(1)exact / smoothedhand-rolled (above)
Exact counts, bounded keysHashMap / groupingBy().eachCount()O(distinct)exactstandard library

Streaming pitfalls

The ones Kotlin makes easy to fall into.

  • Unbounded buffers: Channel(UNLIMITED) or buffer(UNLIMITED) on a hot source grows until the process dies. State a capacity and an onBufferOverflow.
  • Using StateFlow as an event stream — it conflates and skips equal values, so events vanish. Events go through a Channel or a buffered SharedFlow.
  • MutableSharedFlow() with no buffer: tryEmit always returns false once anyone subscribes, busy or idle. Give it extraBufferCapacity and a BufferOverflow policy.
  • Blocking inside collect (Thread.sleep, file or socket I/O) stalls the whole pipeline. Suspend; wrap the blocking call in withContext(Dispatchers.IO); or do the work in an upstream map { } and put flowOn(Dispatchers.IO) after it. flowOn moves only what is above it, never the collect block, and it inserts a buffer.
  • Measuring time with System.currentTimeMillis(): the wall clock jumps. Use TimeSource.Monotonic (or System.nanoTime) in production and a test source in tests.
  • Recomputing the whole window per event (O(n·k)) — slide it. Summing squares for variance — use Welford.
  • Assuming exactly-once delivery. Design for at-least-once and make the consumer idempotent.
  • Decide the lateness policy for event time explicitly: drop, hold until a watermark, or re-open the window and re-emit.
  • Instrument the stream itself: input rate, drop count, queue depth, end-to-end lag.

Virtual time with runTest

Inside `runTest`, `delay` advances a virtual clock — a 300 ms debounce is tested instantly.

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.*

class Debouncer(private val scope: CoroutineScope, private val waitMs: Long, private val action: (String) -> Unit) {
    private var pending: Job? = null
    fun submit(value: String) {
        pending?.cancel()
        pending = scope.launch { delay(waitMs); action(value) }
    }
}

fun main() = runTest {
    val saved = mutableListOf<String>()
    val debouncer = Debouncer(this, 300, saved::add)
    debouncer.submit("h")
    debouncer.submit("he")
    debouncer.submit("hey")
    advanceTimeBy(299); runCurrent()
    check(saved.isEmpty())
    advanceTimeBy(1); runCurrent()
    check(saved == listOf("hey"))
    println("saved $saved at virtual $currentTime ms")
}
Result
saved [hey] at virtual 300 ms
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc), JDK 17 or later, and the jars kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm-1.10.2 and kotlinx-coroutines-test-jvm-1.10.2
  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc -cp <both jars> main.kt -d out && kotlin -cp out:<both jars> MainKt
  3. In a project the same body goes in a @Test fun with testImplementation("org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-test:1.10.2")

Design for testability — inject the clock

A `fun interface` makes the seam a lambda in tests.

fun interface Clock { fun nowMs(): Long }

class Session(private val clock: Clock, private val ttlMs: Long) {
    private val started = clock.nowMs()
    fun expired() = clock.nowMs() - started >= ttlMs
}

fun main() {
    var now = 1_000L
    val session = Session({ now }, ttlMs = 500)
    check(!session.expired())
    now += 500                             // the test owns time: no sleeping
    check(session.expired())
    println("expired after ${now - 1_000} ms of fake time")
}
Result
expired after 500 ms of fake time

A JUnit 5 test class

Backtick names read as sentences; `assertThrows<T>` is JUnit's Kotlin extension.

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
import org.junit.jupiter.api.assertThrows

fun slugify(title: String): String {
    require(title.isNotBlank()) { "blank title" }
    return title.trim().lowercase().replace(Regex("[^a-z0-9]+"), "-").trim('-')
}

class SlugTest {
    @Test
    fun `joins words with single hyphens`() = assertEquals("hello-world", slugify("  Hello, World!  "))

    @Test
    fun `rejects blank titles`() {
        assertThrows<IllegalArgumentException> { slugify("   ") }
    }
}
Result

./gradlew test reports both tests passed.

Test doubles — which to use when

Reach for the simplest double that lets the test assert on an outcome; a framework mock is the last resort, not the default.

DoubleWhat it isUse it whenIn Kotlin
Fakea working, simplified implementation (an in-memory repository)the default for collaborators you own; assert on the state it ends ina small class implementing the interface
Stubreturns canned answers and records nothinga dependency only feeds input: a clock, a feature flag, an approving payment gatewaya fun interface lambda: PaymentGateway { true }
Spya fake or real object that also records its callsthe outcome is a call leaving the system: an email, an analytics eventa lambda or small class that appends to a sent list
Mocka generated double with expectations verified by a frameworkcode you cannot fake cheaply (a final SDK class), or when the interaction itself is the contractMockK: every { gateway.charge(any()) } returns true, then verify(exactly = 1) { gateway.charge(12990) }
Dummypassed in but never useda parameter the path under test ignoresLogger { } or a default argument

A hand-written fake, a stub and a spy

Interfaces at the seams make every double a few lines, and the test checks outcomes — the fake's state and the spy's recorded calls — rather than call sequences.

data class Order(val id: String, val email: String, val totalCents: Long, val paid: Boolean = false)

interface OrderRepository {
    fun find(id: String): Order?
    fun save(order: Order)
}

fun interface PaymentGateway { fun charge(amountCents: Long): Boolean }

fun interface EmailSender { fun send(to: String, subject: String) }

class CheckoutService(
    private val orders: OrderRepository, private val payments: PaymentGateway, private val email: EmailSender,
) {
    fun pay(orderId: String): Result<Order> {
        val order = orders.find(orderId) ?: return Result.failure(NoSuchElementException(orderId))
        if (order.paid) return Result.success(order)      // a repeated tap; concurrent taps need a lock
        if (!payments.charge(order.totalCents)) return Result.failure(IllegalStateException("declined"))
        val paid = order.copy(paid = true).also(orders::save)
        email.send(order.email, "Order ${order.id} confirmed")
        return Result.success(paid)
    }
}

// Fake: a working in-memory implementation you own; assert on its state.
class InMemoryOrderRepository(vararg seed: Order) : OrderRepository {
    private val byId = seed.associateBy { it.id }.toMutableMap()
    override fun find(id: String) = byId[id]
    override fun save(order: Order) { byId[order.id] = order }
}

fun main() {
    val ana = Order("ORD-1042", "ana@example.com", 12990)
    val bo = Order("ORD-1043", "bo@example.com", 500)
    val orders = InMemoryOrderRepository(ana, bo)
    val sent = mutableListOf<String>()
    val email = EmailSender { to, subject -> sent += "$to: $subject" }          // spy: records what left

    val approving = CheckoutService(orders, payments = { true }, email = email)   // stub: always approves
    approving.pay(ana.id)
    approving.pay(ana.id)                                                          // the second tap on "Pay"
    val declined = CheckoutService(orders, payments = { false }, email = email).pay(bo.id)

    println("paid: ${orders.find(ana.id)?.paid}, ${orders.find(bo.id)?.paid}")    // state, from the fake
    println("declined: ${declined.exceptionOrNull()?.message}")
    println("emails sent: $sent")                                                  // calls, from the spy
}
Result
paid: true, false
declined: declined
emails sent: [ana@example.com: Order ORD-1042 confirmed]
Setup

  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar — in a project the body of main is a @Test and the doubles live in src/test

An integration test across a real HTTP boundary

Serve canned responses from a `com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer` bound to the literal `127.0.0.1` on port 0 (not `localhost` or the loopback address, which can resolve to `::1` on IPv6-first CI) and point the real client at it, so headers, status handling and parsing are exercised with no network.

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
import java.io.IOException
import java.net.*
import java.net.http.*
import java.time.Duration

class InventoryClient(private val base: URI, private val token: String, private val http: HttpClient) {
    fun available(sku: String): Int? {
        val request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(base.resolve("/stock/$sku"))
            .header("Authorization", "Bearer $token").timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(2)).build()
        val response = http.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString())
        return when (response.statusCode()) {
            200 -> response.body().trim().toInt()
            404 -> null                                    // an unknown SKU is an answer, not an error
            else -> throw IOException("inventory returned ${response.statusCode()}")
        }
    }
}

fun main() {
    val server = HttpServer.create(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0)     // port 0: any free port
    server.createContext("/stock/") { exchange ->
        val (status, body) = when {
            exchange.requestHeaders.getFirst("Authorization") != "Bearer test-token" -> 401 to "no token"
            exchange.requestURI.path == "/stock/SHOE-42" -> 200 to "3"      // the exact path, nothing else
            exchange.requestURI.path == "/stock/BUSY-1" -> 503 to "try again later"
            else -> 404 to "unknown sku"
        }
        exchange.sendResponseHeaders(status, body.toByteArray().size.toLong())
        exchange.responseBody.use { it.write(body.toByteArray()) }
    }
    server.start()
    try {
        HttpClient.newHttpClient().use { http ->
            val client = InventoryClient(URI("http://127.0.0.1:${server.address.port}"), "test-token", http)
            val skus = listOf("SHOE-42", "HAT-7", "BUSY-1")                     // printed in call order
            println(skus.map { sku -> runCatching { client.available(sku) }.getOrElse { it.message } })
        }
    } finally {
        server.stop(0)                                     // nothing is left listening
    }
}
Result
[3, null, inventory returned 503]
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc) and JDK 21 or later (HttpClient is AutoCloseable from 21)
  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar — it starts its own server on a free loopback port and stops it
  3. In a JUnit class, start the server in @BeforeEach and stop(0) it in @AfterEach, one fresh server per test

Ran with kotlinc 2.4.21, JVM 21.0.12.1 on 2026-11-16: the output matched the result shown.

Sources: java.net.http.HttpClient — Java SE 21 API · com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer — Java SE 21 API

Principles worth stating

The same in every language.

  • Fakes you own (an in-memory repository, a Clock) over mocks of code you do not.
  • Inject dispatchers and scopes; in tests pass StandardTestDispatcher or the TestScope itself.
  • Thread.sleep or real delay in tests: slow and flaky — use virtual time.
  • runTest fails a test that leaves coroutines running — a free leak check.

Clean Code in Kotlin

Names, small functions, named arguments over flags, KDoc that earns its place, sealed results over sentinels, guard clauses, value classes and clean tests — every before/after proved to print the same.

  • jvm
  • android
  • kotlin >=2.0
  • jvm >=17
  • Kotlin/JVM (the standard library and java.time); the same code runs on Android

Sources: Coding conventions — Kotlin docs · Scope functions — Kotlin docs · Inline value classes — Kotlin docs · Document Kotlin code — KDoc

Uncle Bob rule → Kotlin idiom

The classic rules still hold; Kotlin's type system and syntax enforce most of them for you.

Clean Code ruleThe Kotlin way to satisfy it
Avoid nullnullable types with ?. and ?:; return emptyList(), not null; a nullable lookup says so in its name (findOrNull)
Don't return error codesa sealed interface result for expected outcomes; require / check / error() for a broken contract
Prefer polymorphism to switcha sealed hierarchy with an exhaustive when (no else) when the set is closed; an interface when it is open
Encapsulate conditionalsan extension property or function: val Order.isRefundable: Boolean
Avoid output argumentsreturn a new value (copy(...)); take read-only List parameters
No flag argumentsname every Boolean argument at the call site; when two flags encode one choice, an enum class
Avoid primitive obsession@JvmInline value class with a validating factory, created once at the boundary
Keep classes smalltop-level functions and extensions; a class when it owns state or injected dependencies
Separate construction from useconstructor injection; one composition root (Application.onCreate, main) wires the graph
Comments explain whyKDoc on public API, with [name] links; // why beside surprising code; never // what

Naming

Intention-revealing and searchable — `camelCase` values, `PascalCase` types, `SCREAMING_CASE` constants, `is`/`has` booleans, properties instead of `get` functions.

Don't
data class O(val i: String, val t: Int, val s: Int, val d: Int)

val list1 = listOf(
    O("A-1", 4200, 2, 3),
    O("A-2", 1500, 1, 12),
    O("A-3", 9900, 2, 45),
    O("A-4", 2500, 2, 30),
)

fun proc(a: List<O>): List<String> {
    val r = mutableListOf<String>()
    for (o in a) if (o.s == 2 && o.d <= 30) r.add(o.i)   // 2? 30?
    return r
}

fun main() {
    val flag = proc(list1).isNotEmpty()
    println("${proc(list1)} $flag")
}
Do
enum class OrderStatus { PLACED, DELIVERED }

data class Order(val id: String, val totalCents: Int, val status: OrderStatus, val ageInDays: Int)

const val REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS = 30

val Order.isRefundable: Boolean
    get() = status == OrderStatus.DELIVERED && ageInDays <= REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS

fun List<Order>.refundableIds(): List<String> = filter { it.isRefundable }.map { it.id }

fun main() {
    val orders = listOf(
        Order("A-1", 4200, OrderStatus.DELIVERED, ageInDays = 3),
        Order("A-2", 1500, OrderStatus.PLACED, ageInDays = 12),
        Order("A-3", 9900, OrderStatus.DELIVERED, ageInDays = 45),
        Order("A-4", 2500, OrderStatus.DELIVERED, ageInDays = 30),   // the last day still counts
    )
    val refundableIds = orders.refundableIds()
    val hasRefundableOrders = refundableIds.isNotEmpty()
    println("$refundableIds $hasRefundableOrders")
}
Result
[A-1, A-4] true

Small functions, one level of abstraction

When a function needs blank lines or comments to separate its steps, each step wants to be a private function with that name.

Before
data class Item(val sku: String, val priceCents: Long, val quantity: Int, val onSale: Boolean)
data class Cart(val tier: String, val items: List<Item>)

fun checkout(cart: Cart): String {
    var total = 0L
    for (item in cart.items) {
        require(item.quantity > 0) { "bad quantity for ${item.sku}" }
        var price = item.priceCents
        if (item.onSale) price = price * 80 / 100
        if (cart.tier == "pro") price = price * 90 / 100
        total += price * item.quantity
    }
    if (total > 10_000) total -= 500
    val tax = total * 21 / 100
    return "total=${total + tax} tax=$tax"
}

fun main() {
    val items = listOf(Item("mug", 1200, 2, onSale = true), Item("lamp", 9900, 1, onSale = false))
    println(checkout(Cart("pro", items)))
}
After
enum class Tier(val percentPaid: Long) { FREE(100), PRO(90) }
data class Item(val sku: String, val priceCents: Long, val quantity: Int, val onSale: Boolean)
data class Cart(val tier: Tier, val items: List<Item>)
data class Receipt(val totalCents: Long, val taxCents: Long)

private const val SALE_PERCENT_PAID = 80L
private const val BULK_THRESHOLD_CENTS = 10_000L
private const val BULK_DISCOUNT_CENTS = 500L
private const val TAX_PERCENT = 21L

fun checkout(cart: Cart): Receipt {
    val subtotal = cart.items.sumOf { lineTotalCents(it, cart.tier) }
    val discounted = applyBulkDiscount(subtotal)
    val tax = taxCents(discounted)
    return Receipt(totalCents = discounted + tax, taxCents = tax)
}

private fun lineTotalCents(item: Item, tier: Tier): Long {
    require(item.quantity > 0) { "bad quantity for ${item.sku}" }
    val unitPrice = if (item.onSale) item.priceCents * SALE_PERCENT_PAID / 100 else item.priceCents
    return unitPrice * tier.percentPaid / 100 * item.quantity
}

private fun applyBulkDiscount(cents: Long): Long =
    if (cents > BULK_THRESHOLD_CENTS) cents - BULK_DISCOUNT_CENTS else cents

private fun taxCents(cents: Long): Long = cents * TAX_PERCENT / 100

fun main() {
    val items = listOf(Item("mug", 1200, 2, onSale = true), Item("lamp", 9900, 1, onSale = false))
    val receipt = checkout(Cart(Tier.PRO, items))
    println("total=${receipt.totalCents} tax=${receipt.taxCents}")
}
Result
total=12266 tax=2128

  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar

Named and default arguments over flags and builders

A positional `true` is unreadable, so name Boolean arguments, turn two flags that encode one choice into an `enum`, and let default arguments plus `copy` replace a hand-written builder.

Don't
class Notification(val orderId: String) {
    var channel: String = "email"
    var urgent: Boolean = false
    var retries: Int = 3
}

class NotificationBuilder(orderId: String) {           // a Java habit
    private val notification = Notification(orderId)
    fun channel(value: String) = apply { notification.channel = value }
    fun urgent(value: Boolean) = apply { notification.urgent = value }
    fun build() = notification
}

fun render(orderId: String, compact: Boolean, includePrices: Boolean): String {
    if (compact) return "Order $orderId"
    return if (includePrices) "Order $orderId (with prices)" else "Order $orderId"
}

fun main() {
    val n = NotificationBuilder("A-1").channel("sms").urgent(true).build()
    println("${n.orderId} ${n.channel} urgent=${n.urgent} retries=${n.retries}")
    println(render("A-1", false, true))                 // which flag was which?
}
Do
enum class Channel { EMAIL, SMS }
enum class Detail { SUMMARY, WITH_PRICES }

data class Notification(                                 // immutable; defaults replace the builder
    val orderId: String,
    val channel: Channel = Channel.EMAIL,
    val urgent: Boolean = false,
    val retries: Int = 3,
)

fun render(orderId: String, detail: Detail = Detail.SUMMARY): String = when (detail) {
    Detail.SUMMARY -> "Order $orderId"
    Detail.WITH_PRICES -> "Order $orderId (with prices)"
}

fun main() {
    val n = Notification("A-1", channel = Channel.SMS, urgent = true)
    println("${n.orderId} ${n.channel.name.lowercase()} urgent=${n.urgent} retries=${n.retries}")
    println(render("A-1", Detail.WITH_PRICES))
    // A variant is a copy, not a mutation: n.copy(retries = 0)
}
Result
A-1 sms urgent=true retries=3
Order A-1 (with prices)

Comments that earn their place

KDoc says what a caller needs to know; an inline comment says why the code is surprising — never what it does.

Noise
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit

data class Order(val id: String, val totalCents: Long, val shippingCents: Long, val deliveredOn: LocalDate?)

// refund function
fun refund(o: Order, today: LocalDate): Long {
    // check delivered
    require(o.deliveredOn != null) { "order ${o.id} is not delivered" }
    // get the days
    val d = ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(o.deliveredOn, today)
    // if d <= 30 return total else total minus shipping
    return if (d <= 30) o.totalCents else o.totalCents - o.shippingCents
    // return (o.totalCents * 0.9).toLong()   old logic, keep just in case
}

// TODO fix

    val today = LocalDate.of(2026, 11, 16)
    val recent = Order("A-1", 4200, 500, LocalDate.of(2026, 11, 1))
    val old = Order("A-2", 4200, 500, LocalDate.of(2026, 9, 1))

Useful
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit

data class Order(val id: String, val totalCents: Long, val shippingCents: Long, val deliveredOn: LocalDate?)

const val REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS = 30

/**
 * Returns how much of [order] to refund, in cents.
 *
 * Inside [REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS] the refund is the full total; after it the
 * shipping fee is kept back, never the item price.
 *
 * @param today the current date, passed in so callers and tests control it.
 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the order has not been delivered.
 */
fun refundCents(order: Order, today: LocalDate): Long {
    val deliveredOn = requireNotNull(order.deliveredOn) { "order ${order.id} is not delivered" }
    val daysSinceDelivery = ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(deliveredOn, today)
    if (daysSinceDelivery <= REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS) return order.totalCents
    // The carrier bills late returns to us (contract §4.2), so the fee covers it.
    return order.totalCents - order.shippingCents
}

fun main() {
    val today = LocalDate.of(2026, 11, 16)
    val recent = Order("A-1", 4200, 500, LocalDate.of(2026, 11, 1))
    val old = Order("A-2", 4200, 500, LocalDate.of(2026, 9, 1))
    println("${refundCents(recent, today)} ${refundCents(old, today)}")
}
Result
4200 3700

Sealed results over sentinel values

Expected outcomes are a `sealed interface` the caller must `when` over, and a broken contract (a caller bug) is `require`.

Sentinels
val stock = mapOf("mug" to 3, "lamp" to 0)

fun reserve(sku: String, quantity: Int): Int {        // remaining stock, or a code
    if (quantity <= 0) return -2                      // bad quantity
    val available = stock[sku] ?: return -1           // unknown product
    if (quantity > available) return -3               // not enough
    return available - quantity
}

fun main() {
    for ((sku, qty) in listOf("mug" to 2, "lamp" to 1, "desk" to 1, "mug" to 0)) {
        val result = reserve(sku, qty)
        println(
            when (result) {
                -1 -> "$sku: unknown product"
                -2 -> "$sku: quantity must be positive"
                -3 -> "$sku: only ${stock[sku]} left"
                else -> "$sku: reserved, $result left"   // and -4 next year?
            }
        )
    }
}
Sealed result
sealed interface Reservation {
    data class Reserved(val remaining: Int) : Reservation
    data class OutOfStock(val available: Int) : Reservation
    data object UnknownProduct : Reservation
}

val stock = mapOf("mug" to 3, "lamp" to 0)

fun stockLevelOrNull(sku: String): Int? = stock[sku]   // null means one thing: no such product

fun reserve(sku: String, quantity: Int): Reservation {
    require(quantity > 0) { "quantity must be positive, was $quantity" }
    val available = stockLevelOrNull(sku) ?: return Reservation.UnknownProduct
    if (quantity > available) return Reservation.OutOfStock(available)
    return Reservation.Reserved(available - quantity)
}

fun main() {
    for ((sku, qty) in listOf("mug" to 2, "lamp" to 1, "desk" to 1, "mug" to 0)) {
        if (qty <= 0) {                                                          // validate at the edge
            println("$sku: quantity must be positive")
            continue
        }
        val message = when (val result = reserve(sku, qty)) {                    // exhaustive: no else
            is Reservation.Reserved -> "$sku: reserved, ${result.remaining} left"
            is Reservation.OutOfStock -> "$sku: only ${result.available} left"
            Reservation.UnknownProduct -> "$sku: unknown product"
        }
        println(message)
    }
}
Result
mug: reserved, 1 left
lamp: only 0 left
desk: unknown product
mug: quantity must be positive

Guard clauses, not `?.let` pyramids

`val x = y ?: return …` keeps the happy path at the left margin; nested scope functions are Kotlin's arrow anti-pattern.

Nested
data class Address(val city: String?, val postcode: String?)
data class Customer(val name: String, val address: Address?)

fun shippingLabel(customer: Customer?): String {
    customer?.let { c ->
        c.address?.let { a ->
            a.city?.let { city ->
                a.postcode?.let {
                    if (it.length == 5) {
                        return "${c.name}, $it $city"
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return "address incomplete"
}

fun main() {
    println(shippingLabel(Customer("Ada", Address("Lyon", "69001"))))
    println(shippingLabel(Customer("Linus", Address(null, "00100"))))
    println(shippingLabel(null))
}
Flat
data class Address(val city: String?, val postcode: String?)
data class Customer(val name: String, val address: Address?)

fun shippingLabel(customer: Customer?): String {
    val address = customer?.address ?: return "address incomplete"
    val city = address.city ?: return "address incomplete"
    val postcode = address.postcode?.takeIf { it.length == 5 } ?: return "address incomplete"
    return "${customer.name}, $postcode $city"            // customer is smart-cast to non-null
}

fun main() {
    println(shippingLabel(Customer("Ada", Address("Lyon", "69001"))))
    println(shippingLabel(Customer("Linus", Address(null, "00100"))))
    println(shippingLabel(null))
}
Result
Ada, 69001 Lyon
address incomplete
address incomplete

Value classes beat primitives

A `@JvmInline value class` turns a swapped `String` argument into a compile error and costs nothing when used as itself (it is boxed when nullable, generic or behind an interface); parse once, at the boundary.

import kotlin.math.abs
import java.util.Locale

@JvmInline
value class OrderId(val value: String) {
    init { require(value.matches(Regex("[A-Z]-\\d+"))) { "not an order id: $value" } }
}

@JvmInline
value class Email private constructor(val value: String) {
    companion object {
        fun parseOrNull(raw: String): Email? {
            val normalized = raw.trim().lowercase()
            val domain = normalized.substringAfter('@', missingDelimiterValue = "")
            return if ('.' in domain && normalized.count { it == '@' } == 1) Email(normalized) else null
        }
    }
}

@JvmInline
value class Cents(val amount: Long) {
    operator fun plus(other: Cents) = Cents(amount + other.amount)
    override fun toString(): String {
        val sign = if (amount < 0) "-" else ""
        return "%s%d.%02d".format(Locale.ROOT, sign, abs(amount) / 100, abs(amount) % 100)
    }
}

fun sendReceipt(to: Email, order: OrderId, total: Cents) =
    println("receipt for ${order.value} to ${to.value}: $total")

fun main() {
    val email = Email.parseOrNull("  Ada@Example.com ") ?: error("invalid email")
    sendReceipt(email, OrderId("A-1"), Cents(4200) + Cents(550))
    // sendReceipt(OrderId("A-1"), email, Cents(1))   -> does not compile: argument types differ
    println("refund ${Cents(-550)}")
    println(Email.parseOrNull("ada@localhost"))
    println(runCatching { OrderId("42") }.exceptionOrNull()?.message)
}
Result
receipt for A-1 to ada@example.com: 47.50
refund -5.50
null
not an order id: 42

Clean tests: arrange, act, assert

F.I.R.S.T. — fast, independent, repeatable, self-validating, timely: inject the clock, name the test as a sentence, assert one behaviour.

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
import java.time.Clock
import java.time.Instant
import java.time.LocalDate
import java.time.ZoneOffset

class RefundPolicy(private val clock: Clock) {
    fun refundCents(totalCents: Long, shippingCents: Long, deliveredOn: LocalDate): Long {
        val windowEnds = deliveredOn.plusDays(30)
        return if (LocalDate.now(clock) <= windowEnds) totalCents else totalCents - shippingCents
    }
}

class RefundPolicyTest {
    private val clock = Clock.fixed(Instant.parse("2026-11-16T10:00:00Z"), ZoneOffset.UTC)
    private val policy = RefundPolicy(clock)      // a new instance per test: no shared state

    @Test
    fun `refunds the full total inside the 30-day window`() {
        // Arrange
        val deliveredOn = LocalDate.of(2026, 11, 1)
        // Act
        val refund = policy.refundCents(totalCents = 4200, shippingCents = 500, deliveredOn = deliveredOn)
        // Assert
        assertEquals(4200L, refund)
    }

    @Test
    fun `keeps the shipping fee after the window`() {
        val deliveredOn = LocalDate.of(2026, 9, 1)
        val refund = policy.refundCents(totalCents = 4200, shippingCents = 500, deliveredOn = deliveredOn)
        assertEquals(3700L, refund)
    }
}
Result

./gradlew test reports both tests passed, on any day: the clock is fixed.

Setup
  1. A Gradle JVM project with testImplementation(platform("org.junit:junit-bom:5.10.5")), testImplementation("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter") and tasks.test { useJUnitPlatform() }
  2. Put the class under src/test/kotlin and run ./gradlew test

Code smells to name in review

Say the name out loud; it turns taste into an argument.

  • Long function / god class — many reasons to change and no honest name. Extract until each piece has one.
  • Scope-function soup — ?.let { … }.also { … }.apply { … } chains, nested it, a run that hides a return. One scope function per expression, for its documented purpose.
  • !! — a crash with a worse message. Use ?: return, requireNotNull(x) { "why" } or a non-null type.
  • Boolean blindness — two Booleans that encode one state, or a positional render(id, true). Use an enum class or a sealed type, and name the Booleans that remain.
  • Primitive obsession — String ids and Double money. Use value classes and Long cents or BigDecimal.
  • Sentinels and swallowed errors — -1, "", catch (e: Exception) {}. The caller loses the reason.
  • Temporal coupling — a lateinit var that init() must fill before start(). Take it in the constructor.
  • Feature envy / shotgun surgery — a function that mostly reads another type's data; one change that edits ten files.
  • Clean tests — one behaviour per test, a sentence for a name, no sleeps or real clocks, and a test that fails for the right reason before it passes.
  • The boy scout rule — leave each file a little cleaner, in small refactors that keep the tests green.

SOLID in Kotlin

Five principles in Kotlin's own idiom — final-by-default classes, small and functional interfaces, sealed outcomes, class delegation and constructor injection — each before/after proved to print the same.

  • jvm
  • android
  • kotlin >=2.0
  • jvm >=17
  • Kotlin/JVM (the standard library); the same code runs on Android

Sources: Interfaces — Kotlin docs · Functional (SAM) interfaces — Kotlin docs · Delegation — Kotlin docs · Sealed classes and interfaces — Kotlin docs

The one-line versions

Say the name, then the smell it prevents.

  • Single Responsibility — a class has one reason to change: one actor, one kind of change.
  • Open/Closed — add behaviour by adding a type or a value, not by editing a shipped when.
  • Liskov Substitution — any implementation works wherever its supertype is expected, with no is checks and no surprise exceptions.
  • Interface Segregation — clients depend on the slice they use; a one-method fun interface is often the right size.
  • Dependency Inversion — policy declares the interface it needs; the composition root hands it an implementation through the constructor.
  • Kotlin tilts the field: classes are final unless open, by makes composition as cheap as inheritance, and function types are interfaces with no ceremony.

S — Single Responsibility

Smell: one class that parses, prices, persists and formats — four teams' changes collide in one file.

Violates
class OrderManager {
    private val saved = mutableMapOf<String, String>()

    fun handle(line: String): String {
        val parts = line.split(",")                         // parsing
        val id = parts[0].trim()
        val quantity = parts[1].trim().toInt()
        val unitCents = parts[2].trim().toLong()
        val total = quantity * unitCents                    // pricing
        saved[id] = "$quantity x $unitCents"                // persistence
        return "Order $id: ${total / 100}.${(total % 100).toString().padStart(2, '0')}"   // formatting
    }

    fun savedCount() = saved.size
}

fun main() {
    val manager = OrderManager()
    println(manager.handle("A-1, 2, 1250"))
    println(manager.handle("A-2, 1, 999"))
    println("saved ${manager.savedCount()}")
}
Respects
import java.util.Locale

data class Order(val id: String, val quantity: Int, val unitCents: Long) {
    val totalCents: Long get() = quantity * unitCents
}

fun parseOrder(line: String): Order {                       // changes with the file format
    val (id, quantity, unitCents) = line.split(",").map(String::trim)
    return Order(id, quantity.toInt(), unitCents.toLong())
}

interface OrderRepository {                                 // changes with storage
    fun save(order: Order)
    fun count(): Int
}

class InMemoryOrderRepository : OrderRepository {
    private val orders = mutableMapOf<String, Order>()
    override fun save(order: Order) { orders[order.id] = order }
    override fun count() = orders.size
}

fun formatReceipt(order: Order): String =                   // changes with the UI copy
    "Order ${order.id}: %d.%02d".format(Locale.ROOT, order.totalCents / 100, order.totalCents % 100)

class PlaceOrder(private val repository: OrderRepository) {  // a thin coordinator
    fun place(line: String): String {
        val order = parseOrder(line)
        repository.save(order)
        return formatReceipt(order)
    }
}

fun main() {
    val repository = InMemoryOrderRepository()
    val placeOrder = PlaceOrder(repository)
    println(placeOrder.place("A-1, 2, 1250"))
    println(placeOrder.place("A-2, 1, 999"))
    println("saved ${repository.count()}")
}
Result
Order A-1: 25.00
Order A-2: 9.99
saved 2

O — Open/Closed

Open set (promotions) → a `fun interface` and a list of values; closed set (payment states) → a sealed type, where an exhaustive `when` is the better tool.

Violates
data class Order(val subtotalCents: Long, val isStudent: Boolean, val coupon: String?)

fun discountCents(order: Order): Long {
    var discount = 0L
    if (order.isStudent) discount += order.subtotalCents * 10 / 100
    if (order.coupon == "WELCOME5") discount += 500
    // Black Friday: shipped, tested code edited again, and every promotion retested with it
    if (order.coupon == "BLACKFRIDAY") discount += order.subtotalCents * 20 / 100
    return discount.coerceAtMost(order.subtotalCents)
}

fun main() {
    val orders = listOf(
        Order(4000, isStudent = true, coupon = null),
        Order(4000, isStudent = true, coupon = "WELCOME5"),
        Order(300, isStudent = false, coupon = "WELCOME5"),
        Order(5000, isStudent = false, coupon = "BLACKFRIDAY"),
    )
    println(orders.map(::discountCents))
}
Respects
data class Order(val subtotalCents: Long, val isStudent: Boolean, val coupon: String?)

fun interface DiscountRule { fun discountCents(order: Order): Long }

val studentDiscount = DiscountRule { if (it.isStudent) it.subtotalCents * 10 / 100 else 0 }
val welcomeCoupon = DiscountRule { if (it.coupon == "WELCOME5") 500 else 0 }

class Pricing(private val rules: List<DiscountRule>) {       // closed: never edited for a promotion
    fun discountCents(order: Order): Long =
        rules.sumOf { it.discountCents(order) }.coerceAtMost(order.subtotalCents)
}

// Black Friday arrives as a new value; Pricing and the two older rules are untouched.
val blackFriday = DiscountRule { if (it.coupon == "BLACKFRIDAY") it.subtotalCents * 20 / 100 else 0 }

fun main() {
    val pricing = Pricing(listOf(studentDiscount, welcomeCoupon, blackFriday))
    val orders = listOf(
        Order(4000, isStudent = true, coupon = null),
        Order(4000, isStudent = true, coupon = "WELCOME5"),
        Order(300, isStudent = false, coupon = "WELCOME5"),
        Order(5000, isStudent = false, coupon = "BLACKFRIDAY"),
    )
    println(orders.map(pricing::discountCents))
}
Result
[400, 900, 300, 1000]

L — Liskov Substitution

If the caller must ask `is GiftCard`, substitution is broken; put every outcome in the contract as a sealed type instead of throwing.

Violates
open class PaymentMethod {
    open fun refund(cents: Long): String = "refunded $cents to the original method"
}

class Card(private val last4: String) : PaymentMethod() {
    override fun refund(cents: Long) = "refunded $cents to card ending $last4"
}

class GiftCard : PaymentMethod() {
    override fun refund(cents: Long): String =
        throw UnsupportedOperationException("gift cards cannot be refunded")   // breaks the promise
}

fun refundOrder(method: PaymentMethod, cents: Long): String {
    if (method is GiftCard) return "issued $cents as store credit"    // the caller knows the subtype
    return method.refund(cents)
}

fun main() {
    println(refundOrder(Card("4242"), 4250))
    println(refundOrder(GiftCard(), 4250))
}
Respects
sealed interface RefundOutcome {
    data class Returned(val description: String) : RefundOutcome
    data class StoreCredit(val cents: Long) : RefundOutcome
}

// The only change: the contract has a type for every outcome, so no subclass throws.
open class PaymentMethod {
    open fun refund(cents: Long): RefundOutcome =
        RefundOutcome.Returned("refunded $cents to the original method")
}

class Card(private val last4: String) : PaymentMethod() {
    override fun refund(cents: Long) = RefundOutcome.Returned("refunded $cents to card ending $last4")
}

class GiftCard : PaymentMethod() {
    override fun refund(cents: Long) = RefundOutcome.StoreCredit(cents)
}

fun refundOrder(method: PaymentMethod, cents: Long): String = when (val outcome = method.refund(cents)) {
    is RefundOutcome.Returned -> outcome.description
    is RefundOutcome.StoreCredit -> "issued ${outcome.cents} as store credit"
}

fun main() {
    println(refundOrder(Card("4242"), 4250))
    println(refundOrder(GiftCard(), 4250))
}
Result
refunded 4250 to card ending 4242
issued 4250 as store credit

I — Interface Segregation

Smell: fakes full of `TODO()`; a screen that reads one order should depend on a one-method `fun interface`, which a lambda can satisfy.

Violates
interface OrderStore {
    fun orderById(id: String): String?
    fun save(id: String, summary: String)
    fun deleteAll()
    fun exportCsv(): String
}

class ReceiptScreen(private val store: OrderStore) {
    fun title(id: String): String = store.orderById(id)?.let { "Receipt: $it" } ?: "Order not found"
}

class FakeStore : OrderStore {                            // a test fake must stub everything
    override fun orderById(id: String) = if (id == "A-1") "2 mugs" else null
    override fun save(id: String, summary: String) = TODO("not needed")
    override fun deleteAll() = TODO("not needed")
    override fun exportCsv() = TODO("not needed")
}

fun main() {
    val screen = ReceiptScreen(FakeStore())
    println(screen.title("A-1"))
    println(screen.title("Z-9"))
}
Respects
fun interface OrderLookup { fun orderById(id: String): String? }

interface OrderWriter {
    fun save(id: String, summary: String)
    fun saveAll(orders: Map<String, String>) {                // a default method: implementers get it free
        orders.forEach { (id, summary) -> save(id, summary) }
    }
}

class OrderDatabase : OrderLookup, OrderWriter {          // the real store implements both slices
    private val rows = mutableMapOf<String, String>()
    override fun orderById(id: String) = rows[id]
    override fun save(id: String, summary: String) { rows[id] = summary }
}

class ReceiptScreen(private val orders: OrderLookup) {     // asks for the slice it uses
    fun title(id: String): String = orders.orderById(id)?.let { "Receipt: $it" } ?: "Order not found"
}

fun main() {
    val database = OrderDatabase().apply { saveAll(mapOf("A-1" to "2 mugs")) }
    val screen = ReceiptScreen(database)
    println(screen.title("A-1"))
    println(ReceiptScreen { null }.title("Z-9"))           // a one-lambda fake in a test
}
Result
Receipt: 2 mugs
Order not found

D — Dependency Inversion

Smell: a concrete SDK client or a singleton `object` created inside the logic; invert it with constructor injection and wire it once.

Violates
class StripeGateway {
    fun charge(orderId: String, cents: Long): String = "ch_$orderId"   // stands in for a network call
}

object Analytics {
    fun track(event: String) = println("track: $event")
}

class CheckoutService {
    private val gateway = StripeGateway()                // hard-wired: every test charges a card
    fun pay(orderId: String, cents: Long): String {
        val chargeId = gateway.charge(orderId, cents)
        Analytics.track("paid $orderId")
        return chargeId
    }
}

fun main() {
    println(CheckoutService().pay("A-1", 4250))
}
Respects
fun interface PaymentGateway {                           // declared by checkout, the policy
    fun charge(orderId: String, cents: Long): String
}

class StripeGateway : PaymentGateway {                   // a detail that depends on the policy's interface
    override fun charge(orderId: String, cents: Long) = "ch_$orderId"
}

class CheckoutService(
    private val gateway: PaymentGateway,
    private val track: (event: String) -> Unit,          // a function type is the smallest interface
) {
    fun pay(orderId: String, cents: Long): String {
        val chargeId = gateway.charge(orderId, cents)
        track("paid $orderId")
        return chargeId
    }
}

fun main() {
    // The composition root: the only place that names concrete types.
    val checkout = CheckoutService(StripeGateway()) { event -> println("track: $event") }
    println(checkout.pay("A-1", 4250))
    // In a test: CheckoutService({ id, _ -> "ch_test_$id" }, recordedEvents::add)
}
Result
track: paid A-1
ch_A-1

Composition over inheritance, with `by`

Overriding a collection couples you to its internals; class delegation forwards everything to a wrapped instance and overrides only what you change.

// Recently viewed product ids, counting every add for analytics.

class InheritedViews : HashSet<String>() {             // inheritance: depends on HashSet's internals
    var adds = 0
    override fun add(element: String): Boolean {
        adds++
        return super.add(element)
    }
    override fun addAll(elements: Collection<String>): Boolean {
        adds += elements.size
        return super.addAll(elements)                  // HashSet.addAll calls add(): counted twice
    }
}

class DelegatedViews(
    private val ids: MutableSet<String> = HashSet(),
) : MutableSet<String> by ids {                        // every other member is forwarded to ids
    var adds = 0
    override fun add(element: String): Boolean {
        adds++
        return ids.add(element)
    }
    override fun addAll(elements: Collection<String>): Boolean {
        adds += elements.size
        return ids.addAll(elements)                    // ids.add is not ours: counted once
    }
}

fun main() {
    val viewed = listOf("mug", "lamp", "desk")
    val inherited = InheritedViews().apply { addAll(viewed) }
    val delegated = DelegatedViews().apply { addAll(viewed) }
    println("inheritance counted ${inherited.adds}, delegation counted ${delegated.adds}")
    println(delegated.size)
}
Result
inheritance counted 6, delegation counted 3
3

Related principles an interviewer may also ask

Name the principle, then the trade-off.

  • DRY — one source for each piece of knowledge; but two similar-looking whens that change for different reasons are not duplication. Prefer duplication over the wrong abstraction.
  • KISS — a top-level function beats a class with one method; a data class beats a hierarchy.
  • YAGNI — no interface until there is a second implementation or a test that needs a fake.
  • Composition over inheritance — Kotlin makes it the default: final classes, by delegation, and interfaces with default methods instead of abstract base classes.
  • Law of Demeter — order.customer.address.city couples you to three types; ask order.shippingCity — a member that hides the structure, or at least an extension that keeps the chain in one place.
  • Tell, don't ask — cart.applyCoupon(code) rather than reading cart.items and deciding outside.
  • Applying SOLID to a 50-line script: interfaces with one implementation and factories for data classes are the cost, not the benefit.
  • Android angle: a ViewModel (SRP for screen state) takes a repository interface (DIP) through its constructor, and a sealed UiState makes the screen's when exhaustive — the closed-set alternative to OCP.

Functional Programming in Kotlin

Pure functions, immutable values and functions as data — the collection operators, function types and references, nullable and Result containers, sealed types, Sequence, tailrec and inline — every example run.

  • jvm
  • android
  • kotlin >=2.0
  • jvm >=17
  • Kotlin/JVM (the standard library); the same code runs on Android

Sources: Higher-order functions and lambdas — Kotlin docs · Collection operations overview — Kotlin docs · Sequences — Kotlin docs · Inline functions — Kotlin docs · Functions (tail recursive functions) — Kotlin docs

Core ideas

The vocabulary, and where Kotlin gives it to you.

  • Pure function — same input, same output, no observable side effects. Trivially testable and safe to call from any coroutine.
  • Immutability — val by default, read-only List/Map in signatures, and change as a new value with copy(...).
  • Functions are values — function types (Order) -> Boolean, lambdas, and references ::isRefundable, Order::id.
  • Expressions over statements — if, when and try return values, so most vars disappear.
  • Algebraic data types — data class is AND (a product), a sealed interface is OR (a sum). Make illegal states unrepresentable.
  • Kotlin is multi-paradigm: use FP where it clarifies (transforms, pipelines, state), and a plain loop where it reads better.

Imperative → declarative

Say what you want — filter, transform, aggregate — and let the operator names carry the meaning.

Imperative
data class Order(val id: String, val customer: String, val totalCents: Long, val delivered: Boolean)

val orders = listOf(
    Order("A-1", "ada", 4200, delivered = true),
    Order("A-2", "linus", 1500, delivered = false),
    Order("A-3", "ada", 9900, delivered = true),
    Order("A-4", "grace", 2500, delivered = true),
)

fun main() {
    val customers = mutableListOf<String>()
    for (order in orders) {
        if (order.delivered && order.totalCents >= 2000) {
            val name = order.customer.uppercase()
            if (name !in customers) customers.add(name)
        }
    }
    customers.sort()

    var revenue = 0L
    for (order in orders) if (order.delivered) revenue += order.totalCents

    val totals = mutableMapOf<String, Long>()
    for (order in orders) totals[order.customer] = (totals[order.customer] ?: 0L) + order.totalCents

    println(customers)
    println(revenue)
    println(totals)
}
Declarative
data class Order(val id: String, val customer: String, val totalCents: Long, val delivered: Boolean)

val orders = listOf(
    Order("A-1", "ada", 4200, delivered = true),
    Order("A-2", "linus", 1500, delivered = false),
    Order("A-3", "ada", 9900, delivered = true),
    Order("A-4", "grace", 2500, delivered = true),
)

fun main() {
    val customers = orders
        .filter { it.delivered && it.totalCents >= 2000 }
        .map { it.customer.uppercase() }
        .distinct()
        .sorted()

    val revenue = orders.filter(Order::delivered).sumOf { it.totalCents }

    val totals = orders
        .groupBy(Order::customer)                     // keeps first-seen key order
        .mapValues { (_, ordersOfCustomer) -> ordersOfCustomer.sumOf { it.totalCents } }

    println(customers)
    println(revenue)
    println(totals)
}
Result
[ADA, GRACE]
16600
{ada=14100, linus=1500, grace=2500}

Higher-order functions to know cold

All are on `Iterable` and most on `Sequence`; the streaming ones (`map`, `filter`, `fold`, `zip`, `runningFold`) also exist on `Flow`.

FunctionWhat it doesExample
map / mapNotNulltransform; drop the nullsraw.mapNotNull { it.toIntOrNull() }
filter / filterNot / filterIsInstance<T>()keep matches; keep a subtypeevents.filterIsInstance<Purchased>()
flatMap / flattenmap to lists, then join themorders.flatMap { it.lines }
fold / reduceaccumulate; reduce throws on emptylines.fold(0L) { acc, l -> acc + l.cents }
sumOf / maxByOrNull / minOfaggregate by a selectororders.maxByOrNull { it.totalCents }
groupBy / associateBy / associateWithto a Map of lists / of one valueusers.associateBy { it.id }
partitionsplit by a predicate into a Pairval (paid, unpaid) = orders.partition { it.isPaid }
zip / zipWithNextpair two lists; pair neighboursprices.zipWithNext { a, b -> b - a }
chunked / windowedbatches; sliding windowsids.chunked(50) for a batch API
any / all / none / countpredicates over the wholecart.items.all { it.inStock }
firstOrNull / singleOrNullfind without throwingusers.firstOrNull { it.email == email }
sortedWith(compareBy(...))multi-key ordersortedWith(compareBy({ it.country }, { -it.totalCents }))
runningFold / scanevery intermediate accumulatordeposits.runningFold(0L) { b, d -> b + d }

Function types, references, composition and partial application

Store and combine behaviour as values, and partially apply with a plain lambda — it reads better in Kotlin than a curried chain.

data class Order(val id: String, val totalCents: Long, val country: String)

// A function type is a value: store it, pass it, return it.
val isLarge: (Order) -> Boolean = { it.totalCents >= 10_000 }

fun isDomestic(order: Order): Boolean = order.country == "FR"

// Composition: a new function from two existing ones.
infix fun <A, B, C> ((A) -> B).andThen(next: (B) -> C): (A) -> C = { next(this(it)) }

// Partial application: fix the rate now, supply the amount later.
val addTax: (percent: Int, cents: Long) -> Long = { percent, cents -> cents + cents * percent / 100 }
val withFrenchVat: (Long) -> Long = { cents -> addTax(20, cents) }

fun main() {
    val orders = listOf(Order("A-1", 12_000, "FR"), Order("A-2", 4_000, "DE"), Order("A-3", 15_000, "DE"))
    println(orders.filter(isLarge).map(Order::id))
    println(orders.filter(::isDomestic).map(Order::id))        // function and property references

    val grossTotal = Order::totalCents andThen withFrenchVat
    println(orders.filter(isLarge).map(grossTotal))
}
Result
[A-1, A-3]
[A-1]
[14400, 18000]

Lambdas with receivers and type-safe builders

A `T.() -> Unit` parameter makes `this` the builder inside the block, which is how `buildString`, `apply`, Compose modifiers and the Gradle Kotlin DSL read like configuration.

import java.util.Locale

@DslMarker
annotation class ReceiptDsl                                 // stops nested blocks reaching outer receivers

@ReceiptDsl
class ReceiptBuilder {
    private val lines = mutableListOf<Pair<String, Long>>()
    var footer: String = ""

    fun line(item: String, cents: Long) {
        lines += item to cents
    }

    fun build(): String = buildString {                     // a StringBuilder.() -> Unit block
        lines.forEach { (item, cents) -> appendLine(item.padEnd(8) + formatCents(cents)) }
        appendLine("TOTAL".padEnd(8) + formatCents(lines.sumOf { it.second }))
        if (footer.isNotEmpty()) append(footer)
    }
}

fun formatCents(cents: Long): String = "%d.%02d".format(Locale.ROOT, cents / 100, cents % 100)

fun receipt(block: ReceiptBuilder.() -> Unit): String = ReceiptBuilder().apply(block).build()

fun main() {
    val text = receipt {
        line("mug", 1200)                                   // this.line(...): this is the builder
        line("lamp", 9900)
        footer = "Thank you!"
    }
    println(text)
}
Result
mug     12.00
lamp    99.00
TOTAL   111.00
Thank you!

Nullable, Result and a sealed Either as containers

`?.` is `map`, `?.let` is `flatMap`, `?:` is `getOrElse`; `Result` holds a caught exception; a sealed `Either` holds a domain error.

data class Customer(val id: String, val email: String?)

val customers = mapOf("c1" to Customer("c1", "ada@example.com"), "c2" to Customer("c2", null))

fun emailDomain(customerId: String): String =
    customers[customerId]?.email?.substringAfter('@') ?: "no email"

fun parseCents(raw: String): Result<Long> =
    runCatching { (raw.toBigDecimal() * 100.toBigDecimal()).longValueExact() }

sealed interface Either<out E, out A> {
    data class Left<E>(val error: E) : Either<E, Nothing>
    data class Right<A>(val value: A) : Either<Nothing, A>
}

inline fun <E, A, B> Either<E, A>.map(transform: (A) -> B): Either<E, B> = when (this) {
    is Either.Left -> this
    is Either.Right -> Either.Right(transform(value))
}

fun validateQuantity(quantity: Int): Either<String, Int> =
    if (quantity in 1..10) Either.Right(quantity) else Either.Left("quantity must be 1-10")

fun main() {
    println(listOf("c1", "c2", "c9").map(::emailDomain))
    for (raw in listOf("12.50", "12,50")) {
        val message = parseCents(raw)
            .map { it + 499 }                                    // add shipping only on success
            .fold(onSuccess = { "total $it cents" }, onFailure = { "invalid price: ${it::class.simpleName}" })
        println(message)
    }
    println(validateQuantity(3).map { it * 1250 })
    println(validateQuantity(0).map { it * 1250 })
}
Result
[example.com, no email, no email]
total 1749 cents
invalid price: NumberFormatException
Right(value=3750)
Left(error=quantity must be 1-10)
