ConstraintLayout with a ConstraintSet in code

Every child needs an id; `clone` the layout, `connect` sides, set sizes with `constrainWidth`/`constrainHeight`, then `applyTo`.

class OrderRowView(context: Context) : ConstraintLayout(context) {
    val customer = TextView(context).apply {
        id = View.generateViewId()
        maxLines = 1
        ellipsize = TextUtils.TruncateAt.END
    }
    val details = TextView(context).apply { id = View.generateViewId() }
    val total = TextView(context).apply { id = View.generateViewId() }

    init {
        val gap = (16 * resources.displayMetrics.density).roundToInt()
        setPadding(gap, gap / 2, gap, gap / 2)
        addView(customer)
        addView(details)
        addView(total)
        ConstraintSet().apply {
            clone(this@OrderRowView)                     // start from the children just added
            constrainWidth(customer.id, ConstraintSet.MATCH_CONSTRAINT)   // 0dp: stretch between constraints
            constrainHeight(customer.id, ConstraintSet.WRAP_CONTENT)
            connect(customer.id, ConstraintSet.TOP, ConstraintSet.PARENT_ID, ConstraintSet.TOP)
            connect(customer.id, ConstraintSet.START, ConstraintSet.PARENT_ID, ConstraintSet.START)
            connect(customer.id, ConstraintSet.END, total.id, ConstraintSet.START, gap)

            constrainWidth(details.id, ConstraintSet.MATCH_CONSTRAINT)
            constrainHeight(details.id, ConstraintSet.WRAP_CONTENT)
            connect(details.id, ConstraintSet.TOP, customer.id, ConstraintSet.BOTTOM)
            connect(details.id, ConstraintSet.START, customer.id, ConstraintSet.START)
            connect(details.id, ConstraintSet.END, total.id, ConstraintSet.START, gap)

            constrainWidth(total.id, ConstraintSet.WRAP_CONTENT)
            constrainHeight(total.id, ConstraintSet.WRAP_CONTENT)
            connect(total.id, ConstraintSet.END, ConstraintSet.PARENT_ID, ConstraintSet.END)
            centerVertically(total.id, ConstraintSet.PARENT_ID)
        }.applyTo(this)
    }
}
Result

The customer name at the top start and the order details under it, both stopping before the total, which is centred vertically at the end.

  2. Used as the row view of OrdersAdapter in the RecyclerView card

RecyclerView with ListAdapter, DiffUtil and view holders

`submitList` diffs on a background thread and dispatches the minimal `notifyItem…` calls; the view holder caches the row's views.

class OrdersAdapter(private val onOpen: (String) -> Unit) :
    ListAdapter<Order, OrdersAdapter.OrderViewHolder>(OrderDiff) {

    class OrderViewHolder(val row: OrderRowView) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(row)

    private val money = NumberFormat.getCurrencyInstance().apply {   // the user's locale, our currency
        currency = Currency.getInstance("USD")
    }

    override fun onCreateViewHolder(parent: ViewGroup, viewType: Int): OrderViewHolder {
        val row = OrderRowView(parent.context).apply {
            layoutParams = RecyclerView.LayoutParams(MATCH_PARENT, WRAP_CONTENT)
        }
        val holder = OrderViewHolder(row)
        row.setOnClickListener {                       // once per holder, not on every bind
            val position = holder.bindingAdapterPosition
            if (position != RecyclerView.NO_POSITION) onOpen(getItem(position).id)
        }
        return holder
    }

    override fun onBindViewHolder(holder: OrderViewHolder, position: Int) {
        val order = getItem(position)
        holder.row.customer.text = order.customer
        holder.row.details.text = "#${order.id} · ${order.status}"
        holder.row.total.text = money.format(order.totalCents / 100.0)
    }

    object OrderDiff : DiffUtil.ItemCallback<Order>() {
        override fun areItemsTheSame(oldItem: Order, newItem: Order) = oldItem.id == newItem.id   // same row?
        override fun areContentsTheSame(oldItem: Order, newItem: Order) = oldItem == newItem   // redraw it?
    }
}
Result

Submitting a new list animates only the inserted, removed, moved and changed rows; rows scrolled off screen are recycled instead of re-created.

The same row with XML and View Binding

For comparison — layouts stay in XML, and the generated binding gives typed, null-safe references instead of `findViewById`.

// item_order.xml generates ItemOrderBinding: order_details → binding.orderDetails, typed as TextView
class XmlOrdersAdapter(private val onOpen: (String) -> Unit) :
    ListAdapter<Order, XmlOrdersAdapter.OrderViewHolder>(OrdersAdapter.OrderDiff) {   // the same DiffUtil

    class OrderViewHolder(val binding: ItemOrderBinding) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(binding.root)

    private val money = NumberFormat.getCurrencyInstance().apply { currency = Currency.getInstance("USD") }

    override fun onCreateViewHolder(parent: ViewGroup, viewType: Int): OrderViewHolder {
        val binding = ItemOrderBinding.inflate(LayoutInflater.from(parent.context), parent, false)
        val holder = OrderViewHolder(binding)
        binding.root.setOnClickListener {                // once per holder, not on every bind
            val position = holder.bindingAdapterPosition
            if (position != RecyclerView.NO_POSITION) onOpen(getItem(position).id)
        }
        return holder
    }

    override fun onBindViewHolder(holder: OrderViewHolder, position: Int) {
        val order = getItem(position)
        with(holder.binding) {
            customer.text = order.customer
            orderDetails.text = "#${order.id} · ${order.status}"
            total.text = money.format(order.totalCents / 100.0)
        }
    }
}

class OrdersFragment : Fragment(R.layout.fragment_orders) {
    private var _binding: FragmentOrdersBinding? = null
    private val binding get() = _binding!!              // valid only between onViewCreated and onDestroyView

    override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
        _binding = FragmentOrdersBinding.bind(view)      // the layout is already inflated: bind, not inflate
        binding.list.adapter = XmlOrdersAdapter(onOpen = { id ->
            findNavController().navigate(OrderDetail(id))
        })
    }

    override fun onDestroyView() {
        super.onDestroyView()
        _binding = null                                  // the fragment outlives its views
    }
}

The same row and list as the code-only version, with layout in XML; a wrong id or type fails the build instead of crashing at run time.

One StateFlow, rendered by hand — the logic runs on the JVM

The ViewModel's logic without Android, and a renderer that touches only the views whose data changed — what the screen's collector calls.

import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking
import kotlinx.coroutines.yield

data class Order(val id: String, val customer: String)

data class OrdersUiState(
    val query: String = "",
    val visible: List<Order> = emptyList(),
    val loading: Boolean = false,
)

class OrdersStateHolder(private val all: List<Order>) {          // a ViewModel's body, minus Android
    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(OrdersUiState(visible = all))
    val state: StateFlow<OrdersUiState> = _state.asStateFlow()

    fun onQueryChange(query: String) = _state.update { current ->
        current.copy(query = query, visible = all.filter { it.customer.contains(query, ignoreCase = true) })
    }
}

class OrdersRenderer {                                           // what render(state) does with real views
    private var last: OrdersUiState? = null
    fun render(state: OrdersUiState) {
        if (state.visible != last?.visible) println("adapter.submitList(${state.visible.map { it.id }})")
        if (state.loading != last?.loading) println("progress.isVisible = ${state.loading}")
        last = state
    }
}

fun main() = runBlocking {
    val orders = listOf(Order("1041", "Ada"), Order("1042", "Grace"), Order("1043", "Adele"))
    val holder = OrdersStateHolder(orders)
    val renderer = OrdersRenderer()
    val collector = launch { holder.state.collect(renderer::render) }   // the repeatOnLifecycle body
    yield()
    holder.onQueryChange("ad")
    yield()
    holder.onQueryChange("AD")              // new query, same rows: nothing to touch
    yield()
    holder.onQueryChange("gr")
    yield()
    collector.cancel()                       // what onStop does to a STARTED collector
}
Result
adapter.submitList([1041, 1042, 1043])
progress.isVisible = false
adapter.submitList([1041, 1043])
adapter.submitList([1042])

Collecting the state in a Fragment with repeatOnLifecycle

Collect with the view's lifecycle, only while `STARTED`; one `launch` per flow inside the block.

class OrdersFragment : Fragment() {
    private val viewModel: OrdersViewModel by viewModels()

    override fun onCreateView(inflater: LayoutInflater, container: ViewGroup?, saved: Bundle?): View =
        OrdersScreenView(requireContext())

    override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
        val screen = view as OrdersScreenView
        val adapter = OrdersAdapter(onOpen = ::openOrder)
        screen.list.adapter = adapter
        screen.search.doAfterTextChanged { viewModel.onQueryChange(it?.toString().orEmpty()) }

        viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope.launch {
            viewLifecycleOwner.repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {   // cancelled at each onStop
                launch { viewModel.state.collect { state -> render(screen, adapter, state) } }
                launch {
                    viewModel.messages.collect { message ->
                        Snackbar.make(screen, message, Snackbar.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private fun render(screen: OrdersScreenView, adapter: OrdersAdapter, state: OrdersUiState) {
        adapter.submitList(state.visible)                       // DiffUtil finds the minimal change
        screen.progress.isVisible = state.loading
        screen.empty.isVisible = !state.loading && state.visible.isEmpty()
        if (screen.search.text.toString() != state.query) {    // avoid a loop with the text listener
            screen.search.setText(state.query)
        }
    }

    private fun openOrder(id: String) = findNavController().navigate(OrderDetail(orderId = id))
}
Result

The list, spinner and empty state follow every new state while the screen is visible; nothing is collected while it is stopped, and collection ends with the view, not the fragment.

Moving between screens — Navigation component or a FragmentManager transaction

Navigation 2.8+ builds the Fragment graph from the same `@Serializable` routes as Navigation Compose; a plain transaction is the no-library fallback.

@Serializable data object Orders

@Serializable data class OrderDetail(val orderId: String)

class MainActivity : AppCompatActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        setContentView(R.layout.activity_main)
        val navHost = supportFragmentManager.findFragmentById(R.id.nav_host) as NavHostFragment
        val navController = navHost.navController
        navController.graph = navController.createGraph(startDestination = Orders) {
            fragment<OrdersFragment, Orders> { label = "Orders" }
            fragment<OrderDetailFragment, OrderDetail> { label = "Order" }
        }
    }
}

class OrdersFragment : Fragment() {
    private fun openOrder(id: String) = findNavController().navigate(OrderDetail(orderId = id))
}

// OrderDetailFragment's ViewModel: the typed argument, no Bundle keys
class OrderDetailViewModel(handle: SavedStateHandle) : ViewModel() {
    val orderId: String = handle.toRoute<OrderDetail>().orderId
}

// Without Navigation: replace the fragment in a container and keep Back working
fun AppCompatActivity.showOrderDetail(id: String) {
    supportFragmentManager.commit {
        setReorderingAllowed(true)
        replace<OrderDetailFragment>(R.id.container, args = Bundle().apply { putString("orderId", id) })
        addToBackStack("order")
    }
}
Result

Tapping an order shows its detail screen with the id as a typed argument, and the system Back gesture returns to the list in both versions.

Setup
  1. androidx.navigation:navigation-fragment-ktx 2.8 or later and the org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.serialization Gradle plugin
  2. res/layout/activity_main.xml holding a FragmentContainerView with id nav_host and android:name="androidx.navigation.fragment.NavHostFragment"

A custom view in brief — onMeasure and onDraw

Ask for a size in `onMeasure` (always ending in `setMeasuredDimension`), draw with `Paint` objects allocated once, and `invalidate()` when only the pixels change.

class OrderProgressView(context: Context, attrs: AttributeSet? = null) : View(context, attrs) {
    var step: Int = 0
        set(value) {
            field = value.coerceIn(0, STEPS - 1)
            contentDescription = "Step ${field + 1} of $STEPS"     // TalkBack reads this, not the circles
            invalidate()                                          // same size: redraw only, no requestLayout
        }

    private val density = resources.displayMetrics.density
    private val radius = 6 * density
    private val done = Paint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG).apply {        // allocated once, never in onDraw
        color = MaterialColors.getColor(this@OrderProgressView, androidx.appcompat.R.attr.colorPrimary)
        strokeWidth = 2 * density
    }
    private val outline = MaterialColors.getColor(this, com.google.android.material.R.attr.colorOutline)
    private val todo = Paint(done).apply { color = outline }

    init { step = 0 }                                   // run the setter once: described from the start

    override fun onMeasure(widthMeasureSpec: Int, heightMeasureSpec: Int) {
        val dots = STEPS * 2 * radius + (STEPS - 1) * 24 * density   // four dots, 24 dp apart
        val wantedWidth = dots.roundToInt() + paddingStart + paddingEnd
        setMeasuredDimension(
            View.resolveSize(wantedWidth, widthMeasureSpec),   // exact width wins; wrap_content gets ours
            View.resolveSize((2 * radius).roundToInt() + paddingTop + paddingBottom, heightMeasureSpec),
        )
    }

    override fun onDraw(canvas: Canvas) {
        val cy = paddingTop + radius
        val gap = (width - paddingStart - paddingEnd - 2 * radius) / (STEPS - 1)
        val mirror = if (layoutDirection == LAYOUT_DIRECTION_RTL) -1f else 1f   // RTL: step 1 on the right
        canvas.withScale(x = mirror, pivotX = width / 2f) {
            for (i in 0 until STEPS) {
                val cx = paddingStart + radius + i * gap
                val paint = if (i <= step) done else todo
                if (i > 0) drawLine(cx - gap, cy, cx, cy, paint)
                drawCircle(cx, cy, radius, paint)
            }
        }
    }

    companion object { const val STEPS = 4 }
}
Result

Four dots joined by a line — about 120 dp wide under wrap_content, stretched under an exact width — filled in the primary colour up to the current step and in the outline colour after it, mirrored in right-to-left layouts.

Setup
  1. The project above, with Material Components 1.12+ for MaterialColors and a Material 3 app theme; colorPrimary is AppCompat's attribute (Material 1.13+ no longer re-declares it in its non-transitive R)
  2. Add it like any view: OrderProgressView(context).also { it.step = 2 }; it sizes itself under wrap_content

The traps

Most View-system bugs in review are one of these.

  • Holding an Activity, a View or a binding in a ViewModel, a singleton or a long-lived callback: after a rotation it pins the whole old view tree in memory. Pass ids and data, or the application context.
  • Keeping a Fragment's binding after onDestroyView: the back stack keeps the fragment but destroys its views. Null the binding (and adapters that reference views) there.
  • lifecycleScope.launch { flow.collect { } } in a Fragment: it follows the fragment, not its view, and keeps collecting while stopped. Use viewLifecycleOwner.repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED).
  • launchWhenStarted and friends (deprecated since lifecycle 2.6) suspend instead of cancelling, so upstream flows keep working in the background — use repeatOnLifecycle.
  • Network, disk or JSON parsing on the main thread: dropped frames, and an ANR after about 5 seconds. Move it behind withContext(Dispatchers.IO) in the repository.
  • notifyDataSetChanged() after every change rebinds every row and loses animations: submitList with a DiffUtil.ItemCallback.
  • Ignoring window insets: from target SDK 35 the app is edge-to-edge on Android 15+, so the first and last views slide under the status and navigation bars. Pad with ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener, and give scrolling lists clipToPadding = false.
  • Views that hold user input need a stable resource id (not View.generateViewId()) for their state to be restored after recreation.
  • Set click listeners in onCreateViewHolder and read bindingAdapterPosition when clicked; the position captured at bind time goes stale.
  • Need a measured size? doOnLayout { } (androidx.core) runs now if the view is already laid out, otherwise after the next layout; doOnNextLayout always waits.

Translate any View-system answer into Compose and back — the concept map, one screen both ways, interop in both directions, themes and state across the boundary, and a migration plan.

A list screen, both ways

Same `OrdersViewModel`, same `StateFlow`, same routes — only the UI layer differs.

Views (Fragment + RecyclerView)
class OrdersFragment : Fragment() {
    private val viewModel: OrdersViewModel by viewModels()

    override fun onCreateView(inflater: LayoutInflater, container: ViewGroup?, saved: Bundle?): View =
        RecyclerView(requireContext()).apply {
            layoutManager = LinearLayoutManager(context)
            clipToPadding = false                           // rows scroll under the navigation bar
            ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener(this) { list, insets ->
                val bars = insets.getInsets(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars())   // all sides
                list.updatePadding(left = bars.left, right = bars.right, bottom = bars.bottom)
                insets
            }
        }

    override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
        val adapter = OrdersAdapter(onOpen = { id -> findNavController().navigate(OrderDetail(id)) })
        (view as RecyclerView).adapter = adapter
        viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope.launch {
            viewLifecycleOwner.repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) {
                viewModel.state.collect { adapter.submitList(it.visible) }
            }
        }
    }
}
// plus OrdersAdapter, its ViewHolder and DiffUtil.ItemCallback: about 40 more lines
Compose (screen composable)
@Composable
fun OrdersScreen(onOpen: (String) -> Unit, viewModel: OrdersViewModel = viewModel()) {
    val state by viewModel.state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
    LazyColumn(contentPadding = WindowInsets.navigationBars.asPaddingValues()) {   // last row clears the bar
        items(state.visible, key = { it.id }) { order ->
            OrderRow(order, onClick = { onOpen(order.id) })
        }
    }
}

// In the NavHost:
// composable<Orders> { OrdersScreen(onOpen = { navController.navigate(OrderDetail(it)) }) }
Result

Both show the visible orders with the last row clear of the navigation bar, update only the rows that changed, stop collecting while the screen is stopped, and open the detail screen on tap.

Setup
  1. Views: OrdersAdapter (a ListAdapter with a DiffUtil.ItemCallback) and Navigation 2.8+ with the OrderDetail route; Compose: the Compose BOM, lifecycle-viewmodel-compose, lifecycle-runtime-compose and an OrderRow composable
  2. An OrdersViewModel exposing state: StateFlow<OrdersUiState> with a visible: List<Order>

The contract both toolkits share — state, actions and stable ids

Keep the reducer and the ids when you migrate: `DiffUtil` and a keyed `LazyColumn` work out the same changes from them.

enum class Status { Pending, Shipped }

data class Order(val id: String, val customer: String, val status: Status)

data class OrdersUiState(val query: String = "", val orders: List<Order> = emptyList()) {
    val visible: List<Order> get() = orders.filter { it.customer.contains(query, ignoreCase = true) }
}

sealed interface OrdersAction {
    data class Loaded(val orders: List<Order>) : OrdersAction
    data class StatusChanged(val id: String, val status: Status) : OrdersAction
    data class QueryChanged(val query: String) : OrdersAction
}

fun reduce(state: OrdersUiState, action: OrdersAction): OrdersUiState = when (action) {
    is OrdersAction.Loaded -> state.copy(orders = action.orders)
    is OrdersAction.StatusChanged -> state.copy(
        orders = state.orders.map { if (it.id == action.id) it.copy(status = action.status) else it },
    )
    is OrdersAction.QueryChanged -> state.copy(query = action.query)
}

/** What areItemsTheSame (same id) and areContentsTheSame (equal) — or a keyed LazyColumn — conclude. */
fun changes(old: List<Order>, new: List<Order>): String {
    val before = old.associateBy { it.id }
    val inserted = new.filter { it.id !in before }.map { it.id }
    val removed = old.map { it.id } - new.map { it.id }.toSet()
    val changed = new.filter { order -> before[order.id]?.let { it != order } == true }.map { it.id }
    return "inserted=$inserted removed=$removed changed=$changed"
}

fun main() {
    val orders = listOf(Order("1041", "Ada", Status.Pending), Order("1042", "Grace", Status.Pending),
        Order("1043", "Adele", Status.Shipped))
    var state = OrdersUiState()
    listOf(
        OrdersAction.Loaded(orders),
        OrdersAction.StatusChanged("1042", Status.Shipped),
        OrdersAction.QueryChanged("ad"),
    ).forEach { action ->
        val next = reduce(state, action)
        println("${action::class.simpleName}: ${changes(state.visible, next.visible)}")
        state = next
    }
}
Result
Loaded: inserted=[1041, 1042, 1043] removed=[] changed=[]
StatusChanged: inserted=[] removed=[] changed=[1042]
QueryChanged: inserted=[] removed=[1042] changed=[]
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc) and JDK 17 or later
  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar

A View inside Compose — AndroidView

`factory` creates the View once; `update` pushes Compose state into it after each recomposition that changed what it reads; `onReset` enables reuse in lazy lists.

@Composable
fun OrderProgress(step: Int, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    AndroidView(
        factory = { context -> OrderProgressView(context) },  // once: build the View here, never in remember
        modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
        update = { view ->
            view.step = step                                   // Compose → View
            view.setOnClickListener { onClick() }              // View → Compose, with the latest lambda
        },
    )
}

@Composable
fun ShipmentList(orders: List<Order>) {
    LazyColumn {
        items(orders, key = { it.id }) { order ->
            AndroidView(
                factory = { context -> OrderProgressView(context) },
                modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(16.dp),
                onReset = { view -> view.step = 0 },          // non-null: the View is reused for another row
                onRelease = { view -> view.setOnClickListener(null) },
                update = { view -> view.step = order.step },
            )
        }
    }
}
Result

The legacy progress view renders inside the composable, follows step as it changes, and in the list its instances are reused as rows scroll instead of being re-created.

Setup
  1. A project with both the View system and the Compose BOM; OrderProgressView is a custom View with a step property (see kt-android-views), and Order carries id and step
  2. Call the composables from setContent { } or a ComposeView

An XML layout or a Fragment inside Compose

`AndroidViewBinding` (ui-viewbinding) inflates a legacy layout; `AndroidFragment` (fragment-compose 1.8+) hosts a Fragment you cannot rewrite yet.

@Composable
fun LegacyOrderSummary(order: Order, total: String, onTrack: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    AndroidViewBinding(OrderSummaryBinding::inflate, modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
        // `this` is the binding; the block runs again when the composable recomposes with new values
        customer.text = order.customer
        this.total.text = total
        trackButton.setOnClickListener { onTrack() }
    }
}

@Composable
fun TrackingSection(order: Order) {
    Column {
        Text("Live tracking", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
        AndroidFragment<CarrierMapFragment>(
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().height(240.dp),
            arguments = Bundle().apply { putString("orderId", order.id) },   // requireArguments() in it
        )
    }
}
Result

The XML summary and the map fragment appear inside the Compose screen; the fragment is removed when TrackingSection leaves the composition.

Setup
  1. implementation("androidx.compose.ui:ui-viewbinding"), implementation("androidx.fragment:fragment-compose:1.8.0") or later, and buildFeatures { viewBinding = true }
  2. res/layout/order_summary.xml with views customer, total and track_button; an existing CarrierMapFragment

Compose inside Views — ComposeView and the right ViewCompositionStrategy

In a Fragment, dispose with the view's lifecycle (`DisposeOnViewTreeLifecycleDestroyed`); in an Activity or a RecyclerView row the default is right.

class OrderDetailFragment : Fragment() {
    override fun onCreateView(inflater: LayoutInflater, container: ViewGroup?, saved: Bundle?): View =
        ComposeView(requireContext()).apply {
            // The fragment outlives its view on the back stack: tie the composition to the view's lifecycle
            setViewCompositionStrategy(ViewCompositionStrategy.DisposeOnViewTreeLifecycleDestroyed)
            setContent {
                ShopTheme { OrderDetailScreen(viewModel = viewModel()) }
            }
        }
}

// One composable inside an existing XML screen of an Activity: the default strategy is fine
fun showEta(binding: ActivityOrdersBinding, order: Order) {
    binding.etaCompose.setContent { ShopTheme { DeliveryEta(order = order) } }
}

// As a RecyclerView row: the default, DisposeOnDetachedFromWindowOrReleasedFromPool,
// keeps the composition while the row is recycled and disposes it when the pool drops it
class EtaViewHolder(val composeView: ComposeView) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(composeView) {
    fun bind(order: Order) = composeView.setContent { ShopTheme { DeliveryEta(order = order) } }
}
Result

The detail screen is a Compose screen hosted by a Fragment, so Fragment navigation keeps working; its composition is disposed when the fragment's view is destroyed, not merely detached.

Setup
  1. A project with both the View system and the Compose BOM; OrderProgressView is a custom View with a step property (see kt-android-views), and Order carries id and step
  2. Call the composables from setContent { } or a ComposeView

Themes and state across the boundary

During migration both worlds read the same colour resources and the same `StateFlow`; events cross as plain lambdas.

// One palette for both: the XML theme and the Compose theme read the same colour resources,
// and colorResource resolves values-night/ exactly as the View system does
@Composable
fun ShopTheme(content: @Composable () -> Unit) {
    val base = if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) darkColorScheme() else lightColorScheme()
    val colors = base.copy(
        primary = colorResource(R.color.brand_primary),
        onPrimary = colorResource(R.color.brand_on_primary),
        surface = colorResource(R.color.brand_surface),
    )
    MaterialTheme(colorScheme = colors, content = content)
}

class OrdersFragment : Fragment(R.layout.fragment_orders) {
    private val viewModel: OrdersViewModel by viewModels()

    override fun onViewCreated(view: View, savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onViewCreated(view, savedInstanceState)
        val binding = FragmentOrdersBinding.bind(view)
        val strategy = ViewCompositionStrategy.DisposeOnViewTreeLifecycleDestroyed
        binding.filters.setViewCompositionStrategy(strategy)
        binding.filters.setContent {
            val state by viewModel.state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()   // state in: the same StateFlow
            ShopTheme {
                StatusFilterChips(selected = state.filter, onSelect = viewModel::onFilter)   // events out
            }
        }
        // The RecyclerView below still collects the same viewModel.state with repeatOnLifecycle
    }
}
Result

The Compose filter chips and the XML list share one colour palette in light and dark mode, and choosing a chip filters the RecyclerView through the shared ViewModel.

Setup
  1. res/values/colors.xml and res/values-night/colors.xml defining brand_primary, brand_on_primary and brand_surface, used by your Theme.Material3.DayNight XML theme
  2. The Compose BOM with material3 and lifecycle-runtime-compose; an OrdersViewModel whose state has a filter, an onFilter function, and a StatusFilterChips composable

Migrating screen by screen

The incremental path the Android docs recommend; each step ships on its own.

StepWhat you doDone when
1. Set upadd the Compose BOM and the org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose Gradle plugin; write ShopTheme from the XML theme's values (Material Theme Builder helps)a ComposeView renders in brand colours in light and dark
2. New screens in Composea new Fragment returns a ComposeView; navigation stays Fragment-basednew features no longer add XML
3. A component libraryshared composables (OrderRow, StatusChip, buttons) in a design-system modulescreens stop styling components inline
4. Replace existing screens, simplest firststatic screens, then lists (RecyclerView → LazyColumn), then the complex ones; bottom-up inside mixed screensthe screen's behaviour tests pass, rewritten against Compose semantics (createAndroidComposeRule, testTag) where they matched View ids
5. Keep the architectureViewModels, StateFlows and repositories stay; only the UI layer is rewrittenno ViewModel changed for a UI migration
6. Switch navigationwhen every destination is a composable, move from Fragment navigation to Navigation Compose (type-safe routes) or Navigation 3, reusing the @Serializable routesno Fragments left
7. Remove the old worlddelete XML layouts and themes, View Binding, and AppCompat themes where nothing needs themone source of truth for theming

Interview talking points

The distinctions worth saying out loud.

  • Compose is declarative: UI is a function of state. When state changes, the functions that read it run again and Compose applies the difference.
  • Views are imperative: a long-lived, mutable object tree you keep in sync by hand — setters, adapters, notifyItem….
  • A composable is not an object: identity comes from its place in the call tree (and key); state lives in the composition through remember.
  • Compose runs three phases — composition, layout, draw. Reading state only in layout or draw lambdas is the counterpart of requestLayout() versus invalidate().
  • Compose ships inside the app (unbundled), so fixes arrive with a library update rather than an OS update; framework Views change with the platform.
  • Views remain where SDKs only ship Views (ad views, some maps and players, WebView): wrap them with AndroidView.
  • Interop is first class in both directions, so migration is incremental and the ViewModel layer is untouched.
  • The classic interop bugs: the default ViewCompositionStrategy in a Fragment (state lost on detach), a strategy tied to the fragment's lifecycle instead of viewLifecycleOwner (the composition outlives the view), and a View created outside AndroidView's factory.
  • Compare performance on release builds with R8 and a Baseline Profile; a debug Compose build is not representative.

Where each token lives

Define a token once in the theme, read it by role everywhere; Material 3 components already read the Material ones.

TokenDefined withRead in a composable

An app theme — light, dark and dynamic colour

One `ShopTheme` composable picks the scheme: dynamic (wallpaper) colours on Android 12+, your palette elsewhere.

private val LightColors = lightColorScheme(
    primary = Color(0xFF00658E), onPrimary = Color(0xFFFFFFFF),
    primaryContainer = Color(0xFFC7E7FF), onPrimaryContainer = Color(0xFF001E2E),
    surface = Color(0xFFF8F9FC), onSurface = Color(0xFF191C1E),
)   // roles you leave out keep Material's baseline values

private val DarkColors = darkColorScheme(
    primary = Color(0xFF84CFFF), onPrimary = Color(0xFF00344C),
    primaryContainer = Color(0xFF004C6C), onPrimaryContainer = Color(0xFFC7E7FF),
    surface = Color(0xFF111416), onSurface = Color(0xFFE1E2E5),
)

@Composable
fun ShopTheme(
    darkTheme: Boolean = isSystemInDarkTheme(),      // or the user's choice from settings
    dynamicColor: Boolean = true,                    // Material You: colours from the wallpaper
    content: @Composable () -> Unit,
) {
    val colorScheme = when {
        dynamicColor && Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
            val context = LocalContext.current
            if (darkTheme) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context) else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
        }
        darkTheme -> DarkColors
        else -> LightColors
    }
    MaterialTheme(
        colorScheme = colorScheme,
        typography = ShopTypography,                 // next card
        shapes = ShopShapes,
        content = content,
    )
}
Result

Every Material component inside ShopTheme takes these colours; switching the system to dark mode swaps the scheme, and on Android 12+ the palette follows the wallpaper.

Setup
  1. An Android Studio project with the Compose template (Kotlin 2.x with the org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose Gradle plugin, the Compose BOM and androidx.compose.material3:material3)
  2. Wrap your content: setContent { ShopTheme { ShopNavHost() } }

Typography, shapes, and reading tokens in a composable

Override only the styles you use; read `MaterialTheme.colorScheme`, `.typography` and `.shapes` instead of literals.

val Inter = FontFamily(
    Font(R.font.inter_regular),
    Font(R.font.inter_semibold, FontWeight.SemiBold),
)

private val Base = TextStyle(fontFamily = Inter)

val ShopTypography = Typography(                        // unspecified styles keep Material's defaults
    headlineSmall = Base.copy(fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold, fontSize = 24.sp, lineHeight = 32.sp),
    titleMedium = Base.copy(fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold, fontSize = 16.sp, lineHeight = 24.sp),
    bodyMedium = Base.copy(fontSize = 14.sp, lineHeight = 20.sp),
    labelLarge = Base.copy(fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold, fontSize = 14.sp, lineHeight = 20.sp),
)

val ShopShapes = Shapes(
    small = RoundedCornerShape(8.dp),
    medium = RoundedCornerShape(12.dp),
    large = RoundedCornerShape(20.dp),
)

@Composable
fun OrderTotalCard(total: String, itemCount: Int, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    Surface(
        modifier = modifier,
        shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.medium,
        color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primaryContainer,   // content colour becomes onPrimaryContainer
    ) {
        Column(Modifier.padding(16.dp)) {
            Text("Total", style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge)
            Text(total, style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineSmall)
            Text("$itemCount items", style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium)
        }
    }
}

A rounded card in the primary-container colour whose three lines use the theme's label, headline and body styles, all in the matching on-colour, in light and dark.

Your own tokens through CompositionLocal

Spacing and brand colours that Material has no role for: an `@Immutable` class, a `staticCompositionLocalOf`, a provider in the theme and an accessor object.

@Immutable
data class Spacing(val xs: Dp = 4.dp, val sm: Dp = 8.dp, val md: Dp = 16.dp, val lg: Dp = 24.dp)

@Immutable
data class StatusColors(val success: Color, val onSuccess: Color, val warning: Color, val onWarning: Color)

private val LightStatus = StatusColors(
    success = Color(0xFF1B6D2F), onSuccess = Color(0xFFFFFFFF),
    warning = Color(0xFF7A5900), onWarning = Color(0xFFFFFFFF),
)

private val DarkStatus = StatusColors(
    success = Color(0xFF8BD89A), onSuccess = Color(0xFF00391A),
    warning = Color(0xFFF4C04A), onWarning = Color(0xFF402D00),
)

val LocalSpacing = staticCompositionLocalOf { Spacing() }

val LocalStatusColors = staticCompositionLocalOf<StatusColors> {
    error("No StatusColors provided: wrap the content in ShopTheme")    // fail loudly outside the theme
}

// Inside ShopTheme, around MaterialTheme:
CompositionLocalProvider(
    LocalSpacing provides Spacing(),
    LocalStatusColors provides if (darkTheme) DarkStatus else LightStatus,
) {
    MaterialTheme(colorScheme, typography = ShopTypography, shapes = ShopShapes, content = content)
}

// Read them like MaterialTheme's: ShopTheme.spacing.md, ShopTheme.statusColors.success
object ShopTheme {
    val spacing: Spacing
        @Composable @ReadOnlyComposable get() = LocalSpacing.current
    val statusColors: StatusColors
        @Composable @ReadOnlyComposable get() = LocalStatusColors.current
}
Result

ShopTheme.spacing and ShopTheme.statusColors resolve anywhere under the theme and switch with dark mode; reading them outside the theme throws with a clear message.

Setup
  1. The theme from the app-theme card: wrap its MaterialTheme(…) call in the CompositionLocalProvider below

Prove the palette meets contrast — runs on the JVM

Each on-colour against its container must reach 4.5:1 for body text (WCAG AA); check the tokens in a unit test, not by eye.

import java.util.Locale
import kotlin.math.pow

fun luminance(argb: Long): Double {                  // WCAG 2.x relative luminance of an sRGB colour
    fun linear(shift: Int): Double {
        val c = ((argb shr shift) and 0xFF) / 255.0
        return if (c <= 0.03928) c / 12.92 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055).pow(2.4)
    }
    return 0.2126 * linear(16) + 0.7152 * linear(8) + 0.0722 * linear(0)
}

fun contrast(a: Long, b: Long): Double {
    val (lighter, darker) = listOf(luminance(a), luminance(b)).sortedDescending()
    return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05)
}

// The same values as LightColors / DarkColors and the status tokens in ShopTheme
val light = mapOf(
    "primary" to 0xFF00658E, "onPrimary" to 0xFFFFFFFF,
    "primaryContainer" to 0xFFC7E7FF, "onPrimaryContainer" to 0xFF001E2E,
    "surface" to 0xFFF8F9FC, "onSurface" to 0xFF191C1E,
    "success" to 0xFF1B6D2F, "onSuccess" to 0xFFFFFFFF,
    "warning" to 0xFF7A5900, "onWarning" to 0xFFFFFFFF,
)

val dark = mapOf(
    "primary" to 0xFF84CFFF, "onPrimary" to 0xFF00344C,
    "primaryContainer" to 0xFF004C6C, "onPrimaryContainer" to 0xFFC7E7FF,
    "surface" to 0xFF111416, "onSurface" to 0xFFE1E2E5,
    "success" to 0xFF8BD89A, "onSuccess" to 0xFF00391A,
    "warning" to 0xFFF4C04A, "onWarning" to 0xFF402D00,
)

val pairs = listOf("onPrimary" to "primary", "onPrimaryContainer" to "primaryContainer",
    "onSurface" to "surface", "onSuccess" to "success", "onWarning" to "warning")

fun report(label: String, foreground: Long, background: Long) {
    val ratio = contrast(foreground, background)                      // AA body text needs 4.5:1
    println("%-42s %5.2f:1 %s".format(Locale.ROOT, label, ratio, if (ratio >= 4.5) "AA" else "FAIL"))
}

fun main() {
    for ((scheme, colors) in listOf("light" to light, "dark" to dark)) {
        for ((fg, bg) in pairs) report("$scheme $fg on $bg", colors.getValue(fg), colors.getValue(bg))
    }
    report("proposed white on #FF8A00", 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFF8A00)       // a designer's "brand orange" button
}
Result
light onPrimary on primary                  6.46:1 AA
light onPrimaryContainer on primaryContainer 13.31:1 AA
light onSurface on surface                 16.27:1 AA
light onSuccess on success                  6.41:1 AA
light onWarning on warning                  6.45:1 AA
dark onPrimary on primary                   7.74:1 AA
dark onPrimaryContainer on primaryContainer  7.24:1 AA
dark onSurface on surface                  14.28:1 AA
dark onSuccess on success                   7.74:1 AA
dark onWarning on warning                   7.84:1 AA
proposed white on #FF8A00                   2.36:1 FAIL
Setup

  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar

Reusable styles — a composable per variant, a Modifier extension per chain

Callers pick an intent (`StatusChip(status)`), not colours; a repeated modifier chain becomes a plain extension that takes its values as parameters.

@Composable
fun StatusChip(status: OrderStatus, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    val colors = MaterialTheme.colorScheme
    val statusColors = ShopTheme.statusColors
    val (container, content) = when (status) {
        OrderStatus.Pending -> statusColors.warning to statusColors.onWarning
        OrderStatus.Shipped -> colors.secondaryContainer to colors.onSecondaryContainer
        OrderStatus.Delivered -> statusColors.success to statusColors.onSuccess
    }
    Text(
        text = status.name,
        color = content,
        style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelMedium,
        modifier = modifier
            .background(container, CircleShape)
            .padding(horizontal = ShopTheme.spacing.sm, vertical = ShopTheme.spacing.xs),
    )
}

// Not @Composable: the theme values come in as arguments, so the chain is cheap and testable
fun Modifier.cardSurface(shape: Shape, color: Color, elevation: Dp = 1.dp): Modifier =
    this
        .shadow(elevation, shape)          // also clips to the shape when elevation > 0
        .background(color, shape)

@Composable
fun OrderSummaryCard(order: Order, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    Row(
        modifier = modifier
            .cardSurface(MaterialTheme.shapes.medium, MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceContainer)
            .padding(ShopTheme.spacing.md),
        horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(ShopTheme.spacing.sm),
        verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
    ) {
        Text(order.customer, Modifier.weight(1f), style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
        StatusChip(order.status)
    }
}
Result

A raised rounded card with the customer name and a pill-shaped status chip coloured by meaning (warning, neutral, success), correct in light and dark.

Component defaults objects — override a role, keep the rest

`ButtonDefaults`, `CardDefaults` and friends build a component's colours, elevation and padding; pass only what differs and the disabled and pressed states stay correct.

@Composable
fun PlaceOrderButton(onClick: () -> Unit, placing: Boolean, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    Button(
        onClick = onClick,
        enabled = !placing,
        modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth().heightIn(min = 56.dp),   // a minimum, so large fonts still fit
        shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.large,
        colors = ButtonDefaults.buttonColors(
            containerColor = ShopTheme.statusColors.success,          // two roles overridden…
            contentColor = ShopTheme.statusColors.onSuccess,          // …the disabled colours stay Material's
        ),
        contentPadding = ButtonDefaults.ButtonWithIconContentPadding,
    ) {
        val iconModifier = Modifier.size(ButtonDefaults.IconSize)
        if (placing) {
            CircularProgressIndicator(iconModifier, color = LocalContentColor.current, strokeWidth = 2.dp)
        } else {
            val cart = painterResource(R.drawable.shopping_cart_24)
            Icon(cart, contentDescription = null, modifier = iconModifier)
        }
        Spacer(Modifier.size(ButtonDefaults.IconSpacing))
        Text("Place order")
    }
}

@Composable
fun OrderCard(order: Order, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    Card(
        onClick = onClick,
        modifier = modifier,
        colors = CardDefaults.cardColors(containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceContainerHigh),
        elevation = CardDefaults.cardElevation(defaultElevation = 0.dp, pressedElevation = 2.dp),
    ) {
        Row(Modifier.padding(ShopTheme.spacing.md), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
            Text(order.customer, Modifier.weight(1f), style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
            StatusChip(order.status)                     // plain content: the Card is the surface
        }
    }
}
Result

A full-width green Place order button with a cart icon that turns into a spinner and the disabled colours while placing; a flat card holding the name and status chip that lifts slightly when pressed.

Window size classes and font scaling

Branch on the window's width class, not the device; size text in `sp` and give text containers minimum, not fixed, heights.

@Composable
fun OrdersAdaptive(state: OrdersUiState, onOpen: (String) -> Unit) {
    val sizeClass = currentWindowAdaptiveInfo().windowSizeClass          // recomputed on resize, fold, rotate
    when {
        sizeClass.isWidthAtLeastBreakpoint(WindowSizeClass.WIDTH_DP_EXPANDED_LOWER_BOUND) ->   // ≥ 840 dp
            Row {
                OrderList(state.items, onOpen, Modifier.weight(0.4f))
                OrderDetailPane(state.selected, Modifier.weight(0.6f))
            }
        sizeClass.isWidthAtLeastBreakpoint(WindowSizeClass.WIDTH_DP_MEDIUM_LOWER_BOUND) ->     // 600–839 dp
            OrderGrid(state.items, onOpen, columns = 2)
        else -> OrderList(state.items, onOpen)                                                 // compact
    }
}

@Composable
fun TotalLine(label: String, value: String) {
    val largeText = LocalDensity.current.fontScale >= 1.5f                // the user chose big text
    val textStyle = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge                      // sp: scales with the setting
    if (largeText) {
        Column(Modifier.heightIn(min = 48.dp)) {                            // stack instead of squeezing
            Text(label, style = textStyle)
            Text(value, style = textStyle, fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold)
        }
    } else {
        Row(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().heightIn(min = 48.dp), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
            Text(
                label, Modifier.weight(1f), style = textStyle,
                maxLines = 2, overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis,
            )
            Text(value, style = textStyle, fontWeight = FontWeight.SemiBold)
        }
    }
}
Result

A phone shows the list; a 600 dp window a two-column grid; 840 dp and wider list and detail side by side. At 150% font size and above, each total line stacks its label over its value.

Setup
  1. The Compose template project, plus androidx.compose.material3.adaptive:adaptive 1.2 or later (it brings androidx.window 1.4, where isWidthAtLeastBreakpoint and the breakpoint constants are new); adaptive 1.3 deprecates currentWindowAdaptiveInfo() in favour of currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2(), which also reports the large and extra-large width classes
  2. OrderList, OrderGrid and OrderDetailPane composables and an OrdersUiState with items and selected; call OrdersAdaptive from your screen

Styling pitfalls

What breaks dark mode, dynamic colour and large text.

  • Color(0xFF…) literals in screens: dark theme and dynamic colour cannot reach them. Read a role from MaterialTheme.colorScheme or your own tokens.
  • Mismatched roles — onPrimary text on primaryContainer — fail contrast. Pair onX with X, or let Surface(color = …) pick the content colour.
  • Dynamic colour replaces your palette on Android 12+; keep colours that carry meaning (success, warning, brand marks) in your own tokens and decide dynamicColor deliberately.
  • staticCompositionLocalOf for theme tokens that rarely change (cheap reads, the subtree recomposes on change); compositionLocalOf for values that change often and are read in few places.
  • Text sized in dp, or containers with fixed heights: Android 14 scales fonts non-linearly up to 200%. Use sp, heightIn(min = …) and allow wrapping.
  • isTablet-style checks: the window size class changes with split screen, folding and resizing; read currentWindowAdaptiveInfo().
  • Preview every variant: @PreviewLightDark, @PreviewFontScale and @PreviewScreenSizes (or @Preview(uiMode = …, fontScale = 2f)).
  • Material 3 Expressive and the experimental Compose Styles API are newer than this sheet's baseline; check the BOM before adopting them.

A view model is a plain class

Expose a read-only `StateFlow`, take intents as methods and the scope as a parameter — no Android type inside, and a restarted load cancels the one in flight.

@file:OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.*
import java.io.IOException

sealed interface OrdersUiState {
    data object Loading : OrdersUiState
    data class Content(val orderIds: List<Int>) : OrdersUiState
    data class Error(val message: String) : OrdersUiState
}

class OrdersViewModel(private val fetchOrders: suspend () -> List<Int>, private val scope: CoroutineScope) {
    private val _state = MutableStateFlow<OrdersUiState>(OrdersUiState.Loading)
    val state: StateFlow<OrdersUiState> = _state.asStateFlow()        // the view can read, never write
    private var loadJob: Job? = null

    fun load() {                                                       // an intent is a method
        loadJob?.cancel()                                              // a second tap restarts, never races
        _state.value = OrdersUiState.Loading
        loadJob = scope.launch {
            _state.value = try {
                OrdersUiState.Content(fetchOrders())
            } catch (e: IOException) {                     // expected; anything else is a bug: let it crash
                OrdersUiState.Error("Couldn't load orders (${e.message})")
            }
        }
    }
}

fun main() = runTest {
    val replies = ArrayDeque(listOf<suspend () -> List<Int>>(           // the fake repository, one per call
        { delay(1_000); listOf(1041) },                      // slow: superseded before it answers
        { delay(200); throw IOException("offline") },
        { delay(300); listOf(1042, 1043) },
    ))
    val vm = OrdersViewModel({ replies.removeFirst().invoke() }, scope = this)  // viewModelScope in the app
    backgroundScope.launch(UnconfinedTestDispatcher(testScheduler)) { vm.state.collect { println(it) } }

    vm.load()
    advanceTimeBy(100)
    vm.load()                                                             // restarts the slow load; it fails
    advanceUntilIdle()
    vm.load()                                                             // the user taps Retry
}
Result
Loading
Error(message=Couldn't load orders (offline))
Loading
Content(orderIds=[1042, 1043])

  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc -cp kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm-1.10.2.jar:kotlinx-coroutines-test-jvm-1.10.2.jar main.kt -d out && kotlin -cp out:kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm-1.10.2.jar:kotlinx-coroutines-test-jvm-1.10.2.jar MainKt

UiState: flags in a data class, or a sealed interface

Mutually exclusive screens are a sealed interface; keep a data class for fields that vary independently (a form, a refresh spinner over content).

Flags — impossible states compile
data class OrdersUiState(
    val isLoading: Boolean = false,
    val orders: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val error: String? = null,             // isLoading AND error both set compiles: a screen nobody designed
)

fun render(state: OrdersUiState): String = when {
    state.isLoading -> "spinner"
    state.error != null -> "error: ${state.error}"
    else -> "${state.orders.size} orders"  // also what "not loaded yet" looks like
}

fun main() {
    println(render(OrdersUiState(isLoading = true)))
    println(render(OrdersUiState(error = "offline")))
    println(render(OrdersUiState(orders = listOf("#1042", "#1043"))))
}
Sealed — one case at a time
sealed interface OrdersUiState {
    data object Loading : OrdersUiState
    data class Content(val orders: List<String>) : OrdersUiState
    data class Error(val message: String) : OrdersUiState
}

fun render(state: OrdersUiState): String = when (state) {   // exhaustive: a new state breaks the build here
    OrdersUiState.Loading -> "spinner"
    is OrdersUiState.Error -> "error: ${state.message}"
    is OrdersUiState.Content -> "${state.orders.size} orders"
}

fun main() {
    println(render(OrdersUiState.Loading))
    println(render(OrdersUiState.Error("offline")))
    println(render(OrdersUiState.Content(listOf("#1042", "#1043"))))
}
Result
spinner
error: offline
2 orders

Update state atomically

`update { }` is a compare-and-set loop: the lambda may run more than once, so keep it a pure `copy`.

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*

data class KitchenUiState(val newOrders: Int = 0, val acknowledged: Int = 0)

fun main() = runBlocking {
    val state = MutableStateFlow(KitchenUiState())

    withContext(Dispatchers.Default) {                       // two writers on different threads
        launch {                                             // orders pushed by the server
            repeat(10_000) { state.update { it.copy(newOrders = it.newOrders + 1) } }
        }
        launch {                                             // the cook tapping "Seen"
            repeat(10_000) { state.update { it.copy(acknowledged = it.acknowledged + 1) } }
        }
    }
    // With `state.value = state.value.copy(...)` both writers read the same old value
    // and one overwrites the other: the totals come out short, and differently each run.
    println(state.value)

    val before = state.getAndUpdate { it.copy(acknowledged = 0) }   // read-and-reset in one step
    println("cleared ${before.acknowledged} acknowledgements -> ${state.value}")
}
Result
KitchenUiState(newOrders=10000, acknowledged=10000)
cleared 10000 acknowledgements -> KitchenUiState(newOrders=10000, acknowledged=0)

A text field drives a cancellable search

The field owns its text and reports each edit; `transformLatest` cancels the stale request and catches a failure inside, so one error never ends the search (the `Job` version is in Compose — State & Data Flow).

@file:OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.*
import java.io.IOException

sealed interface SearchUiState {
    data object Idle : SearchUiState
    data class Searching(val query: String) : SearchUiState
    data class Results(val query: String, val orderIds: List<Int>) : SearchUiState
    data class Failed(val query: String) : SearchUiState
}

class OrderSearchViewModel(search: suspend (String) -> List<Int>, scope: CoroutineScope) {
    private val query = MutableStateFlow("")

    val results: StateFlow<SearchUiState> = query
        .transformLatest { q ->                                   // a new query cancels the running search
            if (q.isBlank()) {
                emit(SearchUiState.Idle)
            } else {
                emit(SearchUiState.Searching(q))
                val outcome = try { SearchUiState.Results(q, search(q)) }   // caught INSIDE: one failure
                    catch (e: IOException) { SearchUiState.Failed(q) }        // must not end later searches
                emit(outcome)
            }
        }
        .stateIn(scope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000), SearchUiState.Idle)

    fun onQueryChange(text: String) { query.value = text }            // the field owns its text, reports it
}

fun main() = runTest {
    val vm = OrderSearchViewModel(scope = backgroundScope, search = { q ->
        delay(200)                                                    // the server takes 200 ms...
        if (q == "#1") throw IOException("503")                      // ...and fails once
        listOf(1042, 1043, 1049).filter { "#$it".startsWith(q) }
    })
    backgroundScope.launch(UnconfinedTestDispatcher(testScheduler)) { vm.results.collect { println(it) } }

    // (what the user typed, then the pause before the next edit): "#1" fails; the next three come fast
    for ((typed, pause) in listOf("#1" to 300L, "#10" to 100L, "#104" to 100L, "#1042" to 400L)) {
        vm.onQueryChange(typed)
        advanceTimeBy(pause)
    }
}
Result
Idle
Searching(query=#1)
Failed(query=#1)
Searching(query=#10)
Searching(query=#104)
Searching(query=#1042)
Results(query=#1042, orderIds=[1042])

One-off events are state

A `SharedFlow` event emitted while the screen is stopped is dropped and a `Channel` event can be lost when the collector is cancelled mid-handling, but a `userMessage` in state waits until the UI shows it and says so.

@file:OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.*

sealed interface UserMessage {                              // what to say; the UI picks the string resource
    data class OrderCancelled(val orderId: Int) : UserMessage
}

data class OrderDetailUiState(val status: String, val userMessage: UserMessage? = null)

class OrderDetailViewModel(private val scope: CoroutineScope) {
    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(OrderDetailUiState(status = "PLACED"))
    val state: StateFlow<OrderDetailUiState> = _state.asStateFlow()
    val events = MutableSharedFlow<UserMessage>()           // the fragile way, kept to compare

    fun onCancelTapped() {
        scope.launch {
            delay(500)                                      // the server call; the user leaves meanwhile
            _state.update { it.copy(status = "CANCELLED", userMessage = UserMessage.OrderCancelled(1042)) }
            events.emit(UserMessage.OrderCancelled(1042))   // no collector right now: the event is dropped
        }
    }

    fun onUserMessageShown() = _state.update { it.copy(userMessage = null) }
}

fun main() = runTest {
    val vm = OrderDetailViewModel(scope = this)
    vm.onCancelTapped()
    advanceUntilIdle()                                      // the screen is stopped: nobody collects

    val seen = mutableListOf<UserMessage>()                 // the screen is STARTED again
    backgroundScope.launch(UnconfinedTestDispatcher(testScheduler)) { vm.events.collect { seen += it } }
    println("SharedFlow event: ${seen.ifEmpty { "lost" }}")

    vm.state.value.userMessage?.let { message ->            // state-based: still waiting to be shown
        println("snackbar for $message")
        vm.onUserMessageShown()                             // consuming it is an event back to the VM
    }
    println(vm.state.value)
}
Result
SharedFlow event: lost
snackbar for OrderCancelled(orderId=1042)
OrderDetailUiState(status=CANCELLED, userMessage=null)

The Android ViewModel: viewModelScope, SavedStateHandle, stateIn

Subclass `ViewModel` for the back-stack lifetime, catch inside `flatMapLatest` so the next query recovers from an error, and `WhileSubscribed(5_000)` keeps upstream alive through a rotation.

class OrdersViewModel(
    private val repository: OrderRepository,              // constructor injection: a fake in tests
    private val savedStateHandle: SavedStateHandle,
) : ViewModel() {
    val query: StateFlow<String> = savedStateHandle.getStateFlow("query", "")   // survives process death

    @OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)
    val uiState: StateFlow<OrdersUiState> = query
        .flatMapLatest { q ->
            repository.observeOrders(q)                       // Flow<List<Order>>, e.g. from Room
                .map<List<Order>, OrdersUiState> { OrdersUiState.Content(it) }
                .onStart { emit(OrdersUiState.Loading) }
                .catch { emit(OrdersUiState.Error(it.message ?: "Couldn't load orders")) }   // per query
        }
        .stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000), OrdersUiState.Loading)

    fun onQueryChange(text: String) { savedStateHandle["query"] = text }

    fun onCancelTapped(orderId: Int) {
        viewModelScope.launch { repository.cancel(orderId) }  // cancelled when the ViewModel is cleared
    }

    companion object {
        val Factory: ViewModelProvider.Factory = viewModelFactory {
            initializer {
                val app = this[APPLICATION_KEY] as OrdersApplication
                OrdersViewModel(app.orderRepository, createSavedStateHandle())
            }
        }
    }
}
Result

The screen gets Loading, then the orders matching the saved query; a repository error shows Error for that query only, the query survives rotation and process death, and upstream stops 5 s after the screen is backgrounded.

Setup
  1. An Android Studio project with androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-viewmodel and lifecycle-viewmodel-savedstate (2.8 or later; -ktx is empty since 2.8)
  2. An OrderRepository with fun observeOrders(query: String): Flow<List<Order>> and suspend fun cancel(orderId: Int), held by your Application subclass OrdersApplication
  3. The OrdersUiState sealed interface from the cards above

Binding it in Compose: collectAsStateWithLifecycle and a TextFieldState

State flows down, lambdas flow up; only the route-level composable sees the ViewModel.

@Composable
fun OrdersRoute(vm: OrdersViewModel = viewModel(factory = OrdersViewModel.Factory)) {
    val uiState by vm.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()        // collects only while STARTED

    // The field owns its text (Google's "conforming approach"); the VM only receives it. For edits the
    // VM makes itself (Clear, autocomplete), hold a TextFieldState in the VM and call clearText() there.
    val queryState = rememberTextFieldState(initialText = vm.query.value)
    LaunchedEffect(queryState) {                                  // field -> VM on every edit
        snapshotFlow { queryState.text.toString() }.collectLatest { vm.onQueryChange(it) }
    }

    OrdersScreen(uiState, queryState, onCancel = vm::onCancelTapped)   // children get state and lambdas
}

@Composable
fun OrdersScreen(uiState: OrdersUiState, queryState: TextFieldState, onCancel: (Int) -> Unit) {
    Column {
        TextField(state = queryState, lineLimits = TextFieldLineLimits.SingleLine)
        when (uiState) {
            OrdersUiState.Loading -> CircularProgressIndicator()
            is OrdersUiState.Error -> Text(uiState.message)
            is OrdersUiState.Content -> LazyColumn {
                items(uiState.orders, key = { it.id }) { order ->
                    OrderRow(order, onCancel = { onCancel(order.id) })
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
Result

Typing filters the list as the field changes; the list stops updating while the app is in the background and resumes when it returns.

  2. The OrdersViewModel of the card above, and an OrderRow composable

Testing the view model: Main dispatcher, fake repository, errors

`Dispatchers.setMain` stands in for Android's main thread and `runTest` skips the delays, and each check fails if its guarded line (the `IOException` catch, the error reset) is removed.

@file:OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.*
import java.io.IOException

data class OrderUiState(val loading: Boolean = false, val status: String? = null, val error: String? = null)

class OrderViewModel(private val fetchStatus: suspend (orderId: Int) -> String) {
    private val scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main.immediate)   // = viewModelScope
    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(OrderUiState())
    val state: StateFlow<OrderUiState> = _state.asStateFlow()
    private var refreshJob: Job? = null

    fun refresh(orderId: Int) {
        refreshJob?.cancel()                                 // a newer refresh replaces a slower one
        _state.update { it.copy(loading = true, error = null) }
        refreshJob = scope.launch {
            _state.value = try {
                OrderUiState(status = fetchStatus(orderId))
            } catch (e: IOException) {                      // NOT Exception: cancellation must pass through
                _state.value.copy(loading = false, error = e.message)
            }
        }
    }

    fun clear() = scope.cancel()                             // ViewModel.onCleared() in the app
}

fun main() = runTest {                                       // a @Test function in JUnit
    Dispatchers.setMain(StandardTestDispatcher(testScheduler))   // a MainDispatcherRule: before each test
    var reply: suspend () -> String = { delay(1_000); throw IOException("server error") }
    val vm = OrderViewModel { reply() }                  // the fake repository

    vm.refresh(1042)
    advanceUntilIdle()
    check(vm.state.value == OrderUiState(error = "server error"))   // an expected failure is state

    reply = { delay(1_000); "READY" }
    vm.refresh(1042)
    runCurrent()
    check(vm.state.value == OrderUiState(loading = true))   // the next refresh clears the error at once
    vm.clear()
    println("refresh test passed after $currentTime ms of virtual time")
    Dispatchers.resetMain()                                  // ...and after; no rule: @AfterEach/finally
}
Result
refresh test passed after 1000 ms of virtual time
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc), JDK 17 or later, kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm-1.10.2.jar and kotlinx-coroutines-test-jvm-1.10.2.jar

Testing cancellation: a slower, older reply never lands

A newer refresh cancels the one in flight, and the check fails both when the `Job` is not cancelled and when `catch (e: Exception)` turns the cancellation into an error.

@file:OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.*
import java.io.IOException

data class OrderUiState(val loading: Boolean = false, val status: String? = null, val error: String? = null)

class OrderViewModel(private val fetchStatus: suspend (orderId: Int) -> String) {
    private val scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main.immediate)   // = viewModelScope
    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(OrderUiState())
    val state: StateFlow<OrderUiState> = _state.asStateFlow()
    private var refreshJob: Job? = null

    fun refresh(orderId: Int) {
        refreshJob?.cancel()                                 // a newer refresh replaces a slower one
        _state.update { it.copy(loading = true, error = null) }
        refreshJob = scope.launch {
            _state.value = try {
                OrderUiState(status = fetchStatus(orderId))
            } catch (e: IOException) {                      // NOT Exception: cancellation must pass through
                _state.value.copy(loading = false, error = e.message)
            }
        }
    }

    fun clear() = scope.cancel()                             // ViewModel.onCleared() in the app
}

fun main() = runTest {                                       // a @Test function in JUnit
    Dispatchers.setMain(StandardTestDispatcher(testScheduler))   // a MainDispatcherRule: before each test
    var reply: suspend () -> String = { delay(5_000); "PLACED (stale)" }
    val vm = OrderViewModel { reply() }

    vm.refresh(1042)
    runCurrent()                                         // a slow request is in flight...
    reply = { delay(1_000); "READY" }
    vm.refresh(1042)
    runCurrent()                                         // ...and a newer refresh cancels it
    check(vm.state.value == OrderUiState(loading = true)) { "cancellation became ${vm.state.value}" }
    advanceUntilIdle()
    check(vm.state.value == OrderUiState(status = "READY")) { "the stale reply landed: ${vm.state.value}" }
    vm.clear()
    println("cancellation test passed after $currentTime ms of virtual time")
    Dispatchers.resetMain()                                  // ...and after; no rule: @AfterEach/finally
}
Result
cancellation test passed after 1000 ms of virtual time

Rules and pitfalls

What a reviewer flags first in a view model.

  • A public MutableStateFlow: any composable can write state, and the view model stops being the single source of truth.
  • Context, View, Resources or a NavController inside the view model — it outlives them and leaks. Expose ids or a message model; the UI resolves strings.
  • _state.value = _state.value.copy(…) from more than one coroutine: updates are lost. Use update { }.
  • collectAsState() on Android keeps collecting in the background; use collectAsStateWithLifecycle().
  • catch (e: IllegalStateException), catch (e: Exception) or runCatching around a suspend call also catches CancellationException — catch the I/O type, or rethrow CancellationException.
  • catch after flatMapLatest ends the stream for good on the first error — catch inside it, per inner flow.
  • One UiState per screen; a sealed interface when its modes exclude each other, so when is exhaustive.
  • Inject repositories and the scope (or the dispatcher) through the constructor, so a test can pass fakes and virtual time.
  • Pass the ViewModel only to the route-level composable; children take state and lambdas, which keeps them previewable.
  • stateIn(…, WhileSubscribed(5_000), initial) for state derived from repositories; a plain MutableStateFlow for state the view model writes itself.

MVI — Unidirectional State with a Reducer

State, action, reducer, effect, store — a pure reducer and a small store on StateFlow and a Channel, with failures as actions, cancellable effects, composition, selectors and tests, all on the JVM.

  • jvm
  • android
  • kotlinx-coroutines-core
  • kotlin >=2.0
  • kotlinx-coroutines >=1.10
  • jvm >=17
  • Kotlin/JVM with kotlinx.coroutines

Sources: UI layer — Unidirectional data flow (Android Developers) · Coroutines and channels — Kotlin docs · The Composable Architecture (Point-Free)

The nouns, and their TCA twins

Golden rule, as in TCA: the reducer never does async work, effects never write state — they send actions.

NounKotlin MVITCAWhat it is
Statedata class TodosState@ObservableState struct Stateeverything the screen renders, immutable
Action (intent)sealed interface TodosActionenum Actioneverything that happened: user events and results
Reducerfun reduce(state, action): Next<State, Effect>Reduce { state, action in … }pure and synchronous; returns new state plus effects to run
Effecta data value the store hands to a runner that returns an ActionEffect<Action> / .run { send in }the only place I/O and time live; a failure comes back as an action
StoreStateFlow<State> + a Channel<Action> read by one loopStore / StoreOf<Feature>serialises actions, holds state, runs effects
Dependenciesconstructor parameters of the effect runner@Dependency(\.apiClient)swapped for fakes in tests
Cancellationa Job per effect id, or collectLatest.cancellable(id:cancelInFlight:)a newer effect replaces the running one
Compositiona parent reducer delegating to child reducersScope(state:action:)each child sees only its slice
Testingcall reduce directly; call the effect runner with a fake; drive the store with runTestTestStore + store.send / store.receivestate, effects and results are plain values

A minimal feature: state, actions, effects, a pure reducer

Effects come back as data, so the reducer stays a pure function you can call in a loop.

data class Todo(val id: Int, val title: String, val done: Boolean = false)

data class TodosState(val todos: List<Todo> = emptyList(), val loading: Boolean = false,
                      val error: String? = null)

sealed interface TodosAction {                              // everything that can happen
    data object ScreenOpened : TodosAction
    data class TodoToggled(val id: Int) : TodosAction
    data class TodosLoaded(val todos: List<Todo>) : TodosAction
    data class LoadFailed(val message: String) : TodosAction
}

sealed interface TodosEffect {                              // work the store must do: data, not code
    data object FetchTodos : TodosEffect
    data class SaveDone(val id: Int, val done: Boolean) : TodosEffect
}

data class Next(val state: TodosState, val effects: List<TodosEffect> = emptyList())

fun reduce(state: TodosState, action: TodosAction): Next = when (action) {
    TodosAction.ScreenOpened ->
        Next(state.copy(loading = true, error = null), listOf(TodosEffect.FetchTodos))
    is TodosAction.TodosLoaded -> Next(state.copy(todos = action.todos, loading = false))
    is TodosAction.LoadFailed -> Next(state.copy(loading = false, error = action.message))
    is TodosAction.TodoToggled -> {
        val todos = state.todos.map { if (it.id == action.id) it.copy(done = !it.done) else it }
        val done = todos.first { it.id == action.id }.done
        Next(state.copy(todos = todos), listOf(TodosEffect.SaveDone(action.id, done)))   // optimistic
    }
}

fun main() {
    var state = TodosState()
    val actions = listOf(
        TodosAction.ScreenOpened,
        TodosAction.TodosLoaded(listOf(Todo(1, "Buy milk"), Todo(2, "Book flights"))),
        TodosAction.TodoToggled(2),
    )
    for (action in actions) {
        val next = reduce(state, action)
        state = next.state
        println("$state, effects=${next.effects}")
    }
}
Result
TodosState(todos=[], loading=true, error=null), effects=[FetchTodos]
TodosState(todos=[Todo(id=1, title=Buy milk, done=false), Todo(id=2, title=Book flights, done=false)], loading=false, error=null), effects=[]
TodosState(todos=[Todo(id=1, title=Buy milk, done=false), Todo(id=2, title=Book flights, done=true)], loading=false, error=null), effects=[SaveDone(id=2, done=true)]
Setup

A store: StateFlow, a Channel, one loop

One coroutine reads the action channel so the reducer runs one action at a time, and the store catches an effect's `IOException` and sends it back as an action, so the app does not crash and the loop lives on.

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest
import java.io.IOException

data class TodosState(val titles: List<String> = emptyList(), val error: String? = null)

sealed interface TodosAction {
    data object Opened : TodosAction
    data class Loaded(val result: Result<List<String>>) : TodosAction
}

fun reduce(state: TodosState, action: TodosAction): Pair<TodosState, List<String>> = when (action) {
    TodosAction.Opened -> state.copy(error = null) to listOf("/todos")          // effects, as data
    is TodosAction.Loaded -> action.result.fold(
        onSuccess = { TodosState(titles = it) },
        onFailure = { state.copy(error = it.message) },
    ) to emptyList()
}

class TodosStore(private val fetch: suspend (String) -> List<String>, private val scope: CoroutineScope) {
    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(TodosState())
    val state: StateFlow<TodosState> = _state.asStateFlow()
    private val actions = Channel<TodosAction>(Channel.UNLIMITED)   // send() never suspends, never drops

    init { scope.launch { for (action in actions) dispatch(action) } }   // one at a time: no races

    private fun dispatch(action: TodosAction) {
        val (next, effects) = reduce(_state.value, action)
        _state.value = next
        for (path in effects) scope.launch {          // beside the loop; IOException only: cancel passes
            val result = try { Result.success(fetch(path)) } catch (e: IOException) { Result.failure(e) }
            actions.send(TodosAction.Loaded(result))               // a throw becomes an action: no crash
        }
    }

    fun send(action: TodosAction) { actions.trySend(action) }
}

fun main() = runTest {                                         // backgroundScope: viewModelScope in the app
    val replies = ArrayDeque(listOf(null, listOf("Buy milk")))     // the fake API: it throws, then answers
    val store = TodosStore({ replies.removeFirst() ?: throw IOException("503") }, backgroundScope)

    store.send(TodosAction.Opened)
    println(store.state.first { it.error != null })                // the fetch threw: now it is state
    store.send(TodosAction.Opened)
    println(store.state.first { it.titles.isNotEmpty() })          // and Retry works: the loop is alive
}
Result
TodosState(titles=[], error=503)
TodosState(titles=[Buy milk], error=null)
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc), JDK 17 or later, kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm-1.10.2.jar and kotlinx-coroutines-test-jvm-1.10.2.jar

Actions are events, not setters

Name what happened (`AddTapped`), not what to change (`SetSaving`); the rule then lives in the reducer — and both versions provably end in the same state.

Setters — the view runs the logic
data class TodosState(val draft: String = "", val titles: List<String> = emptyList(),
                      val saving: Boolean = false)

sealed interface TodosAction {                         // setters: the view decides what happens
    data class SetDraft(val text: String) : TodosAction
    data class SetTitles(val titles: List<String>) : TodosAction
    data class SetSaving(val saving: Boolean) : TodosAction
}

fun reduce(state: TodosState, action: TodosAction): TodosState = when (action) {
    is TodosAction.SetDraft -> state.copy(draft = action.text)
    is TodosAction.SetTitles -> state.copy(titles = action.titles)
    is TodosAction.SetSaving -> state.copy(saving = action.saving)
}

fun main() {
    var state = TodosState()
    fun send(action: TodosAction) { state = reduce(state, action) }

    send(TodosAction.SetDraft("Buy milk "))
    if (state.draft.isNotBlank()) {                    // the Add button's handler: the rule is in the view
        send(TodosAction.SetTitles(state.titles + state.draft.trim()))   // and each caller repeats it
        send(TodosAction.SetDraft(""))
        send(TodosAction.SetSaving(true))
    }
    println(state)
}
Events — the reducer runs the logic
data class TodosState(val draft: String = "", val titles: List<String> = emptyList(),
                      val saving: Boolean = false)

sealed interface TodosAction {                         // events: what the user did
    data class DraftChanged(val text: String) : TodosAction
    data object AddTapped : TodosAction
}

fun reduce(state: TodosState, action: TodosAction): TodosState = when (action) {
    is TodosAction.DraftChanged -> state.copy(draft = action.text)
    TodosAction.AddTapped ->
        if (state.draft.isBlank()) state               // the rule lives here, tested once
        else state.copy(draft = "", titles = state.titles + state.draft.trim(), saving = true)
}

fun main() {
    var state = TodosState()
    fun send(action: TodosAction) { state = reduce(state, action) }

    send(TodosAction.DraftChanged("Buy milk "))
    send(TodosAction.AddTapped)                        // the view reports the tap and nothing else
    println(state)
}
Result
TodosState(draft=, titles=[Buy milk], saving=true)
