Effects that cancel in flight — and debounce inside the store

A `Job` per effect id gives `cancelInFlight` and a `delay` at the start of the effect makes it a debounce, so only the last keystroke reaches the API (one effect stream can use `collectLatest` instead).

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.Channel
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest

data class SearchState(val query: String = "", val results: List<String> = emptyList())

sealed interface SearchAction {
    data class QueryChanged(val query: String) : SearchAction
    data class ResultsLoaded(val results: List<String>) : SearchAction   // tag it with its query in an app:
}                                                                           // see "Stale results" below

fun reduce(state: SearchState, action: SearchAction): Pair<SearchState, String?> = when (action) {
    is SearchAction.QueryChanged -> SearchState(query = action.query) to action.query   // effect: search it
    is SearchAction.ResultsLoaded -> state.copy(results = action.results) to null
}

class SearchStore(private val search: suspend (String) -> List<String>, private val scope: CoroutineScope) {
    private val _state = MutableStateFlow(SearchState())
    val state: StateFlow<SearchState> = _state.asStateFlow()
    private val actions = Channel<SearchAction>(Channel.UNLIMITED)
    private var searchJob: Job? = null                   // a Job per effect id; this feature has one

    init { scope.launch { for (action in actions) dispatch(action) } }   // one at a time, as above

    private fun dispatch(action: SearchAction) {
        val (next, query) = reduce(_state.value, action)
        _state.value = next
        if (query == null) return
        searchJob?.cancel()                              // cancel in flight: the newer search wins
        searchJob = scope.launch {
            delay(300)                                   // debounce: the next keystroke cancels this wait
            actions.send(SearchAction.ResultsLoaded(search(query)))
        }
    }

    fun send(action: SearchAction) { actions.trySend(action) }
}

fun main() = runTest {
    val searched = mutableListOf<String>()               // the queries that reached the fake API
    val store = SearchStore({ q -> listOf("Buy milk").also { searched += q } }, backgroundScope)
    for (q in listOf("m", "mi", "mil")) {
        store.send(SearchAction.QueryChanged(q))
        delay(100)                                       // a keystroke every 100 ms (virtual time)
    }
    println("${store.state.first { it.results.isNotEmpty() }}, searched $searched")
}
Result
SearchState(query=mil, results=[Buy milk]), searched [mil]

Stale results — cancelling a Job does not recall an action

A result already queued when its Job was cancelled still reaches the reducer, so tag it with what it was computed for and drop it when the state has moved on.

data class SearchState(val query: String = "", val results: List<String> = emptyList())

sealed interface SearchAction {
    data class QueryChanged(val query: String) : SearchAction
    data class ResultsLoaded(val query: String, val results: List<String>) : SearchAction   // tagged
}

fun reduce(state: SearchState, action: SearchAction): SearchState = when (action) {
    is SearchAction.QueryChanged -> SearchState(query = action.query)
    is SearchAction.ResultsLoaded ->
        if (action.query == state.query) state.copy(results = action.results)
        else state                                       // stale: for a query the user has already left
}

fun main() {
    // An order the store's channel really delivers: the "milk" search finished just as "parcel"
    // was typed, so its result was already queued when its Job was cancelled.
    val delivered = listOf(
        SearchAction.QueryChanged("milk"),
        SearchAction.QueryChanged("parcel"),
        SearchAction.ResultsLoaded("milk", listOf("Buy milk")),
        SearchAction.ResultsLoaded("parcel", listOf("Mail parcel")),
    )
    delivered.runningFold(SearchState(), ::reduce).drop(1).forEach(::println)
}
Result
SearchState(query=milk, results=[])
SearchState(query=parcel, results=[])
SearchState(query=parcel, results=[])
SearchState(query=parcel, results=[Mail parcel])

Composing child reducers into a parent

Each child reduces its own slice, and the parent wraps child actions and keeps the cross-cutting ones such as sign-out.

data class TodosState(val titles: List<String> = emptyList())
sealed interface TodosAction { data class Added(val title: String) : TodosAction }
fun todosReducer(state: TodosState, action: TodosAction): TodosState = when (action) {
    is TodosAction.Added -> state.copy(titles = state.titles + action.title)
}

data class SettingsState(val hideDone: Boolean = false)
sealed interface SettingsAction { data object HideDoneToggled : SettingsAction }
fun settingsReducer(state: SettingsState, action: SettingsAction): SettingsState = when (action) {
    SettingsAction.HideDoneToggled -> state.copy(hideDone = !state.hideDone)
}

data class AppState(
    val todos: TodosState = TodosState(),
    val settings: SettingsState = SettingsState(),
    val user: String? = "ana",
)

sealed interface AppAction {
    data class Todos(val action: TodosAction) : AppAction           // a child's actions, wrapped
    data class Settings(val action: SettingsAction) : AppAction
    data object SignedOut : AppAction                               // the parent's own
}

fun appReducer(state: AppState, action: AppAction): AppState = when (action) {
    is AppAction.Todos -> state.copy(todos = todosReducer(state.todos, action.action))   // child: its slice
    is AppAction.Settings -> state.copy(settings = settingsReducer(state.settings, action.action))
    AppAction.SignedOut -> AppState(user = null)          // cross-cutting: the parent resets every child
}

fun main() {
    val actions = listOf(
        AppAction.Todos(TodosAction.Added("Buy milk")),
        AppAction.Settings(SettingsAction.HideDoneToggled),
        AppAction.SignedOut,
    )
    actions.runningFold(AppState(), ::appReducer).drop(1).forEach(::println)
}
Result
AppState(todos=TodosState(titles=[Buy milk]), settings=SettingsState(hideDone=false), user=ana)
AppState(todos=TodosState(titles=[Buy milk]), settings=SettingsState(hideDone=true), user=ana)
AppState(todos=TodosState(titles=[]), settings=SettingsState(hideDone=false), user=null)

Selecting derived state without recomputing everything

`map` the inputs, `distinctUntilChanged`, then compute: unrelated state changes reach neither the computation nor the UI.

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.*

data class Todo(val title: String, val done: Boolean = false)
data class TodosState(val todos: List<Todo> = emptyList(), val hideDone: Boolean = false,
                      val syncing: Boolean = false)

// Selectors: small pure functions of state
fun openCount(state: TodosState) = state.todos.count { !it.done }
var visibleComputations = 0
fun visibleTodos(todos: List<Todo>, hideDone: Boolean): List<String> {
    visibleComputations++                                     // imagine sorting and grouping 5 000 rows
    return todos.filter { !hideDone || !it.done }.map { it.title }
}

@OptIn(ExperimentalCoroutinesApi::class)
fun main() = runTest {
    val state = MutableStateFlow(TodosState(listOf(Todo("Buy milk"), Todo("Book flights"))))   // store state

    val badge = state.map(::openCount).distinctUntilChanged()    // emits only when the number changes
    val visible = state
        .map { it.todos to it.hideDone }                         // pick the inputs...
        .distinctUntilChanged()                                  // ...and recompute only when they change
        .map { (todos, hideDone) -> visibleTodos(todos, hideDone) }
        .distinctUntilChanged()                                  // same rows: do not re-render

    val ui = UnconfinedTestDispatcher(testScheduler)
    backgroundScope.launch(ui) { badge.collect { println("badge: $it") } }
    backgroundScope.launch(ui) { visible.collect { println("list: $it") } }

    state.update { it.copy(syncing = true) }                     // unrelated field: nothing re-renders
    state.update { it.copy(todos = listOf(Todo("Buy milk", done = true), Todo("Book flights"))) }
    state.update { it.copy(hideDone = true) }                    // the list changes, the badge does not
    state.update { it.copy(syncing = false) }
    println("5 states, list computed $visibleComputations times")
}
Result
badge: 2
list: [Buy milk, Book flights]
badge: 1
list: [Book flights]
5 states, list computed 3 times

Testing the reducer — a plain function

The reducer needs no coroutines, no fakes and no store: give it a state and an action, check the state and the effects it returns.

data class TodosState(val titles: List<String> = emptyList(), val loading: Boolean = false,
                      val error: String? = null)

sealed interface TodosAction {
    data object Opened : TodosAction
    data class Loaded(val titles: List<String>) : TodosAction
    data class LoadFailed(val message: String?) : TodosAction
}

fun reduce(state: TodosState, action: TodosAction): Pair<TodosState, List<String>> = when (action) {
    TodosAction.Opened -> state.copy(loading = true, error = null) to listOf("/todos")
    is TodosAction.Loaded -> TodosState(titles = action.titles) to emptyList()
    is TodosAction.LoadFailed -> state.copy(loading = false, error = action.message) to emptyList()
}

fun main() {                                                // no coroutines, no fakes: input -> output
    val (opened, effects) = reduce(TodosState(error = "old"), TodosAction.Opened)
    check(opened == TodosState(loading = true)) { "$opened" }        // a retry clears the old error
    check(effects == listOf("/todos")) { "$effects" }                // and asks for exactly one fetch

    val (failed, none) = reduce(opened, TodosAction.LoadFailed("offline"))
    check(failed == TodosState(error = "offline") && none.isEmpty()) { "$failed" }

    val (loaded, _) = reduce(failed, TodosAction.Loaded(listOf("Buy milk")))
    check(loaded == TodosState(titles = listOf("Buy milk"))) { "$loaded" }
    println("reducer tests passed")
}
Result
reducer tests passed

Testing an effect — success, failure and cancellation

Call the effect runner the store uses with a fake dependency, and check that a failure comes back as an action while a cancellation does not.

import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest
import java.io.IOException

sealed interface TodosAction {
    data class Loaded(val titles: List<String>) : TodosAction
    data class LoadFailed(val message: String?) : TodosAction
}

fun interface TodoApi { suspend fun titles(): List<String> }

// The effect runner the store calls: its dependency comes in through the constructor
class TodoEffects(private val api: TodoApi) {
    suspend fun fetchTodos(): TodosAction = try {
        TodosAction.Loaded(api.titles())
    } catch (e: IOException) {                          // only what the API throws: never Exception
        TodosAction.LoadFailed(e.message)
    }
}

fun main() = runTest {
    val ok = TodoEffects { delay(2_000); listOf("Buy milk") }.fetchTodos()
    check(ok == TodosAction.Loaded(listOf("Buy milk"))) { "$ok" }

    val failed = TodoEffects { throw IOException("offline") }.fetchTodos()
    check(failed == TodosAction.LoadFailed("offline")) { "$failed" }   // a failure is an action, not a throw

    var result: TodosAction? = null
    val job = launch { result = TodoEffects { awaitCancellation() }.fetchTodos() }
    delay(100)
    job.cancel()                                         // the store cancels it: a newer fetch won
    job.join()
    check(result == null) { "cancellation turned into $result" }       // not reported as a failed load
    println("effect tests passed")
}
Result
effect tests passed

When a library earns its place

The hand-rolled store above is enough for most screens; reach for a library for tooling, multiplatform reach, or team-wide conventions.

OptionWhat it gives youEarns its place whenCost
Hand-rolled (this sheet)a reducer, a store, effects as dataone app, a few screens, a team that reads the 30 linesyou write cancellation, logging and test helpers yourself
Orbit MVIan OrbitContainerHost with orbitContainer(initial) (Orbit 12; ContainerHost / container before); intent { reduce { … }; postSideEffect(…) }; an orbit-test moduleyou want MVI on existing ViewModels with little ceremony; Kotlin Multiplatformthe reducer is a lambda inside the intent, not a standalone pure function
MVIKotlina Store of intents, state and labels (one-off outputs), with logging and time-travel debuggingseveral platforms share stores; you want time travel and strict layeringmore types per feature; its own lifecycle and binding APIs
Molecule (Cash App)a @Composable function that produces a StateFlow (launchMolecule, moleculeFlow) — no Compose UIpresenters already think in Compose state; you want if/LaunchedEffect instead of operatorsneeds the Compose compiler plugin in that module; recomposition rules apply to business logic

Rules and pitfalls

What goes wrong in a home-grown store.

  • I/O, delay or launch inside the reducer: it stops being pure, and the order of actions no longer explains the state.
  • An effect that writes _state directly: two writers race, and the action log lies. Effects send actions.
  • runCatching { } around a suspending effect swallows CancellationException, so a cancelled search still reports "failed". Catch the I/O exceptions you expect.
  • One action loop per store (a Channel read by one coroutine); update { } is enough only for a reducer with no effects, because its lambda may run more than once.
  • Give every long-running effect an id, and cancel by id: search, polling, a timer started and stopped by actions.
  • Catch an effect's expected failure (IOException, never Exception) in the store or the runner and send it as an action: an uncaught one crashes the app in viewModelScope and kills the loop in a plain Job scope.
  • Cancelling a Job does not recall an action it already sent — tag results with the query or request id they were computed for.
  • One-off outputs (navigate, show a snackbar) are state too: put them in State and clear them with an action once the UI has acted — see MVVM — ViewModel, UiState & Events.

Networking — REST with Ktor, OkHttp & Retrofit

Which client to pick, typed GET and POST as suspend functions with kotlinx.serialization, a sealed error type, timeouts, cancellation and retry, single-flight token refresh, pagination as a Flow, ETags, progress, and the same calls with Ktor, OkHttp and Retrofit.

Which HTTP client

On Android pick Retrofit or Ktor over OkHttp; on a JVM backend or a script, the JDK client is already there.

ClientWhat it isCoroutinesReach for it when
OkHttp 5the HTTP engine: connection pool, HTTP/2, TLS, cache, interceptors, Authenticatorokhttp-coroutines adds executeAsync()you need the transport underneath Retrofit or Ktor, or raw control
Retrofit 3a typed interface over OkHttp, generated at run timesuspend methods in the interfacean Android app talking to one REST API; the most common choice
Ktor client 3a multiplatform client with plugins (ContentNegotiation, Auth, HttpTimeout, HttpRequestRetry)suspend all the way downKotlin Multiplatform, or you prefer code over annotations; runs on the OkHttp or CIO engine
java.net.http.HttpClientthe JDK's client (JDK 11+), HTTP/2, sendAsync returns a CompletableFuturesendAsync(…).await() from kotlinx.coroutines.futureJVM services, tools and tests — not on Android
HttpURLConnectionthe legacy built-in clientblocking onlynever in new code

A typed GET and POST

Send `Accept` and `Content-Type`, give every request a timeout, and check the status before you decode the body.

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
import java.net.*
import java.net.http.*
import java.time.Duration
import kotlinx.coroutines.future.await
import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking
import kotlinx.serialization.*
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json

@Serializable data class Order(val id: String, val totalCents: Long)
@Serializable data class NewOrder(val sku: String, val quantity: Int)

class OrdersApi(private val base: URI, private val http: HttpClient) {
    private val json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }      // tolerate fields the server adds later

    suspend fun order(id: String): Order = send(HttpRequest.newBuilder(base.resolve("orders/$id")))

    suspend fun create(order: NewOrder): Order = send(
        HttpRequest.newBuilder(base.resolve("orders")).header("Content-Type", "application/json")
            .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString(json.encodeToString(order))))

    private suspend inline fun <reified T> send(builder: HttpRequest.Builder): T {
        val request = builder.header("Accept", "application/json").timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10)).build()
        val response = http.sendAsync(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString()).await()
        check(response.statusCode() in 200..299) { "HTTP ${response.statusCode()}" }   // not an IOException
        return json.decodeFromString(response.body())
    }
}

fun main() = runBlocking {
    val server = HttpServer.create(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0)
    server.createContext("/orders") { ex ->
        if (ex.requestMethod == "POST") println("server got ${ex.requestHeaders.getFirst("Content-Type")}")
        val body = if (ex.requestMethod == "POST") """{"id":"A-1042","totalCents":2598,"currency":"EUR"}"""
            else """{"id":"A-1041","totalCents":1299}"""
        ex.sendResponseHeaders(if (ex.requestMethod == "POST") 201 else 200, body.length.toLong())
        ex.responseBody.use { it.write(body.encodeToByteArray()) }
    }
    server.start()

    HttpClient.newHttpClient().use { http ->
        val api = OrdersApi(URI("http://127.0.0.1:${server.address.port}/"), http)
        println(api.order("A-1041"))
        println(api.create(NewOrder("BOOK-7", 2)))
    }
    server.stop(0)
}
Result
Order(id=A-1041, totalCents=1299)
server got application/json
Order(id=A-1042, totalCents=2598)
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc), JDK 21 or later (HttpClient is AutoCloseable from 21), kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm-1.10.2.jar, kotlinx-serialization-core-jvm-1.13.0.jar and kotlinx-serialization-json-jvm-1.13.0.jar

A sealed error type the screen can `when` over

Map every failure — transport, status, body — onto one sealed hierarchy at the client's edge, so each screen handles all of them and nothing else.

import java.io.IOException
import kotlinx.serialization.*
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json

@Serializable data class Order(val id: String, val totalCents: Long)

sealed class ApiError(cause: Throwable? = null) : Exception(cause) {
    data class Http(val status: Int) : ApiError()
    data class Network(val reason: String?) : ApiError()
    class Decoding(cause: SerializationException) : ApiError(cause)
}

suspend fun fetchOrder(id: String, get: suspend (path: String) -> Pair<Int, String>): Order {
    val (status, body) = try {
        get("orders/$id")                                 // the transport: java.net.http, OkHttp, Ktor
    } catch (e: IOException) {                          // refused, reset, HttpTimeoutException
        throw ApiError.Network(e.message)
    }
    if (status !in 200..299) throw ApiError.Http(status)
    return try {
        Json.decodeFromString<Order>(body)
    } catch (e: SerializationException) {              // e.g. a captive portal's HTML with a 200
        throw ApiError.Decoding(e)
    }
}

fun userMessage(error: ApiError): String = when (error) {   // exhaustive: no else branch
    is ApiError.Http -> if (error.status == 404) "No such order." else "Server error ${error.status}."
    is ApiError.Network -> "Check your connection."
    is ApiError.Decoding -> "Unexpected response. Try again later."
}

suspend fun main() {
    val replies = mapOf(
        "orders/A-9999" to (404 to """{"error":"not_found"}"""),
        "orders/A-1042" to (200 to "<html>Sign in to the café Wi-Fi</html>"),
    )
    for (id in listOf("A-9999", "A-1042", "A-1043")) {
        try {
            fetchOrder(id) { path -> replies[path] ?: throw IOException("Connection refused") }
        } catch (e: ApiError) {
            println("$id: ${e::class.simpleName} → ${userMessage(e)}")
        }
    }
}
Result
A-9999: Http → No such order.
A-1042: Decoding → Unexpected response. Try again later.
A-1043: Network → Check your connection.

Timeouts, cancellation and retry with backoff

Wrap only idempotent calls (GET, PUT, DELETE, or a POST with an `Idempotency-Key`); time out each attempt with `withTimeoutOrNull`, honour a capped `Retry-After`, and let every cancellation — the caller's timeout included — pass untouched.

import java.io.IOException
import kotlinx.coroutines.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.test.*

class HttpStatusException(val status: Int, val retryAfterMs: Long? = null) : IOException("HTTP $status")
class AttemptTimeoutException(ms: Long) : IOException("attempt timed out after $ms ms")

private val retryable = setOf(408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504)
private const val MAX_WAIT_MS = 10_000L

suspend fun <T : Any> withRetry(maxAttempts: Int = 5, timeoutMs: Long = 2_000, call: suspend (Int) -> T): T {
    var backoffMs = 200L
    for (attempt in 1..maxAttempts) {
        val waitMs = try {
            // withTimeoutOrNull returns null only for OUR timeout; the caller's cancellation still throws.
            return withTimeoutOrNull(timeoutMs) { call(attempt) } ?: throw AttemptTimeoutException(timeoutMs)
        } catch (e: IOException) {                         // refused, reset, HttpTimeoutException, 5xx, ours
            if (attempt == maxAttempts || (e is HttpStatusException && e.status !in retryable)) throw e
            (e as? HttpStatusException)?.retryAfterMs ?: backoffMs
        }
        delay(minOf(waitMs, MAX_WAIT_MS))                  // production: add jitter to the backoff
        backoffMs *= 2
    }
    error("unreachable")
}

fun main() = runTest {
    val order = withRetry { attempt ->
        println("t=${currentTime}ms attempt $attempt")
        when (attempt) {
            1 -> awaitCancellation()                         // the server hangs
            2 -> throw IOException("Connection refused")
            3 -> throw HttpStatusException(503, retryAfterMs = 120_000)   // honoured, but capped
            else -> "order A-1041"
        }
    }
    println("t=${currentTime}ms got $order")

    val screen = launch { withRetry { throw HttpStatusException(503) } }
    delay(300)                                             // the user leaves during a back-off
    screen.cancelAndJoin()
    println("t=${currentTime}ms cancelled=${screen.isCancelled}")

    val gaveUp = runCatching { withTimeout(1_500) { withRetry(maxAttempts = 1) { awaitCancellation() } } }
    println("caller's own withTimeout: ${gaveUp.exceptionOrNull()?.javaClass?.simpleName}")
}
Result
t=0ms attempt 1
t=2200ms attempt 2
t=2600ms attempt 3
t=12600ms attempt 4
t=12600ms got order A-1041
t=12900ms cancelled=true
caller's own withTimeout: TimeoutCancellationException

Reading Retry-After in both forms

`Retry-After` is either delta-seconds or an HTTP-date; turn both into a wait against an injected clock, cap it without overflowing, treat a past date as now and anything else as no hint.

import java.time.*
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter

/** Retry-After as delta-seconds ("120") or an IMF-fixdate; null when unreadable, capped otherwise. */
fun retryAfterMs(header: String?, now: Instant, maxMs: Long = 10_000): Long? {
    val value = header?.trim() ?: return null
    if (value.isNotEmpty() && value.all { it in '0'..'9' }) {             // delta-seconds: digits only
        val seconds = value.toLongOrNull() ?: Long.MAX_VALUE             // too long for a Long: just huge
        return if (seconds > maxMs / 1_000) maxMs else seconds * 1_000   // no overflow on the way to the cap
    }
    val date = runCatching { ZonedDateTime.parse(value, DateTimeFormatter.RFC_1123_DATE_TIME) }.getOrNull()
        ?: return null                                                   // "-5", "soon": not a Retry-After
    return Duration.between(now, date.toInstant()).toMillis().coerceIn(0, maxMs)   // a past date means now
}

fun main() {
    val now = Instant.parse("2026-11-16T10:00:00Z")                  // an injected clock in the app
    val headers = listOf("3", "120", "9223372036854775807", "-5", "Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:00:05 GMT",
        "Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:00:00 GMT", "soon")
    for (header in headers) println("Retry-After: $header → wait ${retryAfterMs(header, now)} ms")
}
Result
Retry-After: 3 → wait 3000 ms
Retry-After: 120 → wait 10000 ms
Retry-After: 9223372036854775807 → wait 10000 ms
Retry-After: -5 → wait null ms
Retry-After: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:00:05 GMT → wait 5000 ms
Retry-After: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:00:00 GMT → wait 0 ms
Retry-After: soon → wait null ms

Cancelling a java.net.http transfer for real

`await()` cancels the JDK's future with `cancel(false)`, which leaves the transfer running; `cancel(true)` from `invokeOnCancellation` aborts it — the demo cancels only once the server signals the transfer started.

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
import java.net.*
import java.net.http.*
import java.util.concurrent.CompletionException
import kotlinx.coroutines.*

suspend fun <T> HttpClient.sendCancellable(request: HttpRequest, handler: HttpResponse.BodyHandler<T>) =
    suspendCancellableCoroutine<HttpResponse<T>> { cont ->
        val future = sendAsync(request, handler)
        cont.invokeOnCancellation { future.cancel(true) }        // await() uses cancel(false): no abort
        future.whenComplete { response, error ->
            if (error == null) cont.resumeWith(Result.success(response))
            else cont.resumeWith(Result.failure((error as? CompletionException)?.cause ?: error))
        }
    }

fun main() = runBlocking {
    val started = CompletableDeferred<Unit>()
    val outcome = CompletableDeferred<String>()
    val server = HttpServer.create(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0).apply { start() }
    server.createContext("/csv") { ex ->
        ex.sendResponseHeaders(200, 320L * 65_536)                   // 20 MB, sent slowly
        started.complete(Unit)
        outcome.complete(runCatching {
            repeat(320) {
                ex.responseBody.write(ByteArray(65_536))
                Thread.sleep(10)
            }
        }.fold({ "sent all 20 MB" }, { "stopped: the client is gone" }))
    }
    try {
        HttpClient.newHttpClient().use { http ->
            val request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI("http://127.0.0.1:${server.address.port}/csv")).build()
            val download = launch { http.sendCancellable(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofByteArray()) }
            withTimeoutOrNull(3_000) { started.await() }             // cancel only once the transfer runs
            download.cancelAndJoin()                                 // the user leaves the screen
            println("download cancelled; the server ${withTimeoutOrNull(2_000) { outcome.await() }}")
        }
    } finally {
        server.stop(0)                                               // also when a wait timed out
    }
}
Result
download cancelled; the server stopped: the client is gone

Bearer auth with a single-flight refresh behind a Mutex

When several requests hit 401 at once, one refresh runs in the store's own scope and every waiting caller shares its result; once it ends, the next 401 may try again.

import kotlinx.coroutines.*

class TokenStore(initial: String, private val scope: CoroutineScope, // the store's scope, not a caller's
                 private val refresh: suspend () -> String) {
    @Volatile var accessToken: String = initial                     // also set at sign-in
    private var inFlight: Deferred<String>? = null

    suspend fun refreshAfter(rejected: String): String? {             // null: that refresh failed
        val shared = synchronized(this) {
            if (accessToken != rejected) return accessToken            // already refreshed
            inFlight ?: scope.async { refresh().also { accessToken = it } }.also { job ->
                inFlight = job
                job.invokeOnCompletion { synchronized(this) { inFlight = null } }   // next 401: a new one
            }
        }
        return try {
            shared.await()
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive()                   // our caller left: rethrow that
            null                                                        // this refresh failed
        }
    }
}

fun main() = runBlocking {
    val scenarios = mapOf<String, List<suspend () -> String>>(
        "refresh works" to listOf({ "fresh" }),
        "network down" to listOf({ throw java.io.IOException("connection reset") }, { "fresh" }),
        "refresh rejected" to listOf({ error("400 invalid_grant") }),
    )
    for ((label, replies) in scenarios) {
        val pending = ArrayDeque(replies)
        var calls = 0
        val store = TokenStore("expired", CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob())) {
            calls++
            delay(50)                                               // three 401s arrive meanwhile
            pending.removeFirst()()
        }
        val tokens = List(3) { async { store.refreshAfter("expired") ?: "401" } }.awaitAll()
        println("$label: $tokens, token endpoint calls=$calls")
        if (pending.isNotEmpty()) println("  network back: ${store.refreshAfter("expired")}, calls=$calls")
    }
}
Result
refresh works: [fresh, fresh, fresh], token endpoint calls=1
network down: [401, 401, 401], token endpoint calls=1
  network back: fresh, calls=2
refresh rejected: [401, 401, 401], token endpoint calls=1

One caller leaving does not cancel the shared refresh

Because the refresh is a `Deferred` in the store's scope, cancelling the caller that started it leaves the others with their new token and still one call to the token endpoint.

import kotlinx.coroutines.*

class TokenStore(initial: String, private val scope: CoroutineScope, // the store's scope, not a caller's
                 private val refresh: suspend () -> String) {
    @Volatile var accessToken: String = initial                     // also set at sign-in
    private var inFlight: Deferred<String>? = null

    suspend fun refreshAfter(rejected: String): String? {             // null: that refresh failed
        val shared = synchronized(this) {
            if (accessToken != rejected) return accessToken            // already refreshed
            inFlight ?: scope.async { refresh().also { accessToken = it } }.also { job ->
                inFlight = job
                job.invokeOnCompletion { synchronized(this) { inFlight = null } }   // next 401: a new one
            }
        }
        return try {
            shared.await()
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive()                   // our caller left: rethrow that
            null                                                        // this refresh failed
        }
    }
}

suspend fun authorizedGet(tokens: TokenStore, send: suspend (token: String) -> Int): Int {
    val token = tokens.accessToken
    val status = send(token)
    if (status != 401) return status
    return tokens.refreshAfter(token)?.let { send(it) } ?: 401       // retry once, or 401: signed out
}

fun main() = runBlocking {
    var calls = 0
    val store = TokenStore("expired", CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob())) {
        calls++
        delay(50)                                                   // the token endpoint is slow
        "fresh"
    }
    val requests = List(3) { async { authorizedGet(store) { token -> if (token == "fresh") 200 else 401 } } }
    yield()                                                         // all three now wait on one refresh
    requests[0].cancel()                                            // the user leaves that screen
    val others = requests.drop(1).awaitAll()
    println("first cancelled: ${requests[0].isCancelled}, others: $others, token endpoint calls=$calls")
}
Result
first cancelled: true, others: [200, 200], token endpoint calls=1

Cursor pagination as a Flow

A cold `flow { }` fetches the next page only when the collector wants more, so `take(5)` costs two requests, not every page.

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
import java.net.*
import java.net.http.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.future.await
import kotlinx.serialization.*
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json

@Serializable data class Order(val id: String)
@Serializable data class Page(val items: List<Order>, val nextCursor: String? = null)

fun orders(http: HttpClient, base: String): Flow<Order> = flow {
    var cursor: String? = null
    do {
        val query = "limit=3" + (cursor?.let { "&after=${URLEncoder.encode(it, Charsets.UTF_8)}" } ?: "")
        val request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI("$base/orders?$query")).build()
        val response = http.sendAsync(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString()).await()
        check(response.statusCode() == 200) { "HTTP ${response.statusCode()}" }
        val page = Json.decodeFromString<Page>(response.body())
        emitAll(page.items.asFlow())
        cursor = page.nextCursor
    } while (cursor != null)
}

suspend fun main() {
    val all = (1041..1047).map { Order("A-$it") }
    val server = HttpServer.create(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0)
    server.createContext("/orders") { ex ->
        println("server: ${ex.requestURI.query}")
        val start = all.indexOfFirst { it.id == ex.requestURI.query.substringAfter("after=", "") } + 1
        val items = all.drop(start).take(3)
        val body = Json.encodeToString(Page(items, items.last().id.takeIf { start + 3 < all.size }))
        ex.sendResponseHeaders(200, body.length.toLong())
        ex.responseBody.use { it.write(body.encodeToByteArray()) }
    }
    server.start()

    HttpClient.newHttpClient().use { http ->
        val base = "http://127.0.0.1:${server.address.port}"
        println(orders(http, base).take(5).map { it.id }.toList())
        println("all: ${orders(http, base).count()}")
    }
    server.stop(0)
}

[A-1041, A-1042, A-1043, A-1044, A-1045]

Caching with ETag and If-None-Match

Send back the ETag you stored; a `304 Not Modified` has no body, so you reuse the cached one — OkHttp's `Cache` does this for you.

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
import java.net.*
import java.net.http.*

data class Cached(val etag: String, val body: String)

fun getCached(http: HttpClient, uri: URI, cache: MutableMap<URI, Cached>): String {
    val cached = cache[uri]
    val request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(uri).apply { cached?.let { header("If-None-Match", it.etag) } }
    val response = http.send(request.build(), HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString())
    if (response.statusCode() == 304) return "304, cached: ${cached!!.body}"
    check(response.statusCode() == 200) { "HTTP ${response.statusCode()}" }
    response.headers().firstValue("ETag").ifPresent { cache[uri] = Cached(it, response.body()) }
    return "200: ${response.body()}"
}

fun main() {
    var catalog = """["BOOK-7","PEN-2"]"""
    val server = HttpServer.create(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0)
    server.createContext("/catalog") { ex ->
        val etag = "\"${catalog.hashCode().toUInt().toString(16)}\""     // a version of the representation
        ex.responseHeaders.add("ETag", etag)
        ex.responseHeaders.add("Cache-Control", "no-cache")            // store it, but revalidate each time
        if (ex.requestHeaders.getFirst("If-None-Match") == etag) {
            ex.sendResponseHeaders(304, -1)                            // -1: no body
            ex.close()
        } else {
            ex.sendResponseHeaders(200, catalog.length.toLong())
            ex.responseBody.use { it.write(catalog.encodeToByteArray()) }
        }
    }
    server.start()

    val cache = mutableMapOf<URI, Cached>()                            // on disk in an app
    val uri = URI("http://127.0.0.1:${server.address.port}/catalog")
    HttpClient.newHttpClient().use { http ->
        println(getCached(http, uri, cache))
        println(getCached(http, uri, cache))
        catalog = """["BOOK-7","PEN-2","MUG-1"]"""                     // the server's data changes
        println(getCached(http, uri, cache))
    }
    server.stop(0)
}
Result

304, cached: ["BOOK-7","PEN-2"]
200: ["BOOK-7","PEN-2","MUG-1"]

Download with progress, checked

Check the status before you write a byte, report progress against `Content-Length`, and show an indeterminate bar when a chunked response has none.

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
import java.io.*
import java.net.*
import java.net.http.*

class CountingInputStream(input: InputStream, private val onRead: (Long) -> Unit) : FilterInputStream(input) {
    private var count = 0L
    override fun read(b: ByteArray, off: Int, len: Int): Int = super.read(b, off, len).also {
        if (it > 0) count += it
        onRead(count)
    }
}

fun download(http: HttpClient, uri: URI, target: OutputStream, onProgress: (percent: Long?) -> Unit): Long {
    val response = http.send(HttpRequest.newBuilder(uri).build(), HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofInputStream())
    return response.body().use { body ->
        if (response.statusCode() != 200) throw IOException("HTTP ${response.statusCode()}")   // not the file
        val total = response.headers().firstValueAsLong("Content-Length").orElse(-1).takeIf { it > 0 }
        CountingInputStream(body) { done -> onProgress(total?.let { done * 100 / it }) }.copyTo(target)
    }
}

fun main() {
    val server = HttpServer.create(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0)
    server.createContext("/files/") { ex ->
        val path = ex.requestURI.path
        ex.sendResponseHeaders(if ("missing" in path) 404 else 200, if ("receipt" in path) 262_144L else 0)
        ex.responseBody.use { if ("missing" !in path) it.write(ByteArray(262_144)) }    // length 0: chunked
    }
    server.start()

    val base = "http://127.0.0.1:${server.address.port}/files"
    val sink = ByteArrayOutputStream()                     // a file's output stream in the app
    HttpClient.newHttpClient().use { http ->
        for (name in listOf("receipt.pdf", "export.pdf", "missing.pdf")) {
            var bar = ""
            val result = runCatching {
                download(http, URI("$base/$name"), sink) { bar = it?.let { "$it%" } ?: "indeterminate" }
            }
            println("$name: " + result.fold({ "$it bytes, bar at $bar" }, { it.message }))
        }
    }
    server.stop(0)
}
Result
receipt.pdf: 262144 bytes, bar at 100%
export.pdf: 262144 bytes, bar at indeterminate
missing.pdf: HTTP 404
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc) and JDK 21 or later (HttpClient is AutoCloseable from 21)
  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar — it serves its own endpoint on 127.0.0.1 and stops it; in an app, call these blocking functions from Dispatchers.IO

Upload with progress

Stream the file through a counting `InputStream` and pass its length, so the server gets `Content-Length` and the user gets a real percentage.

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
import java.io.*
import java.net.*
import java.net.http.*

class CountingInputStream(input: InputStream, private val onRead: (Long) -> Unit) : FilterInputStream(input) {
    private var count = 0L
    override fun read(b: ByteArray, off: Int, len: Int): Int = super.read(b, off, len).also {
        if (it > 0) count += it
        onRead(count)
    }
}

fun upload(http: HttpClient, uri: URI, file: File, onPercent: (Long) -> Unit): Int {
    val body = if (file.length() == 0L) HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.noBody() else {   // fromPublisher: >0
        val stream = HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofInputStream {
            CountingInputStream(file.inputStream()) { read -> onPercent(read * 100 / file.length()) }
        }
        HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.fromPublisher(stream, file.length())             // sets Content-Length
    }
    if (file.length() == 0L) onPercent(100)                       // nothing to send counts as done
    val request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(uri).PUT(body).build()
    return http.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.discarding()).statusCode()
}

fun main() {
    val server = HttpServer.create(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0).apply { start() }
    server.createContext("/") { ex ->
        val received = ex.requestBody.readAllBytes().size
        println("server: Content-Length ${ex.requestHeaders.getFirst("Content-Length")}, received $received")
        ex.use { it.sendResponseHeaders(204, -1) }
    }

    HttpClient.newHttpClient().use { http ->
        for (size in listOf(256 * 1024, 0)) {                    // a receipt, and an empty file
            val file = File.createTempFile("receipt", ".pdf").apply { writeBytes(ByteArray(size)) }
            var shown = -1L                                      // read into the client, not yet acknowledged
            val status = upload(http, URI("http://127.0.0.1:${server.address.port}/"), file) { shown = it }
            println("status $status, progress bar ended at $shown%")
            file.delete()
        }
    }
    server.stop(0)
}
Result
server: Content-Length 262144, received 262144
status 204, progress bar ended at 100%
server: Content-Length 0, received 0
status 204, progress bar ended at 100%

  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar — it serves its own endpoint on 127.0.0.1 and stops it; in an app, call these blocking functions from Dispatchers.IO

The same API with the Ktor client

`expectSuccess` turns non-2xx into exceptions, `HttpRequestRetry` retries idempotent calls, and the `Auth` plugin refreshes once — returning `null` signs the user out.

fun ordersClient(tokens: TokenStorage, json: Json) = HttpClient(OkHttp) {
    expectSuccess = true                          // 4xx: ClientRequestException, 5xx: ServerResponseException
    install(ContentNegotiation) { json(json) }
    install(HttpRequestRetry) {                   // before HttpTimeout; requests can opt out with noRetry()
        retryOnExceptionOrServerErrors(maxRetries = 3)
        exponentialDelay()
    }
    install(HttpTimeout) {
        requestTimeoutMillis = 10_000
        connectTimeoutMillis = 5_000
    }
    install(Auth) {
        bearer {
            loadTokens { tokens.load()?.let { BearerTokens(it.access, it.refresh) } }
            refreshTokens {                       // called once for concurrent 401s
                val refreshToken = oldTokens?.refreshToken ?: return@refreshTokens null
                try {
                    val form = parametersOf("grant_type" to listOf("refresh_token"),
                        "refresh_token" to listOf(refreshToken))
                    val fresh: TokenResponse = client.submitForm("https://auth.example.com/token", form) {
                        markAsRefreshTokenRequest()                   // never itself refreshed
                    }.body()
                    tokens.save(fresh.accessToken, fresh.refreshToken)   // the server may rotate it
                    BearerTokens(fresh.accessToken, fresh.refreshToken)
                } catch (e: ResponseException) {      // 400 invalid_grant: the session is over
                    tokens.clear()
                    client.authProvider<BearerAuthProvider>()?.clearToken()   // forget the cached one too
                    null                              // the 401 reaches the caller: show sign-in
                }
            }
        }
    }
    defaultRequest { url("https://api.example.com/v1/") }
}

suspend fun HttpClient.order(id: String): Order = get("orders/$id").body()

suspend fun HttpClient.create(order: NewOrder): Order = post("orders") {
    retry { noRetry() }                           // a POST without an Idempotency-Key is never retried
    contentType(ContentType.Application.Json)
    setBody(order)
}.body()
Result

The same typed calls; a 404 throws ClientRequestException with response.status, an expired token is refreshed once and the request replayed, and a refused refresh clears the tokens and surfaces the 401.

Setup

  2. TokenStorage is your own persistence (load, save, clear); Order, NewOrder and TokenResponse are @Serializable; the Json is your app's shared instance; on sign-out elsewhere also call client.authProvider<BearerAuthProvider>()?.clearToken()

OkHttp with a Cache and an Authenticator, Retrofit on top

Configure one `OkHttpClient` for the whole app; Retrofit turns a `suspend` interface into calls on it.

class TokenAuthenticator(private val tokens: TokenStore) : Authenticator {
    // OkHttp calls this on its own thread after a 401; returning null gives up.
    override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
        if (response.priorResponse != null) return null                     // already retried once
        val rejected = response.request.header("Authorization")?.removePrefix("Bearer ") ?: return null
        val fresh = tokens.refreshBlocking(rejected) ?: return null          // null: signed out
        return response.request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $fresh").build()
    }
}

fun okHttp(context: Context, tokens: TokenStore) = OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .cache(Cache(File(context.cacheDir, "http"), 20L * 1024 * 1024))         // honours ETag, Cache-Control
    .addInterceptor { chain ->
        val token = tokens.accessToken
        chain.proceed(chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $token").build())
    }
    .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator(tokens))
    .connectTimeout(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    .callTimeout(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    .build()

interface OrdersService {
    @GET("orders/{id}")
    suspend fun order(@Path("id") id: String): Order                        // HttpException on non-2xx

    @POST("orders")                                                     // retrofit2.Response, not okhttp3's
    suspend fun create(@Body order: NewOrder): retrofit2.Response<Order>
}

private val apiJson = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }

fun ordersService(client: OkHttpClient): OrdersService = Retrofit.Builder()
    .baseUrl("https://api.example.com/v1/")                                 // must end with /
    .client(client)
    .addConverterFactory(apiJson.asConverterFactory("application/json".toMediaType()))
    .build()
    .create(OrdersService::class.java)
Result

ordersService(okHttp(context, tokens)).order("A-1041") suspends off the main thread and returns an Order; GETs are revalidated from the disk cache, and a 401 is retried once with a refreshed token or given up when the refresh failed.

  2. TokenStore is the store from the single-flight card, plus a blocking refreshBlocking(rejected) = runBlocking { refreshAfter(rejected) } for OkHttp's thread

Pitfalls worth saying out loud

The bugs that ship most often in Android networking code.

  • Network on the main thread — Android throws NetworkOnMainThreadException. Call suspend APIs from viewModelScope; wrap blocking calls (OkHttp execute(), HttpClient.send) in withContext(Dispatchers.IO).
  • Leaking response bodies: every OkHttp Response must be closed — response.use { } — or connections leak until the pool starves. Retrofit and Ktor close for you when you read body().
  • Cleartext http:// on Android: blocked by default since API 28. Do not turn on usesCleartextTraffic; allow a dev host only in a debug network_security_config.xml.
  • Catching Exception around a suspend call and swallowing CancellationException — the coroutine keeps running after its screen is gone. Rethrow it, or catch the specific types.
  • Retrying a POST blindly: a timeout does not mean the server did nothing. Retry only idempotent requests, or send an Idempotency-Key header — and opt POSTs out of client-wide retry plugins.
  • One client instance per app (OkHttp, Ktor or the JDK's): it owns the connection pool and cache. Creating one per request throws both away.
  • Cancelling the coroutine cancels Retrofit's and Ktor's call. With java.net.http, await() only stops waiting and HttpRequest.timeout stops at the headers, so a slow body runs on — abort it with future.cancel(true) from invokeOnCancellation (the cancellable-send card).
  • Decode with ignoreUnknownKeys = true for responses, so a server adding a field does not crash old app versions; check the status before decoding.

SOAP: build the envelope and POST it

Escape every value you put in the envelope and send the SOAP 1.1 headers; then read the reply with the next cards' `readSoap()` and `vatCheck()` rather than guessing.

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
import java.net.*
import java.net.http.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.future.await
import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking

const val VIES = "urn:ec.europa.eu:taxud:vies:services:checkVat:types"

fun String.xmlEscaped() = replace("&", "&amp;").replace("<", "&lt;").replace(">", "&gt;")   // element text

fun checkVatEnvelope(country: String, number: String) = """
    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
    <soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:v="$VIES">
      <soap:Body><v:checkVat>
        <v:countryCode>${country.xmlEscaped()}</v:countryCode>
        <v:vatNumber>${number.xmlEscaped()}</v:vatNumber>
      </v:checkVat></soap:Body></soap:Envelope>""".trimIndent()

suspend fun postSoap(http: HttpClient, endpoint: URI, envelope: String): Pair<Int, String> {
    val request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(endpoint)
        .header("Content-Type", "text/xml; charset=utf-8")
        .header("SOAPAction", "\"\"")                          // SOAP 1.1 requires the header, even empty
        .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString(envelope)).build()
    val response = http.sendAsync(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString()).await()
    return response.statusCode() to response.body()
}

fun main() = runBlocking {                                   // postSoap returns raw status and body
    val server = HttpServer.create(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0)
    server.createContext("/checkVatService") { ex ->
        val sent = ex.requestBody.readAllBytes().decodeToString().lines().first { "vatNumber>" in it }
        println("server: ${ex.requestHeaders.getFirst("Content-Type")}, ${sent.trim()}")
        val reply = """<s:Envelope xmlns:s="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"><s:Body>""" +
            """<checkVatResponse xmlns="$VIES"><valid>true</valid></checkVatResponse></s:Body></s:Envelope>"""
        ex.sendResponseHeaders(200, reply.length.toLong())
        ex.responseBody.use { it.write(reply.encodeToByteArray()) }
    }
    server.start()

    HttpClient.newHttpClient().use { http ->
        val endpoint = URI("http://127.0.0.1:${server.address.port}/checkVatService")
        val (status, body) = postSoap(http, endpoint, checkVatEnvelope("DE", "123<456>789"))
        println("HTTP $status, ${body.length} bytes: next, readSoap() and vatCheck()")
    }
    server.stop(0)
}
Result
server: text/xml; charset=utf-8, <v:vatNumber>123&lt;456&gt;789</v:vatNumber>
HTTP 200, 210 bytes: next, readSoap() and vatCheck()
Setup

  3. Or, in a Gradle project: implementation("org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-core:1.10.2")

SOAP: find the Body, and classify a Fault in 1.1 or 1.2

Look for a Fault only in the envelope's Body, never the Header; `Server` (1.1) or `Receiver` (1.2) means the service is down, `Client` or `Sender` means your request is wrong.

import javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory
import org.w3c.dom.Element

const val SOAP11 = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
const val SOAP12 = "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope"

class SoapFault(val serviceDown: Boolean, reason: String) :
    Exception((if (serviceDown) "service down, retry later: " else "our request is wrong: ") + reason)

fun parseXml(xml: String): Element = DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance().apply {
    isNamespaceAware = true
    setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true)   // no DTD: no XXE
    setFeature("http://javax.xml.XMLConstants/feature/secure-processing", true)   // FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING
}.newDocumentBuilder().parse(xml.byteInputStream()).documentElement

fun Element.child(ns: String?, name: String): Element? = generateSequence(firstChild) { it.nextSibling }
    .filterIsInstance<Element>().firstOrNull { it.namespaceURI == ns && it.localName == name }

fun readSoap(status: Int, xml: String): Element {                       // the Body, SOAP 1.1 or 1.2
    val envelope = runCatching { parseXml(xml) }.getOrNull()           // a proxy's HTML, a refused DOCTYPE
    val ns = envelope?.namespaceURI?.takeIf { it == SOAP11 || it == SOAP12 }
    val body = ns?.let { envelope.child(it, "Body") } ?: throw SoapFault(true, "HTTP $status, not SOAP")
    val fault = body.child(ns, "Fault") ?: return body                 // the Body only, never the Header
    val (code, reason) = if (ns == SOAP11) fault.child(null, "faultcode") to fault.child(null, "faultstring")
        else fault.child(ns, "Code")?.child(ns, "Value") to fault.child(ns, "Reason")?.child(ns, "Text")
    val kind = code?.textContent?.trim()?.substringAfter(':')?.substringBefore('.')   // e:Server.Busy: Server
    throw SoapFault(kind != "Client" && kind != "Sender", "$kind: ${reason?.textContent.orEmpty()}")
}

fun env(body: String, header: String = "", ns: String = SOAP11) =
    """<e:Envelope xmlns:e="$ns"><e:Header>$header</e:Header><e:Body>$body</e:Body></e:Envelope>"""
fun fault11(code: String, text: String) = env("<e:Fault>$code<faultstring>$text</faultstring></e:Fault>")
fun fault12(code: String, text: String, sub: String = "") = env(ns = SOAP12, body = "<e:Fault><e:Code>" +
    "<e:Value>e:$code</e:Value>$sub</e:Code><e:Reason><e:Text>$text</e:Text></e:Reason></e:Fault>")

fun main() {
    val replies = listOf(
        200 to env("<checkVatResponse/>", header = "<e:Fault>spoofed in the Header</e:Fault>"),
        500 to fault11("<faultcode>\n  e:Server.Busy </faultcode>", "MS_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQ"),
        500 to fault11("", "MS_UNAVAILABLE"),                              // no faultcode at all
        500 to fault12("Receiver", "MS_UNAVAILABLE", "<e:Subcode><e:Value>e:Busy</e:Value></e:Subcode>"),
        400 to fault12("Sender", "INVALID_INPUT"),
    )
    for ((status, xml) in replies) {
        println(runCatching { "Body: " + readSoap(status, xml).firstChild.localName }.getOrElse { "$it" })
    }
}
Result
Body: checkVatResponse
SoapFault: service down, retry later: Server: MS_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQ
SoapFault: service down, retry later: null: MS_UNAVAILABLE
SoapFault: service down, retry later: Receiver: MS_UNAVAILABLE
SoapFault: our request is wrong: Sender: INVALID_INPUT
Setup

  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar

SOAP: read the answer from the Body, and nothing else

Read the result only inside the Body, accept every `xs:boolean` spelling, and report a missing answer or an unreadable reply as unknown — never as invalid.

import javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory
import org.w3c.dom.Element

const val SOAP11 = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
const val VIES = "urn:ec.europa.eu:taxud:vies:services:checkVat:types"

sealed interface VatCheck {
    data class Valid(val name: String?) : VatCheck
    data object Invalid : VatCheck
    data class Unknown(val reason: String) : VatCheck                    // never tell the user "invalid"
}

fun Element.child(ns: String?, name: String): Element? = generateSequence(firstChild) { it.nextSibling }
    .filterIsInstance<Element>().firstOrNull { it.namespaceURI == ns && it.localName == name }

fun bodyOf(xml: String): Element? = runCatching {
    DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance().apply {
        isNamespaceAware = true
        setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true)   // no DTD: no XXE
        setFeature("http://javax.xml.XMLConstants/feature/secure-processing", true)
    }.newDocumentBuilder().parse(xml.byteInputStream()).documentElement
}.getOrNull()?.takeIf { it.namespaceURI == SOAP11 }?.child(SOAP11, "Body")

fun vatCheck(body: Element?): VatCheck {
    val result = body?.child(VIES, "checkVatResponse") ?: return VatCheck.Unknown("not a checkVatResponse")
    return when (result.child(VIES, "valid")?.textContent?.trim()) {      // xs:boolean: true, false, 1, 0
        "true", "1" -> VatCheck.Valid(result.child(VIES, "name")?.textContent)
        "false", "0" -> VatCheck.Invalid
        else -> VatCheck.Unknown("no <valid> answer")
    }
}

fun reply(header: String, result: String) = """<s:Envelope xmlns:s="$SOAP11" xmlns:v="$VIES">""" +
    "<s:Header>$header</s:Header><s:Body><v:checkVatResponse>$result</v:checkVatResponse></s:Body>" +
    "</s:Envelope>"

fun main() {
    val replies = listOf(
        reply("", "<v:valid>true</v:valid><v:name>Musterfirma GmbH</v:name>"),
        reply("", "<v:valid>1</v:valid>"),
        reply("<v:valid>true</v:valid>", "<v:valid>false</v:valid>"),   // a Header cannot overrule the Body
        reply("", ""),
        "<html><body>502 Bad Gateway</body>",
        """<!DOCTYPE e [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]><e>&x;</e>""",
    )
    for (xml in replies) println(vatCheck(bodyOf(xml)))
}
Result
Valid(name=Musterfirma GmbH)
Valid(name=null)
Invalid
Unknown(reason=no <valid> answer)
Unknown(reason=not a checkVatResponse)
Unknown(reason=not a checkVatResponse)

GraphQL: a typed query with variables over HTTP

Send values as typed `variables` — a `@Serializable` class keeps `Boolean!` a boolean — never by building the query string.

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
import java.net.*
import java.net.http.*
import kotlinx.serialization.*
import kotlinx.serialization.json.*

@Serializable data class GraphQLRequest<V>(val query: String, val variables: V)
@Serializable data class GraphQLError(val message: String)
@Serializable data class GraphQLResponse<D>(val data: D? = null, val errors: List<GraphQLError> = emptyList())
@Serializable data class OrderVars(val id: String, val withTracking: Boolean)     // typed: ID!, Boolean!
@Serializable data class OrderData(val order: Order?)
@Serializable data class Order(val id: String, val status: String, val trackingNumber: String? = null)

const val ORDER_QUERY = "query OrderById(\$id: ID!, \$withTracking: Boolean!) " +
    "{ order(id: \$id) { id status trackingNumber @include(if: \$withTracking) } }"
val json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }

fun order(http: HttpClient, endpoint: URI, vars: OrderVars): GraphQLResponse<OrderData> {
    val body = json.encodeToString(GraphQLRequest(ORDER_QUERY, vars))    // values as JSON, not in the query
    val request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(endpoint).header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        .header("Accept", "application/graphql-response+json, application/json")
        .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString(body)).build()
    val response = http.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString())        // Dispatchers.IO in an app
    return json.decodeFromString(response.body())               // a non-2xx status: the next card
}

fun main() {
    val server = HttpServer.create(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0)
    server.createContext("/graphql") { ex ->
        val sent = json.parseToJsonElement(ex.requestBody.readAllBytes().decodeToString())
        println("server: variables ${sent.jsonObject["variables"]}")
        val reply = """{"data":{"order":{"id":"A-1041","status":"SHIPPED","trackingNumber":"1Z999"}}}"""
        ex.responseHeaders.add("Content-Type", "application/graphql-response+json")
        ex.sendResponseHeaders(200, reply.length.toLong())
        ex.responseBody.use { it.write(reply.encodeToByteArray()) }
    }
    server.start()

    HttpClient.newHttpClient().use { http ->
        val endpoint = URI("http://127.0.0.1:${server.address.port}/graphql")
        println(order(http, endpoint, OrderVars("A-1041", withTracking = true)))
    }
    server.stop(0)
}

GraphQL: a 4xx can still be a GraphQL answer

Under `application/graphql-response+json` a request error comes as a `4xx` that still carries `errors`, so decode the body; anything else that is not `2xx` is a transport error.

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer
import java.net.*
import java.net.http.*
import kotlinx.serialization.*
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json

const val GQL = "application/graphql-response+json"

@Serializable data class GraphQLError(val message: String)
@Serializable data class GraphQLResponse<D>(val data: D? = null, val errors: List<GraphQLError> = emptyList())
@Serializable data class OrderData(val order: Order?)
@Serializable data class Order(val id: String, val status: String)

fun graphQLResult(response: HttpResponse<String>): GraphQLResponse<OrderData> {
    val graphQL = response.headers().firstValue("Content-Type").orElse("").startsWith(GQL)
    check(response.statusCode() in 200..299 || graphQL) { "HTTP ${response.statusCode()}: not GraphQL" }
    return Json.decodeFromString(response.body())
}

fun main() {
    val replies = ArrayDeque(listOf(
        Triple(400, GQL, """{"errors":[{"message":"Cannot query field \"tracking\" on type \"Order\"."}]}"""),
        Triple(422, GQL, """{"errors":[{"message":"Variable \"${'$'}id\" got invalid value 42."}]}"""),
        Triple(502, "text/html", "<html>Bad Gateway</html>"),
    ))
    val server = HttpServer.create(InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0)
    server.createContext("/graphql") { ex ->
        val (status, type, reply) = replies.removeFirst()
        ex.responseHeaders.add("Content-Type", type)
        ex.sendResponseHeaders(status, reply.length.toLong())
        ex.responseBody.use { it.write(reply.encodeToByteArray()) }
    }
    server.start()

    HttpClient.newHttpClient().use { http ->
        val query = """{"query":"{ order(id: \"A-1041\") { id status } }"}"""
        val request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI("http://127.0.0.1:${server.address.port}/graphql"))
            .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString(query)).build()
        repeat(3) {
            val response = http.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString())
            println(runCatching { graphQLResult(response) }.getOrElse { "transport error: ${it.message}" })
        }
    }
    server.stop(0)
}
Result
GraphQLResponse(data=null, errors=[GraphQLError(message=Cannot query field "tracking" on type "Order".)])
GraphQLResponse(data=null, errors=[GraphQLError(message=Variable "$id" got invalid value 42.)])
transport error: HTTP 502: not GraphQL

GraphQL: a mutation, and errors beside data

Read `errors` next to `data`: a field can fail while the rest of the response is fine, and the error's `path` says which one.

import kotlinx.serialization.*
import kotlinx.serialization.json.*

// mutation CancelOrder($id: ID!, $reason: String!) { cancelOrder(id: $id, reason: $reason) { id status } }

@Serializable
data class GraphQLError(
    val message: String,
    val path: List<JsonElement> = emptyList(),
    val extensions: JsonObject? = null,
)

@Serializable data class GraphQLResponse<D>(val data: D? = null, val errors: List<GraphQLError> = emptyList())
@Serializable data class CancelData(val cancelOrder: CancelledOrder?)
@Serializable data class CancelledOrder(val id: String, val status: String)

sealed interface CancelResult {
    data class Cancelled(val order: CancelledOrder) : CancelResult
    data class Rejected(val code: String, val message: String) : CancelResult   // a field error
    data class Failed(val messages: List<String>) : CancelResult                // a request error: no data
}

fun interpret(response: GraphQLResponse<CancelData>): CancelResult {
    response.data?.cancelOrder?.let { return CancelResult.Cancelled(it) }
    val fieldError = response.errors.firstOrNull { it.path.firstOrNull() == JsonPrimitive("cancelOrder") }
    if (response.data == null || fieldError == null) {
        return CancelResult.Failed(response.errors.map { it.message })
    }
    val code = fieldError.extensions?.get("code")?.jsonPrimitive?.content ?: "UNKNOWN"
    return CancelResult.Rejected(code, fieldError.message)
}

fun main() {
    val replies = listOf(
        """{"data":{"cancelOrder":{"id":"A-1042","status":"CANCELLED"}}}""",
        """{"data":{"cancelOrder":null},"errors":[{"message":"Order A-1041 has already shipped",""" +
            """"path":["cancelOrder"],"extensions":{"code":"FAILED_PRECONDITION"}}]}""",
        """{"errors":[{"message":""" +
            """"Variable \"${'$'}reason\" of required type \"String!\" was not provided."}]}""",
    )
    for (reply in replies) println(interpret(Json.decodeFromString(reply)))
}
Result
Cancelled(order=CancelledOrder(id=A-1042, status=CANCELLED))
Rejected(code=FAILED_PRECONDITION, message=Order A-1041 has already shipped)
Failed(messages=[Variable "$reason" of required type "String!" was not provided.])

GraphQL with Apollo Kotlin, in outline

Apollo generates a typed class per operation from your `.graphql` files and the schema — no hand-written models, no string queries.

// src/main/graphql/Orders.graphql
//   query OrderById($id: ID!) { order(id: $id) { id status totalCents } }
//   mutation CancelOrder($id: ID!, $reason: String!) { cancelOrder(id: $id, reason: $reason) { id status } }

val apollo = ApolloClient.Builder()
    .serverUrl("https://api.example.com/graphql")
    .build()                                                   // one per app, like an OkHttpClient

sealed interface OrderLoad {
    data class Loaded(val status: String) : OrderLoad
    data class NotFound(val message: String) : OrderLoad
    data class Offline(val cause: Throwable) : OrderLoad
}

suspend fun loadOrder(id: String): OrderLoad {
    val response = apollo.query(OrderByIdQuery(id = id)).execute()
    val order = response.data?.order
    val failure = response.exception
    return when {
        order != null -> OrderLoad.Loaded(order.status)          // possibly partial data elsewhere
        failure != null -> OrderLoad.Offline(failure)            // fetch error: no data
        else -> OrderLoad.NotFound(response.errors?.firstOrNull()?.message ?: "no such order")
    }
}

suspend fun cancel(id: String) = apollo
    .mutation(CancelOrderMutation(id = id, reason = "customer request"))
    .execute()
    .dataOrThrow()
    .cancelOrder
Result

loadOrder("A-1041") returns Loaded("SHIPPED"); a network failure lands in Offline and a GraphQL error without data in NotFound.

gRPC with grpc-kotlin: unary, server stream, deadline, status

Coroutine stubs make a unary call a `suspend fun` and a server stream a `Flow`; start each call's deadline when the call starts, and branch on `Status.Code`.

class OrdersRepository(host: String) : Closeable {
    private val channel = ManagedChannelBuilder.forAddress(host, 443)
        .useTransportSecurity()                                 // TLS; usePlaintext() only for an emulator
        .build()
    private val stub = OrdersGrpcKt.OrdersCoroutineStub(channel)

    suspend fun order(id: String): Order? = try {
        stub.withDeadlineAfter(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)               // computed now: this call only
            .getOrder(getOrderRequest { this.id = id })
    } catch (e: StatusException) {
        when (e.status.code) {
            Status.Code.NOT_FOUND -> null
            Status.Code.UNAVAILABLE -> throw RetryableException(e)   // transient; the call is a read
            else -> throw e                                     // DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, PERMISSION_DENIED…
        }
    }

    // Server stream: the deadline starts when someone collects, so a re-collected flow gets a fresh one.
    fun updates(id: String): Flow<OrderUpdate> = flow {
        emitAll(stub.withDeadlineAfter(10, TimeUnit.MINUTES).watchOrder(watchOrderRequest { orderId = id }))
    }

    override fun close() {
        channel.shutdown().awaitTermination(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    }
}

// In a ViewModel: collection ends, and the RPC is cancelled, when viewModelScope is.
// repository.updates("A-1041").onEach { _state.value = it.status.name }.launchIn(viewModelScope)
Result

order("A-1041") suspends until the unary reply or the 5-second deadline; each collection of updates("A-1041") opens one RPC with its own 10-minute deadline, and cancelling the collector cancels the call.

  2. orders.proto declares service Orders { rpc GetOrder(GetOrderRequest) returns (Order); rpc WatchOrder(WatchOrderRequest) returns (stream OrderUpdate); }; RetryableException is your own wrapper that the retry policy recognises

Bonus: a WebSocket as a Flow with OkHttp

`callbackFlow` turns the listener into a cold stream: the socket opens on collect and closes when the collector is cancelled.

fun OkHttpClient.liveOrders(url: String, subscribe: String): Flow<String> = callbackFlow {
    val socket = newWebSocket(Request.Builder().url(url).build(), object : WebSocketListener() {
        override fun onOpen(webSocket: WebSocket, response: Response) {
            webSocket.send(subscribe)                    // e.g. {"type":"subscribe","orderId":"A-1041"}
        }
        override fun onMessage(webSocket: WebSocket, text: String) {
            trySend(text)                                // the buffer below is unbounded: never dropped
        }
        override fun onClosing(webSocket: WebSocket, code: Int, reason: String) {
            webSocket.close(1000, null)
            close()                                      // the server said goodbye: complete the flow
        }
        override fun onFailure(webSocket: WebSocket, t: Throwable, response: Response?) {
            close(t)                                     // the collector sees the exception
        }
    })
    awaitClose { socket.close(1000, "client gone") }     // collector cancelled → close the socket
}.buffer(Channel.UNLIMITED)                  // every order event matters; conflate() if only the latest does

// viewModelScope.launch {
//     client.liveOrders(url, subscribeJson)
//         .retryWhen { cause, attempt -> cause !is ProtocolException && attempt < 5 && backOff(attempt) }
//         .collect { frame -> _state.update { it.copy(lastEvent = frame) } }
// }
// ProtocolException covers a refused upgrade (e.g. 401): sign in again instead of retrying.
Result

Each text frame the server pushes reaches the collector in order, none dropped; cancelling the collecting coroutine closes the socket with code 1000.

Choosing between REST, SOAP, gRPC and GraphQL

The server usually decides; when you get to choose, choose by who the clients are.

ConcernRESTSOAPgRPCGraphQL
ContractOpenAPI, optionalWSDL + XSD, strict.proto, requiredschema (SDL), required
PayloadJSON, any shapeXML envelope, verboseProtobuf binary, smallJSON shaped by the query
HTTP cachingyes — GET, ETag, CDNno (all POST)nohard (POST); persisted queries over GET help
StreamingSSE or chunkednoclient, server and bidirectionalsubscriptions over WebSocket
ErrorsHTTP status + bodyFault (HTTP 500; 400 for a SOAP 1.2 Sender fault)Status.Code in trailerserrors beside data; request errors are 4xx under application/graphql-response+json
Android toolingRetrofit, Ktor, OkHttphand-rolled XML (no maintained client)grpc-kotlin + grpc-okhttp + protobuf-liteApollo Kotlin
Best fitpublic APIs, simple CRUD, cacheable readsenterprise and government integrations you cannot changeinternal service-to-service, low latency, streamingmany screens needing different slices of one graph

Rules worth saying out loud

Each protocol has one mistake that everyone makes once.

  • Parsing untrusted XML with a default DocumentBuilderFactory — set disallow-doctype-decl (XXE, entity expansion), and FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING for size limits. On Android, XmlPullParser leaves FEATURE_PROCESS_DOCDECL off by default — keep it off.
  • Reading a missing <valid> or a fault as false — a SOAP Server fault, an HTML 502 or an empty body means unknown, and the user must not be told their data is invalid.
  • Building SOAP envelopes or GraphQL queries by string concatenation of user input — escape XML text; pass GraphQL values as variables.
  • Treating GraphQL HTTP 200 as success, or throwing away a 4xx body — partial data is normal, and request errors arrive as errors with a 4xx under application/graphql-response+json.
  • A gRPC call without a deadline: it can wait forever on a half-open connection. Set withDeadlineAfter on every call, at the moment of the call, and propagate the remaining time downstream.
  • gRPC on Android: grpc-okhttp transport and the lite protobuf runtime (protobuf-kotlin-lite, grpc-protobuf-lite) to keep the APK small; reuse one ManagedChannel for the app.
  • Map each protocol's failure — HTTP status, SOAP Fault, gRPC Status.Code, GraphQL errors — onto the same sealed error type, so screens do not care which one the backend speaks.
  • Retry rules differ: gRPC UNAVAILABLE is usually transient — retry with backoff, and only idempotent calls; DEADLINE_EXCEEDED may hide a completed write. A SOAP Client fault never succeeds on retry, a Server fault might.

What a multivariant playlist holds, and how ABR picks

ExoPlayer does this for you; knowing the rule — the best rendition within a fraction of measured bandwidth, up to the smallest that fills the view — explains what you configure.

import java.net.URI

data class Rendition(val bandwidth: Long, val width: Int, val height: Int, val codecs: String, val uri: URI)

private val attribute = Regex("""([A-Z0-9-]+)=("[^"]*"|[^,]*)""")    // quoted values may contain commas

fun parseMultivariant(base: URI, text: String): List<Rendition> {
    val lines = text.lines().map(String::trim).filter(String::isNotEmpty)
    require(lines.firstOrNull() == "#EXTM3U") { "not an HLS playlist" }
    return lines.zipWithNext().filter { (tag, _) -> tag.startsWith("#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:") }.map { (tag, uri) ->
        val attrs = attribute.findAll(tag.substringAfter(':'))
            .associate { it.groupValues[1] to it.groupValues[2].trim('"') }
        val (w, h) = attrs.getValue("RESOLUTION").split('x').map(String::toInt)
        Rendition(attrs.getValue("BANDWIDTH").toLong(), w, h, attrs["CODECS"].orEmpty(), base.resolve(uri))
    }.sortedBy { it.bandwidth }
}

/**
 * The highest rendition within 70% of measured throughput (ExoPlayer's default fraction), among those up to
 * the smallest one that fills the view — a simplification of DefaultTrackSelector, which compares pixels.
 */
fun pick(renditions: List<Rendition>, measuredBps: Long, viewHeight: Int, fraction: Double = 0.7): Rendition {
    val fillsView = renditions.filter { it.height >= viewHeight * 0.98 }.minByOrNull { it.height }
    val useful = renditions.filter { fillsView == null || it.height <= fillsView.height }
    return useful.lastOrNull { it.bandwidth <= measuredBps * fraction } ?: renditions.first()   // never stall
}

fun main() {
    val playlist = """
        #EXTM3U
        #EXT-X-INDEPENDENT-SEGMENTS
        #EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=6000000,RESOLUTION=1920x1080,CODECS="avc1.640028,mp4a.40.2"
        1080p/index.m3u8
        #EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=800000,RESOLUTION=640x360,CODECS="avc1.4d401e,mp4a.40.2"
        360p/index.m3u8
        #EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=2800000,RESOLUTION=1280x720,CODECS="avc1.4d401f,mp4a.40.2"
        720p/index.m3u8
    """.trimIndent()
    val renditions = parseMultivariant(URI("https://cdn.example.com/trailers/arrival/master.m3u8"), playlist)
    renditions.forEach { println("${it.height}p ${it.bandwidth / 1000} kbps → ${it.uri}") }
    val conditions = listOf(Triple("3G", 600_000L, 1080), Triple("4G", 5_000_000L, 1080),
        Triple("Wi-Fi", 20_000_000L, 1080), Triple("Wi-Fi, 640 px view", 20_000_000L, 640),
        Triple("Wi-Fi, 1000 px view", 20_000_000L, 1000))
    for ((label, bps, view) in conditions) println("$label: ${pick(renditions, bps, view).height}p")
}

Play a stream in Compose

Since Media3 1.10, the `Player` composable in `media3-ui-compose-material3` replaces wrapping `PlayerView` in `AndroidView`; create the player on start and release it on stop.

@OptIn(UnstableApi::class)
@Composable
fun TrailerPlayer(url: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    var player by remember { mutableStateOf<ExoPlayer?>(null) }
    var resumeAtMs by rememberSaveable(url) { mutableLongStateOf(0L) }    // survives rotation, process death

    LifecycleStartEffect(url) {                         // STARTED: build; STOPPED or left: release
        val exo = ExoPlayer.Builder(context).build().apply {
            setMediaItem(MediaItem.fromUri(url), resumeAtMs)
            prepare()
            playWhenReady = true
        }
        player = exo
        onStopOrDispose {
            resumeAtMs = exo.currentPosition
            exo.release()                               // frees the hardware decoder for other apps
            player = null
        }
    }

    Player(player = player, modifier = modifier.fillMaxWidth().aspectRatio(16f / 9f))   // video and controls
}
Result

The trailer plays in a 16:9 frame with Material 3 controls; leaving the screen or backgrounding the app releases the player, and returning resumes at the saved position.

  2. <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET"/> in the manifest; call TrailerPlayer(url) from a screen

Play a stream with PlayerView, and the lifecycle rule

One player per screen, created in `onStart` and released in `onStop` (API 24+), with the position saved — never kept in a static or a ViewModel that outlives its view.

class TrailerActivity : AppCompatActivity() {
    private lateinit var playerView: PlayerView
    private var player: ExoPlayer? = null
    private var resumeAtMs = 0L

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        setContentView(R.layout.activity_trailer)
        playerView = findViewById(R.id.player_view)
        resumeAtMs = savedInstanceState?.getLong("position") ?: 0L
    }

    override fun onStart() {
        super.onStart()
        val url = requireNotNull(intent.getStringExtra("url"))
        player = ExoPlayer.Builder(this).build().also { exo ->
            playerView.player = exo
            val item = MediaItem.Builder().setUri(url).setMimeType(MimeTypes.APPLICATION_MPD).build()
            exo.setMediaItem(item, resumeAtMs)
            exo.prepare()
            exo.playWhenReady = true
        }
    }

    override fun onStop() {
        super.onStop()
        player?.let {
            resumeAtMs = it.currentPosition
            it.release()
        }
        playerView.player = null
        player = null
    }

    override fun onSaveInstanceState(outState: Bundle) {
        super.onSaveInstanceState(outState)
        outState.putLong("position", player?.currentPosition ?: resumeAtMs)
    }
}
Result

The DASH stream plays with the default controls; switching apps releases the decoder, and coming back resumes where the user left off.
