Building MediaItems: MIME hints, live configuration, captions and DRM

Give the MIME type when the URL has no `.m3u8` or `.mpd` extension, and attach the DRM license server to the item itself.

fun Title.toMediaItem(licenseToken: String?): MediaItem = MediaItem.Builder()
    .setMediaId(id)
    .setUri(streamUrl)                                         // e.g. https://cdn.example.com/play?id=42
    .setMimeType(if (isDash) MimeTypes.APPLICATION_MPD else MimeTypes.APPLICATION_M3U8)
    .setMediaMetadata(MediaMetadata.Builder().setTitle(name).setArtworkUri(posterUrl.toUri()).build())
    .setSubtitleConfigurations(captions.map { track ->
        MediaItem.SubtitleConfiguration.Builder(track.url.toUri())
            .setMimeType(MimeTypes.TEXT_VTT)
            .setLanguage(track.language)
            .setSelectionFlags(if (track.isDefault) C.SELECTION_FLAG_DEFAULT else 0)
            .build()
    })
    .apply {
        if (isLive) setLiveConfiguration(
            MediaItem.LiveConfiguration.Builder()
                .setTargetOffsetMs(8_000)                       // stay 8 s behind the live edge
                .setMaxPlaybackSpeed(1.04f)                     // catch up gently if we drift
                .build(),
        )
        if (licenseToken != null) setDrmConfiguration(
            MediaItem.DrmConfiguration.Builder(C.WIDEVINE_UUID)
                .setLicenseUri("https://license.example.com/widevine")
                .setLicenseRequestHeaders(mapOf("Authorization" to "Bearer $licenseToken"))
                .setMultiSession(false)
                .build(),
        )
    }
    .build()
Result

An item that ExoPlayer routes to the HLS or DASH module without sniffing, with captions, a live latency target and a Widevine license request carrying the user's token.

Setup
  1. media3-exoplayer, media3-exoplayer-hls and media3-exoplayer-dash (1.11.1)
  2. Title is your catalogue model; licenseToken comes from your backend for this user and title

Adaptive bitrate limits and track selection

Constrain ABR with `TrackSelectionParameters` — reset the caps, then cap size and bitrate on cellular and prefer languages — instead of forcing one rendition.

enum class Quality { AUTO, DATA_SAVER, BEST }

fun ExoPlayer.applyQualityPolicy(quality: Quality, isMetered: Boolean, audioLanguage: String) {
    trackSelectionParameters = trackSelectionParameters.buildUpon()
        .clearVideoSizeConstraints()                                  // undo what an earlier call set
        .setMaxVideoBitrate(Int.MAX_VALUE)
        .clearViewportSizeConstraints()
        .apply {
            when {
                quality == Quality.DATA_SAVER || (quality == Quality.AUTO && isMetered) ->
                    setMaxVideoSizeSd().setMaxVideoBitrate(1_500_000)        // ABR adapts below the cap
                quality == Quality.AUTO -> setViewportSizeToPhysicalDisplaySize(true)   // fit the screen
                else -> Unit                                                  // BEST: no caps at all
            }
        }
        .setPreferredAudioLanguage(audioLanguage)
        .setPreferredTextLanguage(audioLanguage)
        .build()
}

/** What is playing now — for a "720p · 2.8 Mbps" debug overlay. */
fun Player.currentVideoFormat(): String? = currentTracks.groups
    .firstOrNull { it.type == C.TRACK_TYPE_VIDEO && it.isSelected }
    ?.let { group -> (0 until group.length).firstOrNull(group::isTrackSelected)?.let(group::getTrackFormat) }
    ?.let { "${it.height}p · ${it.bitrate / 1000} kbps" }
Result

On a metered network the player stays at SD and under 1.5 Mbps while still switching between the renditions that fit; back on Wi-Fi in AUTO the caps are cleared and only the screen size limits it; audio and captions follow the user's language.

Setup
  1. media3-exoplayer (1.11.1); isMetered from ConnectivityManager.isActiveNetworkMetered
  2. Call applyQualityPolicy after building the player and whenever the network or the setting changes

Player state, buffering, errors and recovery; live versus VOD

Drive the UI from `Player.Listener`; recover from falling behind a live window by seeking to the default position and preparing again.

data class PlaybackUi(
    val buffering: Boolean = false,
    val playing: Boolean = false,
    val live: Boolean = false,
    val error: String? = null,
)

class PlaybackObserver(private val player: Player, private val render: (PlaybackUi) -> Unit) :
    Player.Listener {
    private var ui = PlaybackUi()

    override fun onEvents(player: Player, events: Player.Events) {      // one callback per batch of changes
        ui = ui.copy(
            buffering = player.playbackState == Player.STATE_BUFFERING,
            playing = player.isPlaying,
            live = player.isCurrentMediaItemLive,                       // hide the seek bar, show "LIVE"
        )
        render(ui)
    }

    override fun onPlayerError(error: PlaybackException) {
        when (error.errorCode) {
            PlaybackException.ERROR_CODE_BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW -> {        // paused too long on a live stream
                player.seekToDefaultPosition()
                player.prepare()
            }
            PlaybackException.ERROR_CODE_IO_NETWORK_CONNECTION_FAILED,
            PlaybackException.ERROR_CODE_IO_NETWORK_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT -> show("Offline. Tap to retry.")
            PlaybackException.ERROR_CODE_DRM_LICENSE_ACQUISITION_FAILED -> show("Not available here.")
            else -> show("Playback failed (${error.errorCodeName}).")
        }
    }

    private fun show(message: String) {
        ui = ui.copy(error = message)
        render(ui)
    }

    fun retry() {                                        // the retry button: prepare() resumes in place
        ui = ui.copy(error = null)
        player.prepare()
    }
}
Result

The spinner shows while buffering, "LIVE" replaces the seek bar on live items, a live stream left paused rejoins at the live edge by itself, and network failures offer a retry that continues from the same position.

Setup
  1. media3-exoplayer (1.11.1); PlaybackUi is your screen state, rendered by the composable or view
  2. player.addListener(PlaybackObserver(player) { ui = it }) after building, removeListener before release()

Live versus on-demand, read from the media playlist

A live playlist has no `#EXT-X-ENDLIST` and slides forward; the player starts a few target durations behind its end, and a position that slides out of the window is the `BehindLiveWindow` error.

data class MediaPlaylist(
    val live: Boolean,
    val targetSeconds: Double,
    val firstSequence: Long,
    val segments: List<Double>,
) {
    val windowSeconds get() = segments.sum()
    val lastSequence get() = firstSequence + segments.size - 1
    /** RFC 8216: start no closer than three target durations from the end of a live playlist. */
    val defaultStartSeconds get() = if (live) (windowSeconds - 3 * targetSeconds).coerceAtLeast(0.0) else 0.0
}

fun parseMediaPlaylist(text: String): MediaPlaylist {
    val lines = text.lines().map(String::trim)
    fun tag(name: String) = lines.firstOrNull { it.startsWith("$name:") }?.substringAfter(':')
    return MediaPlaylist(
        live = "#EXT-X-ENDLIST" !in lines && tag("#EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE") != "VOD",
        targetSeconds = tag("#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION")!!.toDouble(),
        firstSequence = tag("#EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE")?.toLong() ?: 0,
        segments = lines.filter { it.startsWith("#EXTINF:") }
            .map { it.removePrefix("#EXTINF:").substringBefore(',').toDouble() },
    )
}

fun playlist(firstSequence: Long, count: Int, ended: Boolean) = buildString {
    appendLine("#EXTM3U")
    appendLine("#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION:6")
    appendLine("#EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE:$firstSequence")
    repeat(count) { appendLine("#EXTINF:6.0,\nseg${firstSequence + it}.ts") }
    if (ended) appendLine("#EXT-X-ENDLIST")
}

fun main() {
    val vod = parseMediaPlaylist(playlist(0, 100, ended = true))
    println("VOD: ${vod.windowSeconds} s, seekable from 0, start at ${vod.defaultStartSeconds}")

    val live = parseMediaPlaylist(playlist(1200, 5, ended = false))
    println("live: window ${live.windowSeconds} s, segments ${live.firstSequence}..${live.lastSequence}")
    println("live: start at ${live.defaultStartSeconds} s, three target durations behind the edge")

    val pausedAt = 1201L                                         // paused on this segment for a minute
    val refreshed = parseMediaPlaylist(playlist(1210, 5, ended = false))
    val gone = pausedAt < refreshed.firstSequence
    println(if (gone) "segment $pausedAt is gone: BehindLiveWindow, rejoin at the live edge" else "resume")
}
Result
VOD: 600.0 s, seekable from 0, start at 0.0
live: window 30.0 s, segments 1200..1204
live: start at 12.0 s, three target durations behind the edge
segment 1201 is gone: BehindLiveWindow, rejoin at the live edge
Setup

  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar

Background playback with a MediaSessionService, in outline

Background audio lives in a `MediaSessionService` that owns the player and audio focus; the screen controls it through a `MediaController`.

class PlaybackService : MediaSessionService() {
    private var session: MediaSession? = null

    override fun onCreate() {
        super.onCreate()
        val audio = AudioAttributes.Builder()
            .setUsage(C.USAGE_MEDIA)
            .setContentType(C.AUDIO_CONTENT_TYPE_MOVIE)
            .build()
        val sources = DefaultMediaSourceFactory(this).setDataSourceFactory(Downloads.readOnly(this))
        val player = ExoPlayer.Builder(this)
            .setMediaSourceFactory(sources)                             // downloads play offline
            .setAudioAttributes(audio, /* handleAudioFocus = */ true)   // pause for calls and other apps
            .setHandleAudioBecomingNoisy(true)                          // pause when headphones come out
            .build()
        session = MediaSession.Builder(this, player).build()           // notification, lock screen, Bluetooth
    }

    override fun onGetSession(controllerInfo: MediaSession.ControllerInfo): MediaSession? = session

    @OptIn(UnstableApi::class)
    override fun onTaskRemoved(rootIntent: Intent?) = pauseAllPlayersAndStopSelf()   // swiped away: stop

    override fun onDestroy() {
        session?.run {
            player.release()
            release()
        }
        session = null
        super.onDestroy()
    }
}

// The screen talks to the service through a MediaController: connect on start, release on stop.
class PlaybackConnection(private val context: Context) : DefaultLifecycleObserver {
    private var future: ListenableFuture<MediaController>? = null

    override fun onStart(owner: LifecycleOwner) {
        val token = SessionToken(context, ComponentName(context, PlaybackService::class.java))
        future = MediaController.Builder(context, token).buildAsync()   // await() it in a coroutine
    }

    override fun onStop(owner: LifecycleOwner) {
        future?.let(MediaController::releaseFuture)                   // otherwise the service never stops
        future = null
    }
}
Result

Playback continues with the screen off, pauses for a phone call or unplugged headphones, and shows media controls in the notification and on the lock screen.

Setup
  1. media3-session and media3-exoplayer (1.11.1), androidx.lifecycle 2.11.0 and kotlinx-coroutines-guava; add PlaybackConnection(context) to the screen's lifecycle; the manifest declares FOREGROUND_SERVICE and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK, and the service with android:foregroundServiceType="mediaPlayback", android:exported="true" and the androidx.media3.session.MediaSessionService intent filter
  2. Downloads.readOnly comes from the next card

Offline downloads with DownloadManager, in outline

Download through `DownloadManager` and a cache, with `DownloadHelper` choosing the renditions, and play a completed download from `request.toMediaItem()`, read off the main thread, so the stream keys match.

@OptIn(UnstableApi::class)
object Downloads {                                                     // one database, cache and manager
    private var database: StandaloneDatabaseProvider? = null
    private var cache: SimpleCache? = null
    private var manager: DownloadManager? = null
    private val http = DefaultHttpDataSource.Factory()

    @Synchronized private fun database(context: Context) =
        database ?: StandaloneDatabaseProvider(context.applicationContext).also { database = it }

    @Synchronized private fun cache(context: Context) = cache ?: SimpleCache(   // NoOp: never evicted
        File(context.filesDir, "downloads"), NoOpCacheEvictor(), database(context)).also { cache = it }

    @Synchronized fun manager(context: Context): DownloadManager = manager ?: DownloadManager(
        context.applicationContext, database(context), cache(context), http, Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2),
    ).also { manager = it }

    /** Plays downloaded titles from disk and streams the rest without caching them. */
    fun readOnly(context: Context): DataSource.Factory = CacheDataSource.Factory()
        .setCache(cache(context)).setUpstreamDataSourceFactory(http).setCacheWriteDataSinkFactory(null)

    /** Call on the main thread; DownloadHelper picks the renditions (stream keys) to keep. */
    fun download(context: Context, titleId: String, hlsUrl: String) {
        val item = MediaItem.Builder().setMediaId(titleId).setUri(hlsUrl)
            .setMimeType(MimeTypes.APPLICATION_M3U8).build()            // the URL may have no .m3u8
        val helper = DownloadHelper.Factory()
            .setRenderersFactory(DefaultRenderersFactory(context))
            .setDataSourceFactory(http)
            .create(item)
        helper.prepare(object : DownloadHelper.Callback {
            override fun onPrepared(helper: DownloadHelper, tracksInfoAvailable: Boolean) {
                val request = helper.getDownloadRequest(titleId, null)   // default selection, not all
                DownloadService.sendAddDownload(context, TrailerDownloadService::class.java, request, false)
                helper.release()
            }
            override fun onPrepareError(helper: DownloadHelper, e: IOException) = helper.release()
        })
    }

    /** The item to play offline, or null when the title is not (fully) downloaded: stream it instead. */
    suspend fun offlineItem(context: Context, titleId: String): MediaItem? = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        val download = manager(context).downloadIndex.getDownload(titleId)   // a database read
        download?.takeIf { it.state == Download.STATE_COMPLETED }?.request?.toMediaItem()
    }
}
Result

download(context, "arrival", url) queues the default rendition of an HLS title in the background; once complete, the title plays from the cache in airplane mode.

Setup
  1. media3-exoplayer, -hls, -datasource and -database (1.11.1); the manifest declares FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC, and TrailerDownloadService (your DownloadService subclass returning Downloads.manager(this)) with android:exported="false", android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" and the androidx.media3.exoplayer.downloadService.action.RESTART intent filter
  2. DRM titles also need an offline licence: download it with OfflineLicenseHelper and store its keySetId on the request

Pitfalls worth saying out loud

Most playback bugs are lifecycle bugs.

  • Forgetting release(): hardware decoders are few — a leaked player makes the next video fail with a decoder error. Release in onStop, or in onStopOrDispose in Compose.
  • Several ExoPlayer instances for one screen (one per list item, a new one on every recomposition). Share one player and move it between surfaces.
  • Mixing Media3 module versions: media3-exoplayer, -hls, -dash, -ui and -session must all be the same version.
  • Touching the player off its application thread (normally the main thread) — it throws Player is accessed on the wrong thread.
  • Downloading segments yourself or reading the download directory — use DownloadManager and CacheDataSource, which keep the stream keys consistent. DRM: download the offline licence yourself (OfflineLicenseHelper) and store its keySetId on the request.
  • Pick the protocol by DRM and catalogue: HLS for reach, DASH with Widevine for protected premium content; both need their Media3 module.
  • Constrain adaptive bitrate (setMaxVideoSizeSd(), setMaxVideoBitrate) rather than pinning one track — pinning turns every network dip into a stall.
  • Use @OptIn(UnstableApi::class) deliberately: the Compose UI, DownloadManager and cache APIs are marked unstable and can change between minor versions.
  • Widevine L1 (hardware) is required by most studios for HD; L3 devices may be capped at SD. Check MediaDrm security level before promising 1080p.

Where does this secret go?

Anything inside the APK is public; the Keystore protects keys, not the data you forgot to encrypt.

SecretPut it inNever inWhy
Encryption and signing keysAndroid Keystore (AndroidKeyStore provider; StrongBox where available)a file, SharedPreferences, codethe key material cannot be exported; on most devices it lives in the TEE or StrongBox (check KeyInfo.securityLevel)
Access and refresh tokensciphertext from a Keystore AES-GCM key, stored in DataStore or a private fileSharedPreferences in clear, logs, URLsa rooted device or a backup reads plain prefs
EncryptedSharedPreferences / EncryptedFilemigrate away: deprecated in security-crypto 1.1.0new codeGoogle now points to the platform APIs and direct Keystore use
Third-party API secrets (payment, AI, admin keys)your server; the app calls your backendBuildConfig, strings.xml, assets, native librariesR8 and NDK code are trivially extracted from an APK
Public, restricted keys (Maps, Firebase config)BuildConfig or resources, restricted to your package and signing certificate—they are designed to be public; the restriction is the protection
User passwordsnowhere — use passkeys or the password provider via Credential Manageryour own storageyou cannot leak what you never kept
Personal data cachesapp-specific internal storage, excluded from backup in dataExtractionRules (API 31+) and fullBackupContent (API 30 and lower)external or shared storageother apps and cloud backups can read those

OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE

Send a SHA-256 challenge, keep the verifier and `state` where process death cannot lose them, check `state` on the redirect and prove the verifier at the exchange — or let AppAuth-Android do all of this.

import java.net.*
import java.security.*
import java.util.Base64

const val REDIRECT = "com.example.shop:/oauth2redirect"

fun base64Url(bytes: ByteArray): String = Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding().encodeToString(bytes)
fun s256(verifier: String) = base64Url(MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(verifier.toByteArray()))
fun form(vararg fields: Pair<String, String>) =
    fields.joinToString("&") { (key, value) -> "$key=${URLEncoder.encode(value, Charsets.UTF_8)}" }

// Persist it (SavedStateHandle or DataStore): Android may kill the app while the Custom Tab is open.
data class PkceSession(val verifier: String, val state: String) {
    val challenge get() = s256(verifier)
}

fun newSession(random: SecureRandom = SecureRandom()) = PkceSession(
    verifier = base64Url(ByteArray(32).also(random::nextBytes)),        // 43 characters, 256 bits
    state = base64Url(ByteArray(16).also(random::nextBytes)),
)

fun authorizationUri(s: PkceSession) = URI("https://auth.example.com/authorize?" + form(
    "response_type" to "code", "client_id" to "shop-android", "redirect_uri" to REDIRECT,
    "scope" to "openid orders:read", "state" to s.state,
    "code_challenge" to s.challenge, "code_challenge_method" to "S256"))

fun exchangeForm(redirect: URI, s: PkceSession): String {          // the token request's POST body
    val params = redirect.rawQuery.split('&')
        .associate { it.substringBefore('=') to URLDecoder.decode(it.substringAfter('='), Charsets.UTF_8) }
    params["error"]?.let { error("authorization failed: $it") }
    check(params["state"] == s.state) { "state mismatch, possible CSRF" }
    return form("grant_type" to "authorization_code", "code" to params.getValue("code"),
        "code_verifier" to s.verifier, "client_id" to "shop-android", "redirect_uri" to REDIRECT)
}

fun main() {
    println(s256("dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk"))         // the RFC 7636 test vector
    val session = newSession()
    println("challenge sent: ${"code_challenge=${session.challenge}" in authorizationUri(session).rawQuery}")

    val body = exchangeForm(URI("$REDIRECT?code=c-7f3a&state=${session.state}"), session)
    println(body.replace(session.verifier, "<the 43-character verifier>"))
    val forged = runCatching { exchangeForm(URI("$REDIRECT?code=c-evil&state=forged"), session) }
    println("forged redirect: ${forged.exceptionOrNull()?.message}")

    val tokenEndpoint = { verifier: String -> s256(verifier) == session.challenge }   // the server's check
    println("code + our verifier: ${tokenEndpoint(session.verifier)}")
    println("stolen code + a thief's verifier: ${tokenEndpoint(newSession().verifier)}")
}
Result
E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM
challenge sent: true
grant_type=authorization_code&code=c-7f3a&code_verifier=<the 43-character verifier>&client_id=shop-android&redirect_uri=com.example.shop%3A%2Foauth2redirect
forged redirect: state mismatch, possible CSRF
code + our verifier: true
stolen code + a thief's verifier: false

  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar — POST the body it builds to the token endpoint; the networking sheet's Ktor card makes the refresh call

Verify a JWT, part 1: the algorithm and the signature

Pin the algorithm, verify the signature before reading a claim, and reject everything with one exception type — on a JVM backend use Nimbus JOSE+JWT or jose4j with the issuer's JWKS by `kid`; an Android app treats access tokens as opaque.

import java.security.*
import java.util.Base64
import kotlinx.serialization.json.*

private val encoder = Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding()
private val decoder = Base64.getUrlDecoder()
private fun part(s: String) = Json.parseToJsonElement(decoder.decode(s).decodeToString()).jsonObject

fun verifiedClaims(token: String, issuerKey: PublicKey): JsonObject {           // IllegalArgumentException
    val (header, payload, signature) = token.split('.').also { require(it.size == 3) { "not a JWS" } }
    require(part(header)["alg"] == JsonPrimitive("RS256")) { "unexpected alg" }   // never the token's
    val verifier = Signature.getInstance("SHA256withRSA").apply { initVerify(issuerKey) }
    verifier.update("$header.$payload".toByteArray())
    val valid = runCatching { verifier.verify(decoder.decode(signature)) }.getOrDefault(false)   // may throw
    require(valid) { "bad signature" }
    return part(payload)                                                       // now check the claims
}

fun sign(key: PrivateKey, claims: String, alg: String = "RS256"): String {     // the issuer's side
    val unsigned = listOf("""{"alg":"$alg"}""", claims)
        .joinToString(".") { encoder.encodeToString(it.toByteArray()) }
    val signer = Signature.getInstance("SHA256withRSA").apply { initSign(key) }
    signer.update(unsigned.toByteArray())
    return "$unsigned.${encoder.encodeToString(signer.sign())}"
}

fun main() {
    val issuer = KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("RSA").apply { initialize(2048) }.generateKeyPair()
    val attacker = KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("RSA").apply { initialize(2048) }.generateKeyPair()
    val token = sign(issuer.private, """{"sub":"user-42","aud":"shop-api"}""")
    val (header, _, signature) = token.split('.')
    val admin = encoder.encodeToString("""{"sub":"admin","aud":"shop-api"}""".toByteArray())
    val cases = listOf(
        "genuine" to token,
        "payload swapped" to "$header.$admin.$signature",
        "alg none" to sign(issuer.private, """{"sub":"admin"}""", alg = "none"),
        "signed by another key" to sign(attacker.private, """{"sub":"admin"}"""),
        "empty signature" to "$header.$admin.",
    )
    for ((label, jwt) in cases) {
        val result = runCatching { verifiedClaims(jwt, issuer.public) }
        println("$label: " + result.fold({ "claims $it" }, { "rejected ($it)" }))
    }
}
Result
genuine: claims {"sub":"user-42","aud":"shop-api"}
payload swapped: rejected (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: bad signature)
alg none: rejected (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: unexpected alg)
signed by another key: rejected (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: bad signature)
empty signature: rejected (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: bad signature)
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc), JDK 17 or later, kotlinx-serialization-core-jvm-1.13.0.jar and kotlinx-serialization-json-jvm-1.13.0.jar (only JsonObject is used, so no compiler plugin)
  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc -cp <the two jars> main.kt -d out && kotlin -cp out:<the two jars> MainKt

Verify a JWT, part 2: issuer, audience, expiry and not-before

After the signature, check `iss`, `aud` as a string or an array, and `exp`, `nbf` and `iat` as NumericDates (fractional allowed) against an injected clock — a missing `exp` or any malformed time claim is a rejection.

import java.time.Instant
import kotlinx.serialization.json.*

private fun JsonObject.text(key: String) = (get(key) as? JsonPrimitive)?.contentOrNull
private fun JsonObject.audiences() =                                    // a string or an array of strings
    (get("aud") as? JsonArray)?.map { it.jsonPrimitive.content } ?: listOfNotNull(text("aud"))

private fun JsonObject.time(key: String): Instant? {                       // a NumericDate, or absent
    val value = get(key) ?: return null
    val seconds = (value as? JsonPrimitive)?.takeUnless { it.isString }?.doubleOrNull   // may be fractional
    require(seconds != null && seconds.isFinite()) { "$key is not a number" }
    return Instant.ofEpochMilli((seconds * 1_000).toLong())              // toLong saturates: no overflow
}

/** Throws IllegalArgumentException for every rejection; `now` comes from an injected clock. */
fun checkClaims(claims: JsonObject, issuer: String, audience: String, now: Instant) {
    require(claims.text("iss") == issuer) { "wrong issuer" }
    require(audience in claims.audiences()) { "wrong audience" }
    val expires = requireNotNull(claims.time("exp")) { "exp missing" }
    require(now.isBefore(expires.plusSeconds(30))) { "expired" }                     // 30 s of clock skew
    claims.time("iat")                                                              // validates its type
    val notBefore = claims.time("nbf")
    require(notBefore == null || !now.plusSeconds(30).isBefore(notBefore)) { "not yet valid" }
}

fun main() {
    val now = Instant.parse("2026-11-21T09:45:00Z")                         // exp 1795255200 is 10:00Z
    val c = """"iss":"https://auth.example.com""""
    val cases = listOf(
        "aud array" to """{$c,"aud":["shop-web","shop-api"],"exp":1795255200}""",
        "fractional exp" to """{$c,"aud":"shop-api","exp":1795255200.5}""",
        "nbf in 15 min" to """{$c,"aud":"shop-api","exp":1795258800,"nbf":1795255200}""",
        "nbf as text, far ahead" to """{$c,"aud":"shop-api","exp":1795255200,"nbf":"1895255200"}""",
        "exp as text" to """{$c,"aud":"shop-api","exp":"1795255200"}""",
        "iat as text" to """{$c,"aud":"shop-api","exp":1795255200,"iat":"yesterday"}""",
        "no exp" to """{$c,"aud":"shop-api"}""",
        "expired" to """{$c,"aud":"shop-api","exp":1795250000}""",
    )
    for ((label, json) in cases) {
        val claims = Json.parseToJsonElement(json).jsonObject
        val result = runCatching { checkClaims(claims, "https://auth.example.com", "shop-api", now) }
        println("$label: " + result.fold({ "accepted" }, { "rejected ($it)" }))
    }
}
Result
aud array: accepted
fractional exp: accepted
nbf in 15 min: rejected (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: not yet valid)
nbf as text, far ahead: rejected (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: nbf is not a number)
exp as text: rejected (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: exp is not a number)
iat as text: rejected (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: iat is not a number)
no exp: rejected (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: exp missing)
expired: rejected (java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: expired)
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc), JDK 17 or later, kotlinx-serialization-core-jvm-1.13.0.jar and kotlinx-serialization-json-jvm-1.13.0.jar (only JsonObject is used, so no compiler plugin)
  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc -cp <the two jars> main.kt -d out && kotlin -cp out:<the two jars> MainKt

Ran with kotlinc 2.4.21, JVM 21.0.12.1, kotlinx-serialization-json 1.13.0 on 2026-11-16: the output matched the result shown.

AES-GCM encryption and SHA-256 with javax.crypto

A fresh random 12-byte nonce for every message, stored beside the ciphertext — and rotate the key well before 2^32 messages, the limit for random nonces.

import java.security.*
import java.util.HexFormat
import javax.crypto.*
import javax.crypto.spec.*

private val random = SecureRandom()

/** Returns nonce ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag. The AAD (here the record id) is authenticated, not encrypted. */
fun seal(key: SecretKey, plaintext: ByteArray, aad: ByteArray): ByteArray {
    val nonce = ByteArray(12).also(random::nextBytes)               // never reuse a nonce with the same key
    val cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")
    cipher.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, key, GCMParameterSpec(128, nonce))
    cipher.updateAAD(aad)
    return nonce + cipher.doFinal(plaintext)
}

fun open(key: SecretKey, sealed: ByteArray, aad: ByteArray): ByteArray {
    val cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")
    cipher.init(Cipher.DECRYPT_MODE, key, GCMParameterSpec(128, sealed, 0, 12))
    cipher.updateAAD(aad)
    return cipher.doFinal(sealed, 12, sealed.size - 12)             // AEADBadTagException if altered
}

fun main() {
    val key = KeyGenerator.getInstance("AES").apply { init(256) }.generateKey()   // Android: a Keystore key
    val note = "card ending 4242, expires 09/29".toByteArray()
    val first = seal(key, note, "order:A-1041".toByteArray())
    val second = seal(key, note, "order:A-1041".toByteArray())
    println("same plaintext, same ciphertext: ${first.contentEquals(second)}")
    println(open(key, first, "order:A-1041".toByteArray()).decodeToString())

    val tampered = first.copyOf().also { it[20] = (it[20].toInt() xor 1).toByte() }
    val attempts = listOf(Triple("tampered", tampered, "order:A-1041"), Triple("moved", first, "order:A-9"))
    for ((label, blob, aad) in attempts) {
        try {
            open(key, blob, aad.toByteArray())
        } catch (e: AEADBadTagException) {
            println("$label: rejected")
        }
    }
    val digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest("receipt-A-1041".toByteArray())
    println(HexFormat.of().formatHex(digest))                         // a fingerprint, not a password hash
}
Result
same plaintext, same ciphertext: false
card ending 4242, expires 09/29
tampered: rejected
moved: rejected
bf60b7894390b98acfbd6b962af2284eb844dddbb7c24b5e1a39c1ce4abbd91f
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc) and JDK 17 or later; javax.crypto and java.security are in the JDK
  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar

HMAC: verify a webhook on your server

Sign the timestamp with the body, accept ±5 minutes of clock difference, compare in constant time, take the event id from the signed body, remember it only for the window, and answer `false` to a malformed header.

import java.security.MessageDigest
import java.time.Instant
import java.util.HexFormat
import javax.crypto.Mac
import javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec
import kotlinx.serialization.json.*

fun hmacSha256(secret: ByteArray, message: String): ByteArray =
    Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA256").apply { init(SecretKeySpec(secret, "HmacSHA256")) }
        .doFinal(message.toByteArray())

class WebhookVerifier(private val secret: ByteArray, private val window: Long = 300) {
    private val seen = HashMap<String, Long>()          // id → its timestamp; in a fleet: Redis SET NX EX
    val remembered get() = seen.size

    /** `header` is `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC of "t.body">`; the id is read from the signed body. */
    fun accept(header: String, body: String, now: Instant): Boolean {
        val fields = header.split(',').associate { it.substringBefore('=') to it.substringAfter('=') }
        val t = fields["t"]?.toLongOrNull() ?: return false
        if (now.epochSecond - t !in -window..window) return false           // ±5 min of clock difference
        val received = runCatching { HexFormat.of().parseHex(fields["v1"].orEmpty()) }.getOrNull()
        if (received == null || !MessageDigest.isEqual(hmacSha256(secret, "$t.$body"), received)) return false
        val id = runCatching { Json.parseToJsonElement(body).jsonObject["id"]?.jsonPrimitive?.content }
        seen.values.removeIf { now.epochSecond - it > window }   // too old to pass the time check again
        return id.getOrNull()?.let { seen.putIfAbsent(it, t) == null } ?: false   // a replay is dropped
    }
}

fun main() {
    val secret = "whsec_test_only".toByteArray()                // a test value; real ones live in a vault
    val now = Instant.parse("2026-11-16T10:00:00Z")
    val verifier = WebhookVerifier(secret)
    fun event(id: String) = """{"id":"$id","orderId":"A-1041","status":"paid"}"""
    fun sign(body: String, t: Long) = "t=$t,v1=${HexFormat.of().formatHex(hmacSha256(secret, "$t.$body"))}"
    fun deliver(id: String, at: Instant, signedAt: Long = at.epochSecond, sentId: String = id) =
        verifier.accept(sign(event(id), signedAt), event(sentId), at)  // sentId ≠ id: the body was edited

    println("genuine: ${deliver("evt_81", now)}")
    println("replayed 2 min later: ${deliver("evt_81", now.plusSeconds(120), signedAt = now.epochSecond)}")
    println("same request, id changed to evt_99: ${deliver("evt_81", now, sentId = "evt_99")}")
    println("sender clock 5 s ahead: ${deliver("evt_82", now, signedAt = now.epochSecond + 5)}")
    println("malformed signature: ${verifier.accept("t=${now.epochSecond},v1=xyz", event("evt_83"), now)}")
    println("ids remembered: ${verifier.remembered}")
    println("7 min later: ${deliver("evt_90", now.plusSeconds(420))}, ids remembered: ${verifier.remembered}")
}
Result
genuine: true
replayed 2 min later: false
same request, id changed to evt_99: false
sender clock 5 s ahead: true
malformed signature: false
ids remembered: 2
7 min later: true, ids remembered: 1
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc), JDK 17 or later, kotlinx-serialization-core-jvm-1.13.0.jar and kotlinx-serialization-json-jvm-1.13.0.jar (only JsonObject, so no plugin)
  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc -cp <the two jars> main.kt -d out && kotlin -cp out:<the two jars> MainKt — this runs on your backend; an app never holds the webhook secret

A Keystore-backed key for tokens, stored in DataStore

What replaces `EncryptedSharedPreferences`: an AES-GCM key that lives in the Keystore, and only the IV and ciphertext in DataStore.

private val Context.sessionStore by preferencesDataStore(name = "session")
private val REFRESH_TOKEN = stringPreferencesKey("refresh_token")

sealed interface StoredToken {
    data class Present(val value: String) : StoredToken
    data object Locked : StoredToken                        // device locked: try again after unlock
    data object Gone : StoredToken                          // none, key lost or data altered: sign in again
}

class TokenVault(private val context: Context) {
    private val alias = "session-token-key"
    private val keyguard = context.getSystemService(KeyguardManager::class.java)

    @Synchronized private fun key(): SecretKey {                // one key, even for two first callers
        val keyStore = KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore").apply { load(null) }
        (keyStore.getKey(alias, null) as? SecretKey)?.let { return it }
        val purposes = KeyProperties.PURPOSE_ENCRYPT or KeyProperties.PURPOSE_DECRYPT
        val spec = KeyGenParameterSpec.Builder(alias, purposes)
            .setBlockModes(KeyProperties.BLOCK_MODE_GCM)
            .setEncryptionPaddings(KeyProperties.ENCRYPTION_PADDING_NONE)
            .setKeySize(256)
            .apply { if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 28) setUnlockedDeviceRequired(true) }   // locked: unusable
            .build()                                      // setIsStrongBoxBacked(true) where StrongBox exists
        return KeyGenerator.getInstance(KeyProperties.KEY_ALGORITHM_AES, "AndroidKeyStore")
            .apply { init(spec) }.generateKey()
    }

    suspend fun save(refreshToken: String) = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        val cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding").apply { init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, key()) }
        val sealed = cipher.iv + cipher.doFinal(refreshToken.toByteArray())
        context.sessionStore.edit { it[REFRESH_TOKEN] = Base64.encodeToString(sealed, Base64.NO_WRAP) }
    }

    suspend fun load(): StoredToken = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        val stored = context.sessionStore.data.first()[REFRESH_TOKEN] ?: return@withContext StoredToken.Gone
        if (keyguard.isDeviceLocked) return@withContext StoredToken.Locked   // the key refuses to work now
        val sealed = Base64.decode(stored, Base64.NO_WRAP)
        runCatching {
            val cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")
            cipher.init(Cipher.DECRYPT_MODE, key(), GCMParameterSpec(128, sealed, 0, 12))
            StoredToken.Present(cipher.doFinal(sealed, 12, sealed.size - 12).decodeToString())
        }.getOrDefault(StoredToken.Gone)
    }

    suspend fun clear() = context.sessionStore.edit { it.remove(REFRESH_TOKEN) }   // on sign-out
}
Result

The refresh token survives app restarts as ciphertext in DataStore; load() answers Locked while the device is locked and Gone when the key or data is lost, and copying the DataStore file to another device yields nothing, because the key cannot leave this device's Keystore.

Setup
  1. An Android project with androidx.datastore:datastore-preferences 1.1.1; exclude datastore/session.preferences_pb in dataExtractionRules (the restored ciphertext is useless without the key anyway)
  2. setUnlockedDeviceRequired(true) (API 28+) makes the key unusable while the device is locked: drop it if WorkManager or FCM code must read the token on a locked device
  3. Construct TokenVault(applicationContext) once (e.g. in your DI graph); call it from a coroutine

Excerpt, not compiled or run here: it needs an Android app (needs the Android SDK, AndroidKeyStore and DataStore).

  • androidx.datastore:datastore-preferences
  • kotlinx-coroutines-android
  • kotlin >=2.4
  • datastore 1.1.1
  • android API 23+
  • an Android app (API 23+) with DataStore

BiometricPrompt bound to a Keystore key

Pass a `CryptoObject`, so the biometric unlocks a key that signs a server challenge — and handle the key being invalidated by a new fingerprint.

private const val ALIAS = "payment-approval-key"

fun createApprovalKey(): PublicKey {                    // once, at enrolment
    val spec = KeyGenParameterSpec.Builder(ALIAS, KeyProperties.PURPOSE_SIGN)
        .setAlgorithmParameterSpec(ECGenParameterSpec("secp256r1"))
        .setDigests(KeyProperties.DIGEST_SHA256)
        .setUserAuthenticationRequired(true)
        .setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, KeyProperties.AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG)   // 0: every use needs auth
        .setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment(true)      // a newly added fingerprint invalidates the key
        .build()
    val generator = KeyPairGenerator.getInstance(KeyProperties.KEY_ALGORITHM_EC, "AndroidKeyStore")
    return generator.apply { initialize(spec) }.generateKeyPair().public
}

fun FragmentActivity.approve(challenge: ByteArray, onSigned: (ByteArray) -> Unit, onReEnrol: () -> Unit) {
    val keyStore = KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore").apply { load(null) }
    val privateKey = keyStore.getKey(ALIAS, null) as? PrivateKey ?: return onReEnrol()   // never enrolled
    val signature = try {
        Signature.getInstance("SHA256withECDSA").apply { initSign(privateKey) }
    } catch (e: KeyPermanentlyInvalidatedException) {   // biometrics changed since enrolment
        keyStore.deleteEntry(ALIAS)
        return onReEnrol()                              // confirm with the password, then enrol again
    }
    val callback = object : BiometricPrompt.AuthenticationCallback() {
        override fun onAuthenticationSucceeded(result: BiometricPrompt.AuthenticationResult) {
            val unlocked = result.cryptoObject?.signature ?: return
            unlocked.update(challenge)
            onSigned(unlocked.sign())                   // the server verifies with the enrolled public key
        }
        override fun onAuthenticationError(errorCode: Int, errString: CharSequence) {
            // cancelled or locked out: offer the password flow instead
        }
    }
    val info = BiometricPrompt.PromptInfo.Builder()
        .setTitle("Approve €25.98 to Example Shop")
        .setAllowedAuthenticators(BiometricManager.Authenticators.BIOMETRIC_STRONG)
        .setNegativeButtonText("Cancel")
        .build()
    BiometricPrompt(this, ContextCompat.getMainExecutor(this), callback)
        .authenticate(info, BiometricPrompt.CryptoObject(signature))
}
Result

The system biometric sheet appears; only after a Class 3 biometric match does the Keystore sign the server's challenge. After the user adds a fingerprint, the key is deleted and the user is sent through re-enrolment instead of the app crashing.

Setup
  1. An Android project with androidx.biometric:biometric 1.1.0 and androidx.fragment; call from a FragmentActivity
  2. Enrol only when BiometricManager.from(context).canAuthenticate(BIOMETRIC_STRONG) == BIOMETRIC_SUCCESS, then send createApprovalKey()'s public key to your server; challenge is a one-time value from the server, so a captured signature cannot be replayed

Excerpt, not compiled or run here: it needs an Android app on a device with a Class 3 biometric enrolled (needs the Android SDK and androidx.biometric).

  • androidx.biometric
  • androidx.fragment
  • kotlin >=2.4
  • biometric 1.1.0
  • android API 30+ for setUserAuthenticationParameters
  • an Android app with androidx.biometric

Sources: Show a biometric authentication dialog — Android Developers · KeyPermanentlyInvalidatedException — Android API reference

Passkeys with Credential Manager, in outline

Your server issues a WebAuthn challenge as JSON; Credential Manager shows the system sheet and returns the signed response for the server to verify.

class PasskeyAuth(private val credentials: CredentialManager, private val authApi: AuthApi) {

    suspend fun register(activity: Activity): Boolean {
        val options = authApi.registrationOptions()        // JSON: challenge, rp, user, pubKeyCredParams
        return try {
            val request = CreatePublicKeyCredentialRequest(requestJson = options)
            val response = credentials.createCredential(activity, request)
                as CreatePublicKeyCredentialResponse
            authApi.finishRegistration(response.registrationResponseJson)   // the server keeps the public key
        } catch (e: CreateCredentialCancellationException) {
            false                                          // the user said no: not an error
        } catch (e: CreateCredentialException) {           // e.g. a Digital Asset Links mismatch
            Log.w("Passkeys", "create failed: ${e.type} ${e.errorMessage}")
            false
        }
    }

    suspend fun signIn(activity: Activity): Session? {
        val request = GetCredentialRequest(listOf(
            GetPublicKeyCredentialOption(requestJson = authApi.signInOptions()),   // challenge, rpId
            GetPasswordOption(),                           // password users still see their account
        ))
        return try {
            when (val credential = credentials.getCredential(activity, request).credential) {
                is PublicKeyCredential -> authApi.verifyAssertion(credential.authenticationResponseJson)
                is PasswordCredential -> authApi.passwordSignIn(credential.id, credential.password)
                else -> null
            }
        } catch (e: NoCredentialException) {
            null                                           // offer registration instead
        } catch (e: GetCredentialException) {
            Log.w("Passkeys", "sign-in failed: ${e.type} ${e.errorMessage}")
            null
        }
    }
}
Result

register shows the system sheet and creates a passkey in the user's provider (Google Password Manager by default); signIn returns a session after the server verifies the signed assertion, and configuration errors are logged by type instead of looking like a refusal.

Setup
  1. androidx.credentials:credentials and credentials-play-services-auth 1.6.0, and Digital Asset Links linking your app to the relying-party domain (/.well-known/assetlinks.json)
  2. authApi is your backend: it creates the WebAuthn options (with a fresh challenge) and verifies the responses

Excerpt, not compiled or run here: it needs an Android app (API 28+) with Credential Manager, Google Play services and Digital Asset Links set up.

  • androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth
  • kotlin >=2.4
  • credentials 1.5.0 – 1.6.0
  • android API 28+
  • an Android app (API 28+ for passkeys) with Credential Manager

Network security config and certificate pinning

Block cleartext app-wide, trust user CAs only in debug, and pin only if you can ship a backup pin and an expiry — a wrong pin bricks the app.

// res/xml/network_security_config.xml
// <network-security-config>
//   <base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false" />
//   <domain-config>
//     <domain includeSubdomains="true">api.example.com</domain>
//     <pin-set expiration="2027-06-30">                  <!-- after this date, pinning is off, not broken -->
//       <pin digest="SHA-256">7HIpactkIAq2Y49orFOOQKurWxmmSFZhBCoQYcRhJ3Y=</pin>
//       <pin digest="SHA-256">fwza0LRMXouZHRC8Ei+4PyuldPDcf3UKgO/04cDM1oE=</pin>   <!-- backup key -->
//     </pin-set>
//   </domain-config>
//   <debug-overrides><trust-anchors><certificates src="user" /></trust-anchors></debug-overrides>
// </network-security-config>

// The same pins in OkHttp, when the config file is not enough (e.g. pins fetched per tenant):
val pinnedClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .certificatePinner(
        CertificatePinner.Builder()
            .add("api.example.com", "sha256/7HIpactkIAq2Y49orFOOQKurWxmmSFZhBCoQYcRhJ3Y=")
            .add("api.example.com", "sha256/fwza0LRMXouZHRC8Ei+4PyuldPDcf3UKgO/04cDM1oE=")
            .build(),
    )
    .build()
// A mismatch fails the call with SSLPeerUnverifiedException — report it, never "retry without pinning".
Result

Plain http:// requests fail with UnknownServiceException; a TLS connection to api.example.com whose chain does not contain a pinned key fails with SSLPeerUnverifiedException.

Setup
  1. res/xml/network_security_config.xml (shown in the comment) referenced from <application android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config">
  2. Pins are base64 SHA-256 hashes of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo of your leaf or intermediate key and a backup key

WebView and deep-link input are untrusted

A deep link or an extra is input from any app on the device: parse it against an allow-list, and keep the WebView on your own origin.

private val ORDER_ID = Regex("^A-\\d{4,10}$")
private const val ASSETS_HOST = "appassets.androidplatform.net"     // WebViewAssetLoader's default origin

/** Deep link: https://shop.example.com/orders/A-1041 — validate the shape, never forward raw input. */
fun handleDeepLink(intent: Intent, openOrder: (String) -> Unit) {
    val uri = intent.data ?: return
    if (uri.scheme != "https" || uri.host != "shop.example.com") return
    val id = uri.pathSegments.takeIf { it.size == 2 && it[0] == "orders" }?.get(1) ?: return
    if (ORDER_ID.matches(id)) openOrder(id)               // a typed id, not a URL or a file path
}

class HelpActivity : AppCompatActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        val assets = WebViewAssetLoader.Builder()         // serves the bundled pages over https
            .addPathHandler("/assets/", WebViewAssetLoader.AssetsPathHandler(this)).build()
        val web = WebView(this).apply {
            settings.javaScriptEnabled = true             // only because our own help pages need it
            settings.allowFileAccess = false
            settings.allowContentAccess = false
            webViewClient = object : WebViewClientCompat() {
                override fun shouldInterceptRequest(view: WebView, request: WebResourceRequest) =
                    assets.shouldInterceptRequest(request.url)
                override fun shouldOverrideUrlLoading(view: WebView, request: WebResourceRequest): Boolean {
                    val url = request.url
                    if (url.scheme == "https" && url.host == ASSETS_HOST) return false
                    if (url.scheme == "https") runCatching { startActivity(Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, url)) }
                    return true                           // intent:, tel:, custom schemes: dropped
                }
            }
        }
        setContentView(web)
        web.loadUrl("https://$ASSETS_HOST/assets/help/index.html")
    }
}
Result

A link to A-1041 opens that order; ../../files, javascript: or foreign hosts are ignored, the help WebView never navigates off the bundled pages, and only https links leave for the browser.

Setup
  1. An Android project with androidx.webkit:webkit 1.15.0; an <intent-filter android:autoVerify="true"> for https://shop.example.com/orders/* (App Links)
  2. openOrder(id) navigates inside the app; HelpActivity hosts the WebView

Excerpt, not compiled or run here: it needs an Android app with androidx.webkit (needs the Android SDK).

Security and privacy rules

The things reviewers and the Play Console will ask about.

  • Disabling certificate or hostname checks — a trust-all X509TrustManager, a HostnameVerifier that returns true, handler.proceed() in onReceivedSslError. Test against a debug CA in debug-overrides instead; Google Play rejects apps that ship these.
  • Exposing native code to web content with addJavascriptInterface on a page you do not control — use WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener with an origin allow-list.
  • Logging tokens, passwords, full card numbers, email addresses or request bodies with Log.d — Logcat is readable over adb and ends up in bug reports. Log ids and outcomes; strip debug logs in release with R8 rules or a no-op logger.
  • Treating R8 obfuscation as a security control — it renames classes, it does not hide strings, keys or endpoints. Anything shipped in the APK is readable.
  • Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token and expect rotation: store the new refresh token at once, and treat invalid_grant — which a replayed old token also gets — as signed out (see the networking sheet's Ktor and single-flight cards).
  • Signing in through an embedded WebView — the app can read the password. Use a Custom Tab (AppAuth does this) or Credential Manager; the redirect returns via an App Link or a private scheme.
  • Building SQL with string templates — use Room's @Query parameters or ? bind arguments; SQL injection works on-device too.
  • Exporting components by accident: set android:exported="false" unless another app must start it, and create PendingIntents with FLAG_IMMUTABLE.
  • Ask for runtime permissions in context, at the moment of use, and handle denial; prefer permission-less APIs (the photo picker instead of READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, coarse instead of fine location).
  • Consent: no analytics, ads or crash-report personal data before the user agrees where the law requires it, and withdrawing consent stops collection at once.
  • Data minimisation: collect only what a feature needs, keep it only as long as needed, exclude it from backups, and declare it truthfully in the Play Data safety form.
  • A fresh random nonce for every AES-GCM encryption; random values from SecureRandom, never kotlin.random.Random; compare MACs with MessageDigest.isEqual.
  • Hash passwords only on the server, with a slow KDF (Argon2id, scrypt, or PBKDF2 with a high iteration count) — a client-side hash just becomes the password.

Accessibility on Android

What TalkBack reads and how to shape it — content descriptions, Compose semantics and their Views equivalents, 48dp targets, focus order, live regions, text that survives 200%, contrast, reduced motion, and how to test it all.

  • kotlin >=2.0
  • compose-bom >=2025.04.00
  • core-ktx >=1.13
  • android API 23+ (checks in Compose tests: API 34+)

What TalkBack reads — Compose and Views

Every node is read as label, role, state, then the action hint; each row is one of those, in both toolkits.

NeedComposeViews

skip a decorative graphiccontentDescription = null; semantics { hideFromAccessibility() }android:importantForAccessibility="no"
label an input with visible textTextField(label = { Text(…) })android:labelFor="@id/email" on the TextView

Content descriptions — and when to pass null

Describe what a graphic means or does in a localized string, pass `null` when the text beside it already says it, and never say "button" or "icon" because TalkBack adds the role.

@Composable
fun OrderRow(order: Order, onReorder: () -> Unit) {
    Row(verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
        Image(
            painter = painterResource(order.thumbnailRes),
            contentDescription = null,                 // decorative: the product name is read next
            modifier = Modifier.size(48.dp),
        )
        Column(Modifier.weight(1f).padding(horizontal = 12.dp)) {
            Text(order.productName)
            Row(verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
                // This icon carries information colour alone cannot: describe it.
                Icon(
                    imageVector = if (order.delayed) Icons.Filled.Warning else Icons.Filled.CheckCircle,
                    contentDescription = stringResource(
                        if (order.delayed) R.string.status_delayed else R.string.status_on_time,
                    ),
                )
                Text(order.etaLabel)
            }
        }
        IconButton(onClick = onReorder) {
            // "Reorder Running shoes", not "Refresh icon": say the action and its object.
            Icon(
                Icons.Filled.Refresh,
                contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.reorder_product, order.productName),
            )
        }
    }
}
Result

TalkBack reads "Running shoes", "Delayed", "Arrives Tuesday", then "Reorder Running shoes, button, double-tap to activate"; the thumbnail is skipped.

Semantics: merge, clear, heading, state and custom actions

One focus stop per order, read as one sentence; nested buttons and swipe gestures move into the actions menu so TalkBack and Switch Access users reach them too.

@Composable
fun RecentOrders(orders: List<Order>, actions: OrderActions) {
    LazyColumn {
        item {
            Text(
                stringResource(R.string.recent_orders),
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge,
                modifier = Modifier.semantics { heading() },     // TalkBack can jump from heading to heading
            )
        }
        items(orders, key = { it.id }) { order ->
            val archiveLabel = stringResource(R.string.archive_order)
            Row(
                Modifier
                    // clickable merges the row's children into one focus stop
                    .clickable(onClickLabel = stringResource(R.string.open_order)) { actions.open(order) }
                    .semantics {
                        stateDescription = order.statusLabel           // "Shipped", read as the row's state
                        customActions = listOf(
                            CustomAccessibilityAction(archiveLabel) { actions.archive(order); true },
                        )
                    }
                    .padding(16.dp),
            ) {
                Column(Modifier.weight(1f)) {
                    Text(order.title)
                    Text(order.dateLabel, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall)
                }
                // Still there for touch; for assistive tech it is the custom action above.
                IconButton(
                    onClick = { actions.archive(order) },
                    modifier = Modifier.clearAndSetSemantics { },
                ) {
                    Icon(Icons.Filled.Delete, contentDescription = null)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
Result

Each row is one stop: "Running shoes, 16 Nov, Shipped, double-tap to open order, actions available"; the TalkBack menu (swipe down then right) offers "Archive order".

A custom component made accessible — with 48dp targets

Five drawn stars become one adjustable, slider-like node for TalkBack and Switch Access; each star still keeps a 48dp touch target.

@Composable
fun StarRating(rating: Int, onRatingChange: (Int) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    val label = stringResource(R.string.rate_product)
    val state = pluralStringResource(R.plurals.star_count, rating, rating)    // "3 stars"
    Row(
        modifier.clearAndSetSemantics {                    // the five icons become one node
            contentDescription = label
            stateDescription = state
            progressBarRangeInfo = ProgressBarRangeInfo(rating.toFloat(), 1f..5f, steps = 3)
            setProgress { target ->
                onRatingChange(target.roundToInt().coerceIn(1, 5))
                true
            }
        },
    ) {
        for (star in 1..5) {
            Icon(
                imageVector = if (star <= rating) Icons.Filled.Star else Icons.Outlined.Star,
                contentDescription = null,
                modifier = Modifier
                    .clickable { onRatingChange(star) }
                    .minimumInteractiveComponentSize()     // reserves 48dp; put it before any size
                    .size(24.dp),
            )
        }
    }
}
// Views: the same contract through ViewCompat.setAccessibilityDelegate — set a RangeInfo,
// a state description, and handle ACTION_SET_PROGRESS in performAccessibilityAction.
Result

TalkBack reads "Rate this product, 3 stars" once instead of five unlabelled images, and its adjust gestures call setProgress to move to 4 or 2 stars; a tap anywhere in a star's 48dp box selects it.

Focus order, traversal groups and keyboard operation

Group columns with `isTraversalGroup` so TalkBack does not read across them; move keyboard and switch focus to where the user must act next.

@Composable
fun CheckoutForm(
    state: CheckoutState,
    onEmail: (String) -> Unit,
    onCard: (String) -> Unit,
    onPay: () -> Unit,
) {
    val focusManager = LocalFocusManager.current
    val cardFocus = remember { FocusRequester() }
    LaunchedEffect(state.cardError) {
        if (state.cardError != null) cardFocus.requestFocus()      // land on the problem, not the top
    }
    Column(Modifier.verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())) {
        // Two columns of label/value: without groups TalkBack reads "Subtotal, Shipping, €120, €9.90".
        Row {
            val column = Modifier.semantics { isTraversalGroup = true }
            SummaryColumn(stringResource(R.string.subtotal), state.subtotal, Modifier.weight(1f).then(column))
            SummaryColumn(stringResource(R.string.shipping), state.shipping, Modifier.weight(1f).then(column))
        }
        OutlinedTextField(
            value = state.email, onValueChange = onEmail,
            label = { Text(stringResource(R.string.email)) },
            keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Email, imeAction = ImeAction.Next),
            keyboardActions = KeyboardActions(onNext = { focusManager.moveFocus(FocusDirection.Down) }),
        )
        OutlinedTextField(
            value = state.card, onValueChange = onCard,
            label = { Text(stringResource(R.string.card_number)) },
            isError = state.cardError != null,
            supportingText = { state.cardError?.let { Text(it) } },   // read with the field
            modifier = Modifier.focusRequester(cardFocus),
        )
        Button(onClick = onPay, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) { Text(stringResource(R.string.pay)) }
    }
}
Result

TalkBack reads "Subtotal, €120" then "Shipping, €9.90"; Tab or the IME's Next moves from email to card; a rejected card moves keyboard focus straight to that field with its error.

Announcements and live regions

Announce state changes through semantics — a live region, a pane title, a Snackbar — not with `announceForAccessibility`, which is deprecated from API 36.

@Composable
fun OrderSearch(state: OrderSearchState, onQueryChange: (String) -> Unit) {
    Column {
        OutlinedTextField(
            value = state.query,
            onValueChange = onQueryChange,
            label = { Text(stringResource(R.string.search_orders)) },
        )
        // Read politely each time it changes, without moving focus out of the field.
        // The count changes once per (debounced) search, not on every keystroke.
        Text(
            pluralStringResource(R.plurals.results_count, state.results.size, state.results.size),
            modifier = Modifier.semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite },
        )
        LazyColumn { items(state.results, key = { it.id }) { OrderRow(it, onReorder = {}) } }
    }
}

@Composable
fun FilterSheet(content: @Composable () -> Unit) {
    val title = stringResource(R.string.filter_orders)
    // A custom sheet: paneTitle makes TalkBack announce it like a window opening.
    Surface(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().semantics { paneTitle = title }) { content() }
}

// Transient confirmation: Material's Snackbar is already announced.
suspend fun confirmArchived(snackbar: SnackbarHostState, message: String) {
    snackbar.showSnackbar(message, duration = SnackbarDuration.Short)
}
// Views: android:accessibilityLiveRegion="polite" and ViewCompat.setAccessibilityPaneTitle(view, title).
Result

Typing "shoe" leaves focus in the field while TalkBack says "3 results"; opening the sheet announces "Filter orders"; archiving announces the Snackbar text.

Text that survives 200%

Size text in `sp`, give rows a minimum rather than a fixed height, let them wrap and let the screen scroll, then look at the 200% preview.

// Text in sp follows the user's font size: up to 200% on Android 14+, scaled non-linearly.
@Composable
fun TotalRow(label: String, amount: String) {
    FlowRow(                                                // wraps instead of clipping at large sizes
        Modifier.fillMaxWidth().heightIn(min = 48.dp),     // a minimum, never a fixed height
        horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
    ) {
        Text(label, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge)
        Text(amount, style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
    }
}

@Composable
fun OrderSummary(order: Order) {
    Column(Modifier.verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())) {   // at 200% the content outgrows the screen
        TotalRow(stringResource(R.string.subtotal), order.subtotalLabel)
        TotalRow(stringResource(R.string.shipping_and_handling), order.shippingLabel)
        TotalRow(stringResource(R.string.total), order.totalLabel)
    }
}

@Preview(name = "100%")
@Preview(name = "200%", fontScale = 2f)
@Composable
private fun TotalRowPreview() = TotalRow("Shipping and handling", "€9.90")
Result

The 200% preview wraps each amount under its label and the summary scrolls; nothing is clipped or overlapped.

Reduced motion and a pause control for moving content

Compose and Animator animations already jump to their end when the user removes animations, but motion you start yourself — an auto-advancing carousel — must check the scale, stop under TalkBack and offer Pause.

import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityManager
import androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.rememberSaveable
import androidx.compose.ui.MotionDurationScale

@Composable
fun PromoCarousel(promos: List<Promo>) {
    val pagerState = rememberPagerState { promos.size }
    var playing by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(true) }
    val accessibility = LocalContext.current.getSystemService(AccessibilityManager::class.java)

    LaunchedEffect(pagerState, playing, promos.size) {
        if (!playing || promos.size < 2) return@LaunchedEffect
        while (true) {
            delay(5_000)
            // Checked on every tick, so turning either setting on mid-run stops the carousel.
            // Compose hands the system animator duration scale to every animation; 0 = "Remove animations".
            val reduceMotion = (coroutineContext[MotionDurationScale]?.scaleFactor ?: 1f) == 0f
            if (reduceMotion || accessibility.isTouchExplorationEnabled) continue
            pagerState.animateScrollToPage((pagerState.currentPage + 1) % promos.size)
        }
    }

    Column {
        HorizontalPager(state = pagerState) { page -> PromoCard(promos[page]) }
        // WCAG 2.2.2: content that moves on its own for more than 5 s needs a way to pause it.
        TextButton(onClick = { playing = !playing }) {
            Text(stringResource(if (playing) R.string.pause_promos else R.string.play_promos))
        }
    }
}
Result

With Remove animations or TalkBack on the carousel never advances on its own; otherwise it moves every 5 s until the user taps Pause, and an empty or single-item list never schedules a page change.

Check contrast in code

Run the WCAG ratio over your theme's colour pairs in a unit test, so a palette change that drops below 4.5:1 fails the build.

import java.util.Locale
import kotlin.math.pow

// WCAG 2.x relative luminance of an sRGB color written as 0xRRGGBB.
fun luminance(rgb: Int): Double {
    fun linear(shift: Int): Double {
        val c = ((rgb shr shift) and 0xFF) / 255.0
        return if (c <= 0.04045) c / 12.92 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055).pow(2.4)
    }
    return 0.2126 * linear(16) + 0.7152 * linear(8) + 0.0722 * linear(0)
}

fun contrastRatio(foreground: Int, background: Int): Double {
    val (lighter, darker) = listOf(luminance(foreground), luminance(background)).sortedDescending()
    return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05)
}

// WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for body text; 3:1 for large text (18sp, or 14sp bold) and for icons and borders.
enum class Use(val minimum: Double) { BODY_TEXT(4.5), LARGE_TEXT(3.0), ICON(3.0) }
data class ColorPair(val name: String, val foreground: Int, val background: Int, val use: Use)

fun main() {
    val theme = listOf(
        ColorPair("body on surface", 0x1D1B20, 0xFEF7FF, Use.BODY_TEXT),
        ColorPair("error on surface", 0xB3261E, 0xFEF7FF, Use.BODY_TEXT),
        ColorPair("hint on white", 0x9E9E9E, 0xFFFFFF, Use.BODY_TEXT),
        ColorPair("hint on white, 18sp", 0x9E9E9E, 0xFFFFFF, Use.LARGE_TEXT),
        ColorPair("outline icon on white", 0x79747E, 0xFFFFFF, Use.ICON),
    )
    for (pair in theme) {
        val ratio = contrastRatio(pair.foreground, pair.background)
        val verdict = if (ratio >= pair.use.minimum) "pass" else "FAIL"
        val line = "%-22s %5.2f:1  %s (needs %.1f)"
        println(line.format(Locale.ROOT, pair.name, ratio, verdict, pair.use.minimum))
    }
}
Result
body on surface        16.23:1  pass (needs 4.5)
error on surface        6.21:1  pass (needs 4.5)
hint on white           2.68:1  FAIL (needs 4.5)
hint on white, 18sp     2.68:1  FAIL (needs 3.0)
outline icon on white   4.55:1  pass (needs 3.0)
Setup
  1. A Kotlin 2.x compiler (kotlinc) and JDK 17 or later
  2. Save as main.kt; run kotlinc main.kt -include-runtime -d main.jar && java -jar main.jar (in a project, the same loop asserts in a JVM unit test)

Accessibility checks in Compose and Espresso tests

The Accessibility Test Framework — the engine behind Accessibility Scanner — runs on every test action once enabled; assert your own semantics beside it.

import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.accessibility.enableAccessibilityChecks
import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.v2.createAndroidComposeRule
import androidx.compose.ui.test.tryPerformAccessibilityChecks
import androidx.test.filters.SdkSuppress

@SdkSuppress(minSdkVersion = 34)                    // the checks need API 34+; older devices skip the class
class RecentOrdersAccessibilityTest {
    @get:Rule val composeRule = createAndroidComposeRule<ComponentActivity>()

    @Before
    fun enableChecks() {
        // One validator for Compose and Espresso, so a hybrid screen is checked by the same rules.
        val validator = AccessibilityChecks.enable().setRunChecksFromRootView(true)
        composeRule.enableAccessibilityChecks(validator)          // labels, contrast, 48dp targets, order
    }

    @Test
    fun orderRowsCarryStateAndActions() {
        composeRule.setContent { AppTheme { RecentOrders(sampleOrders, FakeOrderActions()) } }

        composeRule.onNode(hasText("Running shoes") and hasClickAction())
            .assert(SemanticsMatcher.expectValue(SemanticsProperties.StateDescription, "Shipped"))
            .assert(SemanticsMatcher.keyIsDefined(SemanticsActions.CustomActions))
            .performClick()                                         // each action also runs the checks

        composeRule.onRoot().tryPerformAccessibilityChecks()        // or check the whole screen explicitly
    }
}

// A Views-only screen: AccessibilityChecks.enable() once in the class; every ViewAction then checks.
Result

On an API 34+ device a row without a label, an icon button under 48dp or grey-on-white text fails the test with the Accessibility Test Framework's finding; below API 34 the class is skipped, not failed.

  2. androidTestImplementation("androidx.test.espresso:espresso-accessibility") for the shared validator and androidx.test:runner for @SdkSuppress
  3. Run with ./gradlew connectedDebugAndroidTest

Test it by hand, and the pitfalls

Automated checks catch labels, contrast and sizes; only a screen reader session catches a confusing journey.

  • TalkBack: swipe right / left for next / previous, double-tap to activate, two-finger swipe to scroll, swipe down then right (or a three-finger tap) for the TalkBack menu and its actions, swipe down then left for back.
  • Run Accessibility Scanner on every new screen, and Compose UI Check in the preview pane; try Switch Access and Voice Access for the main journey.
  • Test at 200% font and Display size: largest, with Remove animations on, in dark theme — in previews (fontScale = 2f) and on a device.
  • Modifier.clickable on a Box with an icon and no label: TalkBack says "unlabelled, button". Give it a contentDescription or text.
  • Colour as the only signal (a red border for an error): add text, an icon with a description, or semantics { error(…) }.
  • clearAndSetSemantics { } everywhere to silence noise: it also hides the content from tests and autofill. Prefer mergeDescendants or hideFromAccessibility().
  • Fixed height(48.dp) around text or maxLines = 1 on a label: clipped at 200%. Use heightIn(min = …) and let text wrap.
  • Swipe, drag and long-press gestures need a custom action or a visible alternative — TalkBack users cannot perform them directly.

strings.xml, qualifiers and positional arguments

The default `values/` must be complete while other folders override it key by key, and positional `%1$s` arguments let a translator reorder the sentence.

// res/values/strings.xml — the fallback for every locale
// <string name="order_title">Order %1$s</string>
// <string name="order_ships">%1$s, your order ships on %2$s.</string>
//
// res/values-es/strings.xml — Spanish reorders the arguments
// <string name="order_ships">El %2$s sale tu pedido, %1$s.</string>
//
// res/values-b+sr+Latn/strings.xml — BCP 47 folder: Serbian in Latin script
// res/values-pt-rBR/strings.xml    — legacy form: Portuguese (Brazil)
// <string name="brand" translatable="false">Acme</string>  (lint skips it in values-*)

@Composable
fun OrderHeader(order: Order) {
    val locale = LocalConfiguration.current.locales[0]
    val shipDate = remember(order.shipsOn, locale) {
        DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDate(FormatStyle.LONG).withLocale(locale).format(order.shipsOn)
    }
    Column {
        Text(stringResource(R.string.order_title, order.code), style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge)
        Text(stringResource(R.string.order_ships, order.customerName, shipDate))
    }
}

// Outside composition (a notification, a worker) the same lookup goes through a Context:
fun shippingNotificationText(context: Context, order: Order, shipDate: String): String =
    context.getString(R.string.order_ships, order.customerName, shipDate)
Result

English shows "Ana, your order ships on November 16, 2026."; with the device in Spanish the same call shows "El 16 de noviembre de 2026 sale tu pedido, Ana."

Setup
  1. An Android Studio project with the Compose template (Kotlin 2.x and the Compose BOM)
  2. Put the XML in the named res/ folders, call the composable from setContent { }, and switch the device language (or the app language) to see each translation

Plurals: quantity strings, and why "one" is not 1

Ship `one` and `other` in English and let each language add the CLDR categories it needs — Russian `one` matches 1, 21 and 101, so never test `count == 1` yourself.

// res/values/strings.xml
// <plurals name="cart_items">
//     <item quantity="one">%d item in your cart</item>     <!-- keep %d: in other languages "one" ≠ 1 -->
//     <item quantity="other">%d items in your cart</item>
// </plurals>
//
// res/values-ru/strings.xml
//   one: 1, 21, 101…   few: 2–4, 22–24…   many: 0, 5–20, 25…   other: fractions such as 1.5
// <plurals name="cart_items">
//     <item quantity="one">%d товар в корзине</item>
//     <item quantity="few">%d товара в корзине</item>
//     <item quantity="many">%d товаров в корзине</item>
//     <item quantity="other">%d товара в корзине</item>
// </plurals>

@Composable
fun CartBadge(count: Int) {
    // The first count picks the category, the second fills %d.
    Text(pluralStringResource(R.plurals.cart_items, count, count))
}

// Views, notifications, workers:
fun cartSummary(resources: Resources, count: Int): String =
    resources.getQuantityString(R.plurals.cart_items, count, count)

// The rule itself, when you need it (API 24+): android.icu.text.PluralRules
fun pluralCategory(locale: Locale, count: Int): String =
    PluralRules.forLocale(locale).select(count.toDouble())   // ru: 21 → "one", 22 → "few", 25 → "many"
Result

In English 1 shows "1 item in your cart" and 21 "21 items…"; in Russian 21 picks one ("21 товар…"), 22 few and 25 many.

Grammatical gender: -feminine resources and GrammaticalInflectionManager

On Android 14+ the app stores how the user wants to be addressed and the resource system picks `values-fr-feminine/` or `-masculine/`, falling back to the neutral `values-fr/` text everywhere else.

import android.app.GrammaticalInflectionManager
import android.content.res.Configuration
import android.os.Build

// res/values-fr/strings.xml — the neutral default, shown when no gender is set
// <string name="subscribed">Abonnement à %1$s confirmé</string>
//
// res/values-fr-feminine/strings.xml (and -masculine, -neuter)
// <string name="subscribed">Vous êtes abonnée à %1$s</string>
//
// res/values-fr-masculine/strings.xml
// <string name="subscribed">Vous êtes abonné à %1$s</string>

// How the user asked to be addressed, mapped to the platform's four values.
enum class AddressAs(val platformValue: Int) {
    FEMININE(Configuration.GRAMMATICAL_GENDER_FEMININE),
    MASCULINE(Configuration.GRAMMATICAL_GENDER_MASCULINE),
    NEUTRAL(Configuration.GRAMMATICAL_GENDER_NEUTRAL),
    NOT_SPECIFIED(Configuration.GRAMMATICAL_GENDER_NOT_SPECIFIED),   // "don't say": back to values-fr/
}

// Called from the profile screen once the user has chosen, or cleared, how to be addressed.
fun saveGrammaticalGender(context: Context, choice: AddressAs) {
    if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.UPSIDE_DOWN_CAKE) return     // API 34+
    // Recreates the activity, unless it declares android:configChanges="grammaticalGender".
    context.getSystemService(GrammaticalInflectionManager::class.java)
        .setRequestedApplicationGrammaticalGender(choice.platformValue)
}

@Composable
fun SubscriptionConfirmed(newsletter: String) {
    // Resolves values-fr-feminine/ or -masculine/ when a gender is set, else the neutral values-fr/.
    Text(stringResource(R.string.subscribed, newsletter))
}
Result

On Android 14+ in French, a user who chose the feminine form sees "Vous êtes abonnée à Nouveautés"; below API 34, or with no choice made, the neutral "Abonnement à Nouveautés confirmé" appears.

Setup
  1. An Android project with compileSdk 34 or later and Compose; the qualifiers need Android Studio Giraffe or later
  2. Put each string in the named res/ folders, ask the user in a profile screen, then call saveGrammaticalGender
